title: Labor Leaders Press Trump Administration on Union-Busting Consultants’ and Corporations’ Compliance with Federal Law

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON – Today, House labor leaders demanded information from Office of Labor-Management Standards (OLMS) Director Elisabeth Messenger on whether corporations and their union-busting consultants comply with federal transparency requirements.

The letter was sent by House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), Subcommittee on Health, Employment, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Ranking Member Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), and Education and Workforce Member Rep. Summer L. Lee (PA-12).

Too often, when workers exercise their right to organize a union, corporations and bosses hire outside consultants to wage anti-union campaigns. Over the last several decades, union-avoidance has become a multi-billion-dollar industry. The latest analysis found that companies spend approximately $1.7 billion every year, including nearly $500 million on union-busting consultants, to break their organizing drives. Some consultants are reportedly paid $500 per hour or $4,000 per day for their services.

Under the Labor-Management Reporting and Disclosure Act (LMRDA), employers and consultants are required to file public reports about their matter because it allows workers to see how much their bosses are spending to influence their decision to unionize. However, for decades, employers and union-busting consultants have routinely failed to meet this requirement, allowing bosses and their consultants to operate in the shadows. Under the Trump Administration, the problem is only becoming worse. A recent watchdog report found that, as of August 8, 2026, nearly 60 percent of employers required to file a disclosure in 2025 have still not submitted their reports—the largest year-over-year decline on record.

“Over the last several years, while worker organizing has skyrocketed, employers have increasingly responded with hostile anti-union campaigns, including by hiring well-compensated outside consultants. As more employers seek to quash their workers’ unionization drives, it is imperative that employer and consultant disclosure requirements under the LMRDA are robustly enforced by OLMS, so workers have a complete picture of who is attempting to influence their decision as they exercise their right to organize,” wrote the Members.

To determine whether OLMS is effectively carrying out its responsibility to enforce the LMRDA, the Members requested a response to their extensive questions by no later than November 16, 2026.

To read the full letter to OLMS Director Elisabeth Messenger, click here.

title: Ranking Member Scott Slams ED for Playing Games with Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) demanded answers from Department of Education (ED) Secretary Linda McMahon, following concerning reports from borrowers in the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program that several qualifying payments were erased from their accounts.

Established in 2007, PSLF offers loan forgiveness to public servants who work for a qualified employer for 10 years and make 120 payments toward their federal student loans. However, borrowers have recently reported that the number of PSLF-qualifying payments, tracked on a counter on the Office for Federal Student Aid’s (FSA’s) website, appeared incorrect. Despite acknowledging the data error, ED failed to provide detailed information on the cause of the error.

“Without additional information from the Department, borrowers cannot know whether changes to the PSLF qualifying payment count were the result of an error that will be fixed; if it is a decision that can be appealed; or if the statement reflects an unappealable decision made by this Administration. Without any additional information, borrowers are left in the dark as to why they must remain in repayment longer than the law requires. This is particularly concerning if a borrower believes they have met all the statutory and regulatory requirements to have their debt forgiven through the PSLF,” wrote Ranking Member Scott.

In his letter, Ranking Member Scott also emphasized that the qualifying payment-count errors come as the Department has not addressed the 88,000-application backlog in the PSLF buyback program and has eliminated affordable repayment plans, creating financial uncertainty and distress for student loan borrowers.

On Friday, October 30, 2026, the American Federation of Teachers (AFT), with support from Protect Borrowers, sued the Trump Administration, alleging it unlawfully blocked student loan forgiveness for tens of thousands of borrowers who qualify. The lawsuit, Weingarten v. McMahon, alleges ED Secretary McMahon mismanaged PSLF by incorrectly counting borrowers’ payment timelines and not awarding people credit for time served.

title: Neal Statement on Trump’s Termination of South Africa from AGOA

committee.name: House Committee on Ways and Means

text:
SPRINGFIELD, MA— Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) released the following statement after President Trump announced intention to terminate South Africa from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) trade preference program:

“For 26 years, AGOA has been the cornerstone of a profound economic partnership between the U.S. and sub-Saharan African countries. Together, we’ve expanded trade, promoted job creation and worker rights, and strengthened democratic institutions. For the Trump Administration to abandon South Africa and strip them of that progress and opportunity over a debunked fixation on anti-apartheid efforts is unconscionable. It’s yet another trade decision grounded in grievance that flies in the face of what responsible policy should be.

“The Administration owes the American people a more thorough explanation as to why South Africa was removed from AGOA and what steps South Africa can take to be reinstated to the program. Livelihoods, businesses, and U.S. credibility are on the line. The power of our trade laws shouldn’t be twisted so Trump can further policies based on biased accusations made by those in his orbit looking to settle scores. The last thing our trade policy needs, and families and businesses at home can afford, is more Trump chaos that shakes our economy, puts investment at risk, and erodes America’s standing on the continent.”

title: Walberg Requests GAO Review of Graduate School Tuition Costs

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
Today, Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-MI) sent a letter to Government Accountability Office (GAO) Acting Comptroller General Orice Williams Brown requesting a review of how public universities determine tuition and fees for graduate programs.

The request comes as graduate student loans make up approximately half of the $1.7 trillion federal student loan portfolio. Meanwhile, tuition and fees vary widely across graduate programs, even within the same university, raising questions about how schools determine what students pay.

In the letter, Walberg writes: “Tuition and fees vary widely by graduate program, even within the same institution. For example, at one California public university, annual tuition and fees for the 2026–2027 academic year range from approximately $23,000 for certain non-professional graduate programs to $94,000 for a Master of Business Administration.”

The letter continues: “Given the varying costs to students by college and by program, the [Committee] seeks to better understand how institutions of higher education set their graduate program costs, particularly among public universities that receive both federal and state taxpayer funds.”

The letter concludes by requesting that GAO examine what factors public universities consider when setting graduate tuition, including operating costs, student demand, graduates' expected earnings, and access to federal student aid. The review will also examine differences between in-state and out-of-state tuition and whether graduate program revenue helps fund other university operations.

Read the full letter here.

title: Sanctuary City Boston Helping Foreign Criminals Flout Federal Immigration Law: Report
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the House Judiciary Committee and its Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement released an interim staff report titled, "Boston: The Dangerous Consequences of Sanctuary Policies." The report exposes how Boston's radical sanctuary city policies routinely prevent local local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, even in cases with illegal aliens who are repeat offenders and have violent histories.

The Boston Police Department (BPD) is "prohibited from asking people about their immigration status, sharing information with ICE, making arrests or holding someone based on ICE administrative warrants if there is no other criminal charge, transferring anyone to ICE custody[,] or otherwise 'performing the functions of an immigration officer.'" The Trust Act also prohibits BPD from notifying ICE about an alien’s release from BPD custody.

Because of its sanctuary policies, the city has attracted and harbored dangerous criminal aliens from around the world. Data and information provided to the Committee and Subcommittee show that in the first 10 months of 2026, Boston law enforcement encountered illegal aliens from Colombia, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, Brazil, Mexico, Ecuador, China, Morocco, and Venezuela. The aliens for whom ICE placed detainers included numerous foreign nationals with final removal orders and previous criminal history, including criminal convictions.

Despite Boston's attempts to keep the extent of its pro-criminal alien policies shrouded in secrecy, data provided to the Committee and Subcommittee reveal that in 2026 alone, the BPD has received 54 detainers and has not honored one. Since 2021, BPD has not transferred a single foreign national criminal to ICE custody based off an ICE detainer.

As Boston residents feel unsafe in their own city, state and local sanctuary laws force law enforcement officers to release dangerous criminals back onto Boston streets where they are free to reoffend. Even worse, the Boston City Council has voted to keep the full detainer-related information, including the criminal histories of the aliens for whom the detainers were placed, hidden from the public. While sanctuary cities continue to shield criminal aliens from accountability for their crimes, the Committee will continue its oversight into sanctuary jurisdictions that prioritize the comfort of illegal alien criminals over the safety of U.S. citizens.

title: Warren, Van Hollen Call on SEC to Abandon Counterproductive Deregulatory IPO Agenda Putting Families and Investors at Risk

committee.name: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

text:
“Taken together, your ‘making IPOs great again’ agenda is part and parcel of the Trump Administration’s approach to our financial markets: make it easier for the President’s billionaire donors and corporate executives to avoid accountability or transparency, while leaving regular investors in the dark.”

Text of Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, and Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), member of the Committee, wrote to Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chair Paul Atkins with concerns that a recent slate of deregulatory proposals purportedly aimed at “making IPOs great again” would reduce transparency, damage investor confidence, and undermine the integrity of America’s capital markets.

In May, Chair Atkins announced an effort to “Make IPOs Great Again” and encourage more companies to “go and stay public.” While the policy initiative aims to reverse the decline in publicly-listed U.S. companies over the past three decades by reducing public-market disclosures and requirements, research shows that deregulation in the private markets is a key reason why fewer companies have gone public. The Senators note that the SEC’s proposals would be counterproductive and risk exacerbating the decline in public companies.

“While we share the goal of revitalizing the public markets and providing more companies with the opportunity to go public, the ill-conceived deregulatory measures you have taken will not revive or sustain a healthy IPO market,” wrote the Senators. “These proposals would ultimately erode the very framework of transparency and investor protections that makes our public markets so appealing to investors the world over.”

“Your proposals posit that the compliance burden of the robust regulations and disclosures required in the public markets is the sole reason that companies choose to stay private,” the Senators continued. “Academic research has repeatedly discredited your theory and found that more – not less – disclosure from public companies can make markets more liquid, is rewarded by investors with greater returns, and associated with larger stock markets. Moreover, research has shown that deregulation in the private markets is a key reason for why companies do not go public.”

“Our capital markets thrive when more companies go public and go public earlier. Transparency and robust disclosure in our public markets facilitates a more trustworthy and efficient market where Main Street investors are more willing to provide capital because they have faith in the integrity of public markets,” wrote the Senators. “Our goal should be bringing as much capital raising as possible into our public markets to provide more growth opportunities for American companies and more wealth-building opportunities for the broadest range of American investors.”

“As the SEC guts regulations protecting investors from untested issuers, the Commission is simultaneously ‘reliev(ing) a significant portion of all publicly traded issuers from making a wide variety of disclosures that they are currently required to provide,’” the Senators continued. “The result of this wholesale rollback of required disclosure requirements would almost certainly increase the level of fraud and raise the cost of capital.”

The Senators requested that the letter be added to the comment file for all four of the SEC’s proposed deregulatory rules.

title: Peters & Kim Lead Senate Colleagues in Demanding Census Bureau Rescind Proposed Rule That Violates Constitution ➞

committee.name: Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Gary Peters (D-MI), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and Andy Kim (D-NJ), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Census, led a bipartisan group of 24 colleagues urging the U.S. Census Bureau to rescind a proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from census counts and eliminate questions on race and ethnicity.

In their letter, the Senators warn that the exclusion of non-citizens violates the Constitution, which expressly says that the census must count the “whole number of persons in each state.” The Bureau has proposed two methods by which it would exclude non-citizens, both of which would cause undercounts and errors in the census counts.

“We write to urge that you rescind your proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from decennial census counts and omit questions about race and ethnicity from the decennial census. The proposed rule violates the clear meaning of the Constitution, which requires that the Census Bureau count the ‘whole number of persons in each state.’ The proposed rule would also cause communities across the country to be counted inaccurately, jeopardizing their fair representation in Congress and access to billions of federal dollars for education, health care, and public safety services,” the senators wrote.

The letter also describes how the Bureau’s proposal to eliminate race and ethnicity questions would undermine the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws and would degrade the quality of all census data. The compliance of civil and voting rights laws rely on demographic data, and only the decennial census provides accurate and precise data. Additionally, eliminating the collection of race and ethnicity data from the decennial census undermines other federal survey data. Businesses and local governments that depend on such data have said that they would be harmed by this proposed rule.

“In its attempt to undermine the data used for the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws, the Bureau will degrade the accuracy of all other federal survey data, particularly for small and rural geographic areas. The Bureau writes in its own regulatory filing that the proposed rule ‘deteriorates the accuracy’ of ‘fertility/mortality rates, cancer rates, poverty rates, unemployment rates, [and] labor force participation’ because the Bureau relies on accurate decennial census information to adjust and design other survey estimates,” the senators continued. “The Bureau also admits in its filing that the proposal would hamper the usability of data for state and local governments who rely on precise and accurate population estimates for small geographic areas. Businesses and local governments that depend on reliable and complete federal data have warned that the Census Bureau’s proposal would increase costs as data is degraded.”

The full text of the letter is available here.

Joining Senators Peters and Kim in sending the letter were Senators Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Angus King (I-ME), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

title: Blumenthal, 29 Armed Services Democrats & Veterans, Raise Alarm over March Attack on NSA Bahrain, Pentagon's Poor Treatment of Evacuated Military Families
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal, a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, and U.S. Representatives Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Pat Ryan (NY-18) led 30 members of Congress in a letter demanding action and answers from the Pentagon about the poor treatment of military servicemembers and their families who were evacuated from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March 2026.

This letter comes after MS NOW reported on the details of a hasty and traumatic evacuation from NSA Bahrain in March, noting that many military family members have been living out of hotels and short-term rentals and are being required to pay out of pocket to cover these expenses. The letter demands that the Department of Defense right this wrong and support these evacuated military families.

The members of Congress also asked the Secretary how much it would cost to repair the severe damage to NSA Bahrain and how the incapacitation of the base has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the wider Middle East.

“President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress... While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation,” the letter reads.

The members continue, “Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations… We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.”

Specifically, the members requested answers by November 13, 2026 to the following questions:

Why was the Navy’s request to extend the safe haven entitlements for evacuees denied?

Who made this decision?

Why are safe haven entitlements for evacuees being terminated before the arrival of household goods?

What will the Department of Defense do to ensure that evacuees from NSA Bahrain are not paying out of pocket for living expenses incurred by the evacuation?

What processes, if any, are in place for evacuees to receive reimbursement for expenses incurred, and how many reimbursement cases are pending?

Given the damage to NSA Bahrain, which logistic hub (or hubs) has the Department of Defense been using amidst the Iran War?

What has been the operational impact of the loss of NSA Bahrain?

Does the Department of Defense intend to repair and rebuild NSA Bahrain?

If so, how much is the expected cost for such work?

What is the financial cost of the damage to NSA Bahrain?

The Senate signatories of the letter are: Sens. Richard Blumenthal (CT, co-lead), Tammy Duckworth (IL), Kirstin Gillibrand (NY), Mazie Hirono (HI), Jacky Rosen (NV), Elizabeth Warren (MA).

The House signatories of the letter are: Reps. Chris Deluzio (PA-17, co-lead), Pat Ryan (NY-18, co-lead), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Herb Conaway (NJ-03), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Jason Crow (CO-06), Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), John Garamendi (CA-08), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Bill Keating (MA-09), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Adam Smith (WA-09), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Mike Thompson (CA-04), Derek Tran (CA-45), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), and George Whitesides (CA-27).

The full text of the letter is below and is linked here.

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

We write to raise concern over reporting that servicemembers and their families are continuing to face significant hardship following their evacuation from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March this year. Additionally, we seek to better understand how the incapacitation of NSA Bahrain has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the broader Middle East. In an August town hall, Chief of Naval Operations, Adm. Daryl Caudle, said that the Navy would not be using NSA Bahrain for the foreseeable future. This is significant not only for the thousands of servicemembers and their families personally involved, but also because NSA Bahrain is a critical logistics hub that has served as the headquarters for U.S. Naval Forces Central Command and U.S. Navy Fifth Fleet since 1995.

Servicemembers and Their Families are Not Receiving Adequate Support

As you know, President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress. Some have had to move across continents, stay in temporary lodging for months, enroll their children in a new school mid-year, pay out of pocket for significant costs associated with a move and more, all often without access to belongings they were forced to leave behind. While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation.

In a recent town hall, Navy officials relayed that your Department of Defense leadership had denied a request to extend the safe haven entitlements, and that each evacuee had to seek individual approval from the Acting Secretary of the Navy. This is unacceptable. To make matters worse, the signing of a lease is being used as a triggering event for termination of the safe haven entitlement. This is bad policy. Although a family may have signed a lease for a permanent residence, they may still have to use a rental vehicle or stay in temporary lodging while they wait for their household goods to arrive from overseas. Requiring servicemembers to pay out of pocket for expenses that were forced upon them by your mismanagement of the Iran War is wrong. You must fix this.

Loss of NSA Bahrain and U.S. Presence in the Middle East

As the Iran War reaches the ninth month, our constituents have expressed increasing concern about the cost of the conflict and the lack of transparency surrounding U.S. operations and strategic goals in the region. Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations. In August, the New York Times reported that the U.S Navy is now resupplying from Diego Garcia, an island in the Indian Ocean 2,200 miles away from the Persian Gulf. We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.

In executing the Congress’s oversight authority under Article I of the Constitution, we request answers to the following questions by November 13, 2026.

title: Ernst Names Small Business of the Week, Natural Fertilizer

committee.name: Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship

text:
Throughout this Congress, Chair Ernst plans to recognize a small business in every one of Iowa’s 99 counties.

RED OAK, Iowa – U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), Chair of the Senate Small Business Committee, today announced Natural Fertilizer of Harrison County as her small business of the week. Throughout the 119th Congress, Chair Ernst plans to recognize a small business in each of Iowa's 99 counties.

“Abe Sandquist is a grow getter when it comes to operating a small business,” said Chair Ernst. “Over the course of 20 years, Natural Fertilizer has bloomed into a thriving business that has cultivated over 1,000 relationships with partners and farmers across the Midwestern region.”

Abe Sandquist developed the idea of Natural Fertilizer after spending several years developing nutrient management plans for the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. During his time there, Abe’s work revealed that many agricultural producers did not realize the value of organic nutrients until they received professional guidance on how to effectively use them. Seeing this need, Abe established Natural Fertilizer in 2007, providing consulting services focused on nutrient management.

Since then, Natural Fertilizer has transformed into a full-service operation focusing on the nutrient cycle of organic residuals. Beyond building his business, Abe has remained committed to serving his local community. Abe helped launch Woodbine Iowa’s IGNITE Pathways Program and remains an active member of the Iowa Composting Council, where he continues to bring members of the agricultural industry together through nutrient cycle advocacy.

Stay tuned as Chair Ernst continues to recognize outstanding Iowa small businesses with her Small Business of the Week award.

title: Smith Statement on HASC Democrats' Priorities for the 120th Congress
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- House Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Adam Smith (D-Wash.) released the following statement outlining the priorities of the HASC Democrats in the coming Congress.

“My Democratic colleagues on the House Armed Services Committee and I are ready to hit the ground running in the 120th Congress and the top priority will be to conduct vigorous oversight of the Department of Defense and the Trump Administration. As a start, we must demand public transparency and accountability from senior Pentagon officials through increased public testimony. I also believe it is important to reestablish an Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee to help support the committee’s work.

“The list of potential oversight topics is long, but the illegal war against Iran is top of mind for me and the American people. So too are sweetheart deals and favoritism to certain entities and individuals. We must dive into any waste, fraud, and abuse by examining contracts and other financial support awarded to private companies. The list continues with the unauthorized military strikes in the Caribbean and Latin America, the deployment of the military to U.S. cities, and the blatant and corrosive politicization of our Armed Forces and purging of the ranks based on loyalty and ideology are high on the list.

“I continue to listen to voters regarding costs.We must push for the development of a more realistic and sustainable approach to our national security—one that does not require a defense budget in excess of $1 trillion or one paid for with draconian cuts to critical domestic programs. We also need to reform the way resources are spent and accounted for. Investment in new weapon systems must take lessons learned from recent conflicts and provide relevant capabilities in a more cost-effective manner. I also believe the bipartisan efforts on acquisition reform should continue.

“Finally, another cornerstone for this committee has focused on the people who are the heart of our national defense—service members, civilian personnel, and their families. We need to ensure we are recruiting, developing, and retaining the military and civilian talent we need by providing the benefits and standard of living they need. And we need to address the Trump Administration’s sustained assault on the federal workforce and his promotion of loyalty to a political ideology over competence for key senior military and civilian positions, and the erosion of the apolitical foundation of the armed forces.

“I am confident that we can address these issues and many more in the coming Congress. I also look forward to working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to ensure a return to our duty of oversight as a coequal branch of government that is responsible for providing for the common defense and our national security.”

title: Ranking Member Scott to Trump Administration: “Save Everything”

text:
“Any agency employee who ‘willfully and unlawfully conceals, removes, mutilates, obliterates, falsifies, or destroys’ or attempts any such action against a federal record is subject to fine and/or imprisonment for up to three years.”

WASHINGTON – Today, House Education and Workforce Committee Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) issued notices to heads of ten federal departments and agencies under the Committee’s jurisdiction, reminding them of their obligation under the Federal Records Act of 1950 (FRA) to preserve all records that may be in the public interest.

“As you are aware, the FRA requires all departments and agencies in the Executive Branch to collect, retain, and preserve records that document ‘the transaction of public business’ or contain ‘informational value.’ The FRA’s regulations require the head of each federal agency to ‘make and preserve records containing adequate and proper documentation of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, and essential transactions of the agency,’” wrote Ranking Member Scott.

In his letters, the Ranking Member emphasized the importance of full compliance with the law that allows Congress to conduct oversight on behalf of the American people, noting that federal officials and employees who violate the FRA face criminal penalties, including up to three years in prison. In addition, any federal officeholder convicted of violating the FRA can lose their position and be disqualified from holding future federal office.

“The American people have given Congress a clear mandate to root out waste, fraud, and abuse within the Administration. I request an assurance, in writing, by November 18, 2026, that records, documents, data, or information have not been and will not be concealed, modified, removed, transferred, destroyed, or otherwise rendered inaccessible,” concluded Ranking Member Scott.

title: Huffman, Hoyle Warn Changes to U.S. Positions on Wildlife Trade Could Increase Wildlife Trafficking, Zoonotic Disease Risks
text:
Ahead of international conference on wildlife trade, Ranking Members warned Trump political appointees are weakening protections against international wildlife trafficking

Washington, D.C. – House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) and Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife, and Fisheries Ranking Member Val Hoyle (D-Ore.) demanded answers from the U.S. Department of State and Interior regarding U.S. engagement in the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

CITES is an international treaty that regulates the lawful trade in endangered species and combats illegal wildlife trafficking. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) serves as the lead federal agency on CITES issues due to its statutory role in implementing the treaty and its science-based approach to regulating wildlife trade.

However, under the Trump administration, the State Department is asserting itself as the lead agency for CITES, and the U.S. delegation from FWS has been filled with political appointees who are changing the United States’ longstanding positions on key issues. CITES Standing Committee meetings commenced on November 2, 2026, with a number of State Department officials in attendance. The United States has long held that a science-based management approach is key to the treaty’s success. The Ranking Members warned that the delegation is moving away from those science-based principles to favor wildlife trade industry interests, potentially weakening protections for endangered species and increasing the risk of trafficking.

Among these changes is a new position advanced by FWS Deputy Assistant Secretary at the Department of the Interior, Dr. Jenifer Chatfield, a Trump Administration appointee, to turn a blind eye to zoonotic disease risks. At a CITES meeting in July, Dr. Chatfield claimed that wildlife trade does not pose a significant zoonotic risk and that zoonotic risks should not lead to changes in international wildlife trade policy. These are diseases that can spread from animals to people, making safeguards for wildlife trade a matter of public health as well as conservation. Ignoring those risks could leave families and communities more vulnerable to future outbreaks. Dr. Chatfield has come under fire for her close association with industries that would benefit from weaker protections in international wildlife trade.

Dr. Chatfield’s actions are particularly concerning given her track record of involving herself in official government decisions that could benefit her family’s lemur breeding operation and other wildlife businesses. In April, Ranking Member Huffman referred an investigation to the Interior Inspector General regarding Dr. Chatfield’s potential violations of federal ethics rules and federal laws.

Combating wildlife trafficking and other illegal activities that often operate alongside it has long been a bipartisan priority. The Ranking Members emphasized that “Congress has repeatedly expressed its interest in confronting wildlife trafficking, most recently through the 2022 reauthorization of the END Wildlife Trafficking Act. We are firmly committed to ensuring the proper implementation of CITES. Proper implementation safeguards American businesses and helps ensure that traffickers cannot corrupt legitimate trade or exploit global supply chains to undermine species’ survival.”

title: Khanna, Moolenaar Seek Answers on Air Force Changes to China Aerospace Studies Institute

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) and Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party today requested a briefing from the Department of the Air Force on changes to the China Aerospace Studies Institute (CASI) at Air University, raising concerns that decisions affecting the Institute’s resources and personnel could weaken the United States’ ability to understand and counter the People’s Republic of China’s rapidly advancing aerospace capabilities.

In a letter to Air Force Secretary Troy E. Meink, the lawmakers emphasized CASI’s critical role in providing the U.S. government, military, Congress, and the public with research and analysis on the PRC’s aerospace strategy, military modernization, and strategic thinking.

“Under-resourcing CASI’s mission could risk undermining the ability of military leaders and civilian policymakers to understand the PRC’s aerospace strategy and capabilities and, by extension, deter Beijing from using them in a military conflict,” Ranking Member Khanna and Chairman Moolenaar wrote in the letter. “Any potential loss of such expertise is particularly worrisome given the PRC’s continued efforts to rapidly modernize its aerospace forces while expanding its aggressive activities in the Indo-Pacific region.”

The lawmakers further warn that reductions in CASI’s resources or in-house expertise could leave the Air Force and other government agencies less equipped to assess the PRC’s military capabilities, potentially forcing them to rely on costly outside contractors to fill critical knowledge gaps. As the PRC continues to advance its military technology, access to reliable, specialized research will remain essential to informing defense planning and national security policy, the lawmakers added.

“Understanding the PLA’s capabilities in these domains is critical for deterring conflict and, as stated in CASI’s charter, for ‘improving [the U.S.] ability to be successful in strategic competition,’” the Members concluded. “As the PLA continues to expand its aerospace capabilities, our need to understand these advancements will continue to grow.”

The Ranking Member and Chairman have requested a briefing from the Department of the Air Force on its resourcing and personnel decisions concerning CASI by October 30, 2026.

title: FACT SHEET: Heinrich Details How Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act Holds Data Centers Accountable, Lowers Utility Bills for American Families

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, released a fact sheet detailing how his Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will hold data centers accountable, forcing them to pay for grid upgrades instead of passing costs onto electricity customers, helping to lower utility bills for working families.

Heinrich’s fact sheet can be found here and below.

Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act

Making sure data centers pay for their grid costs, lowering utility bills for families

Large data centers can require as much electricity as a small city. When a data center connects to the grid, the utility may need to add or upgrade transmission infrastructure to serve that new demand. If those costs are not assigned to the data center, they can ultimately be reflected in electricity rates paid by other customers. A Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas working paper estimates that data center demand has already pushed up wholesale electricity prices 6.9% nationally, a number that it projects could increase to 12.3% by 2028.

What The Bill Does:

Requires data centers to pay the costs they create. The bill directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to require utilities to establish rates that force large data centers to pay for both the cost of serving them and the grid upgrades needed to handle them. This means the cost of accommodating a new data center does not fall on other electricity customers.

Ends a current barrier to charging data centers for grid upgrades. Current FERC policy generally prevents utilities from charging customers for both their share of existing grid costs and the additional grid upgrades needed to serve that customer. The bill directs FERC to change that policy to ensure that large data centers pay for both. If a data center needs the grid to be expanded or upgraded to power its operations, utilities must charge customers serving that data center for those costs on top of the regular cost of electricity. The bill makes these charges mandatory—not voluntary—ultimately driving down costs for consumers.

Gives states a way to reduce costs for families and businesses. States can use the revenue collected from data centers to reduce electricity rates for homes, small businesses, and other existing electricity customers.

Requires the reporting of information on data center energy usage. Requires the Energy Information Administration to update its annual survey to require utilities to report electricity sales to data centers—which utilities currently report for residential, commercial, and industrial sectors, but not for data centers.

title: Crapo Highlights $185 Million Rural Health Investment Secured Through Working Families Tax Cuts
text:
Washington, D.C.—The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has announced an initial $185 million in funding for Idaho through the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP), a historic $50 billion investment in rural health care established under the Working Families Tax Cuts, spearheaded by U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho). The funding will support Idaho-led initiatives to strengthen rural health care delivery, including innovative care models, workforce development, chronic disease prevention, behavioral and maternal health services and infrastructure improvements for rural providers. Based on priorities established by the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare and a committee created by the state legislature, Idaho’s $185 million allocation is part of the program’s nationwide investment in rural health care over five years.

“From supporting workforce development programs to deploying cutting-edge technologies, these projects will tackle some of the biggest challenges facing Idaho’s rural health care system,” said U.S. Senate Finance Committee Chairman Mike Crapo. “With more funding to come in the next few years, the Rural Health Transformation Program will permanently increase access to high-quality health care across Idaho.”

“For many Idaho families—especially in rural areas—affordable, accessible health care is a real concern. This investment recognizes those challenges and puts resources where they’re needed most. It helps strengthen local health care and ensures Idahoans can get the affordable care they need, no matter where they live,” Idaho Governor Brad Little said.

“President Trump made a historic commitment to rural America, and these investments are turning that commitment into better care for patients in communities across Idaho,” said CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz. “This is what rural health transformation should look like: federal investment that is putting patients first, driving lasting improvements and expanding healthcare for the hardworking Americans who call these communities home.”

Examples of Year 1 RHTP projects in Idaho:

$2.7 million for mobile healthcare vehicles and clinics in southwest and eastern Idaho;

About $900,000 for a mobile pediatric hearing clinic;

$1.2 million for opioid use disorder treatment in Bonneville and Twin Falls Counties;

Almost $7 million to bolster health systems for Idaho’s five Native tribes;

$1.5 million for a mobile dental clinic in north Idaho; and

Infrastructure upgrades at rural hospitals.

$5.8 million for several projects at Bonner General Health in Sandpoint

$6.6 million for clinic modernization at Benewah Community Hospital in St. Maries

$4.8 million for several projects at St. Mary’s in Cottonwood, including purchase of a new MRI machine and x-ray equipment

title: Trade Gap Decreases in September, Ends 50 Percent Above 12-Month Average
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Joint Economic Committee released its analysis of the latest Monthly Trade Update based on information compiled from the Bureau of Economic Analysis, U.S. Census Bureau, Treasury Department, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The total trade deficit in September was $105.05 billion, down from $690 million in August and 50 percent above the 12-month average.

In trade of goods, the U.S. ran a trade deficit of $135.91 billion, down $716 million from August and 36 percent above the 12-month average. In trade of services, the U.S. ran a trade surplus of $30.86 billion, down $26 million from August and 3 percent above the 12-month average.

Over the 12 months through September 2026:

The U.S. ran a total trade deficit of $839.58 billion. In trade of goods, the U.S. ran a trade deficit of $1.20 trillion. In trade of services, the U.S. ran a trade surplus of $358.39 billion. Total exports were $3.73 trillion while total imports were $4.57 trillion.

The U.S. had the largest goods trade deficits with Vietnam, with net exports of -$239.47 billion, 20.34 percent of the total goods trade deficit; Mexico, with net exports of -$235.11 billion, 19.97 percent of the total goods trade deficit; and Taiwan, with net exports of -$223.33 billion, 18.97 percent of the total goods trade deficit.

The U.S. had the largest goods trade surpluses with Netherlands, with net exports of $84.33 billion, -7.16 percent of the total goods trade deficit; United Kingdom, with net exports of $48.77 billion, -4.14 percent of the total goods trade deficit; and Hong Kong, with net exports of $44.92 billion, -3.82 percent of the total goods trade deficit.

The most exported goods by value were civilian aircraft, engines, equipment, and parts; crude oil; and nonmonetary gold. Together, these goods accounted for 17.76 percent of the value of all exported goods over those 12 months.

The U.S. exported the most to Mexico ($381.73 billion), Canada ($344.16 billion), and United Kingdom ($113.97 billion). Together, these countries accounted for 34.85 percent of the value of all U.S. exports over those 12 months.

The most imported goods by value were computers; computer accessories; and pharmaceutical preparations. Together, these goods accounted for 21.76 percent of the value of all imported goods over those 12 months.

The U.S. imported the most from Mexico ($616.84 billion), Canada ($395.97 billion), and Taiwan ($282.50 billion). Together, these countries accounted for 36.11 percent of the value of all U.S. imports over those 12 months.

In September 2026, the U.S. calculated $22.94 billion in import duties, which is 0.75 percent lower than the 12-month average. Over the 12 months through September 2026, the U.S. calculated $277.41 billion in import duties. In September 2026, the average applied duty rate, defined as calculated duty revenue as a share of total imports for consumption, was 6.49 percent, which is 1.46 percentage points lower than the 12-month average.

The U.S. dollar strengthened against three of the five leading global currencies. From September 2025 to September 2026, the U.S. dollar weakened against the Chinese yuan by 5.8 percent, and the Mexican peso by 1.5 percent. The dollar strengthened against the Euro by 3.4 percent, the British pound by 1.3 percent, and the Japanese yen by 6.3 percent. A stronger U.S. dollar can improve U.S. Terms of Trade (ToT) with trading partners by lowering the dollar price of imports from the foreign country. Terms of trade (ToT) is the ratio of a country’s export prices to its import prices. Stronger ToT means a country can buy more imports for a given amount of exports.

For the full update, with greater detail of the U.S. exports, imports, duties, and trading partners, visit https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/trade-update/.

title: Durbin Releases GAO Report Raising Alarms Over Changes In Inspections In ICE Immigration Detention Facilities
text:
SPRINGFIELD – Today, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, led the release of the Government Accountability Office’s (GAO) newly-completed report examining the Trump Administration’s decision to cut U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) inspection requirements of immigration detention facilities. These cuts stand in stark contrast to a massive surge in immigration detention. From April 2025 to April 2026, the average daily detained population jumped by more than 50 percent as active facilities expanded from 128 to 172. This growth was fueled by an explosion in funding, with ICE receiving over $45 billion for immigration detention in those two years alone.

With fewer inspections, there is even less accountability for ICE and its contractors, including widely documented failures to provide adequate medical care and safe and edible food and to prevent suicides. The GAO report is released after Durbin called for the GAO to expand its pending investigation of mental health care to include medical care and mismanagement of federal contracts in ICE detention facilities.

In the report, GAO outlines how detention oversight has been gutted during the second Trump Administration. The GAO examined four Department of Homeland Security (DHS) offices charged with inspecting detention facilities. The DHS Office of the Immigration Detention Ombudsman (OIDO), an independent office with statutory authority to conduct surprise inspections, has been shut down entirely. ICE’s Office of Detention Oversight (ODO) office has decreased its inspections following policy changes under this Administration—it went from inspecting larger facilities twice a year to once a year or less. Its total inspections dropped from 194 to 102 in one year. DHS now allows many smaller facilities to inspect themselves and usually tells facilities in advance when inspectors are coming. ICE justified these changes by stating few inspections would ease the obligations on facilities and would make it easier to contract with local and state partners to detain individuals. ICE Health Service Corps (IHSC), which inspects medical care in detention, has kept its process the same. The DHS Office of Inspector General (OIG) received $20 million for extra inspections.

Consistent with this Administration’s irresponsible and cruel approach to immigration policy, the GAO found ICE’s changes to detention inspections were not backed by data. ICE failed to analyze evidence, such as past inspection deficiencies or contract compliance, to assess how ICE can adequately conduct oversight over its rapidly growing detention facilities and ensure facilities comply with detention standards.

“On Tuesday, the American people overwhelmingly rejected the Trump Administration’s cruel immigration tactics—including inhumane ICE detention facilities, where people lack adequate access to food, water, and medical care,” said Durbin. “Now that the power has shifted in Congress, the Trump Administration should take immediate steps to respond to this new alarming GAO report, which found ICE has reduced inspections without assessing the impact on detained individuals.”

In the report, GAO also noted that another accountability measure recently lapsed. Since Fiscal Year 2019, appropriations language barred funding a contract with a facility after two consecutive less-than-adequate ODO ratings. That provision was left out of the FY26 DHS Appropriations Act. ICE told GAO that failing ratings now will no longer block continued funding, allowing private prison contractors like GEO and CoreCivic to fail inspections by ODO with no consequences.

In the report, GAO urges ICE to use real data to determine whether the reduced inspections are enough to keep facilities safe and compliant, and adjust its inspections based on what it finds.

title: Ranking Member Scott Condemns Trump Effort to Eliminate Magnet Schools

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON –Today, Ranking Member Robert C. "Bobby" Scott (VA-03) issued the following statement after the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel issued a Slip opinion to effectively purge federal support for magnet schools by stating the Magnet Schools Assistance Program (MSAP) is unconstitutional.

“President Trump’s effort to effectively eliminate the Magnet Schools Assistance Program is another step in the Republican Party’s campaign to undermine public education and roll back equal opportunity.

“Created in the wake of Brown v. Board of Education, MSAP helps school districts establish and expand magnet schools that give students from every background access to specialized, high-quality programs in science, technology, the arts, and more. Magnet schools serve 3.5 million students across 4,340 schools in almost every state across the United States, and for many families, they are a path to opportunities that would otherwise be out of reach. Significantly curtailing the application and use of this program will hurt students, families, and communities.

“I disagree with the administration’s position. The opinion draws an incorrect conclusion that MSAP, a federal program created by Congress on a bipartisan basis, violates the Constitution. If President Trump believes the program is unconstitutional, he ought to bring that question to a court, not just declare it so by fiat. MSAP has been operating for over 40 years, working well for families and communities across the nation, and it ought to be able to continue doing so.

“This proposal does not stand alone. The administration has already withheld MSAP funding from school districts, including Fairfax County in Virginia, because they would not abandon policies that support their students. Declaring MSAP unconstitutional and severely restricting its implementation will limit choices for families and make it harder for students from every background to get a quality education.

“As the leader of the House Committee on Education and Workforce, I will fight to protect MSAP and to make sure every student has access to a high-quality public education, no matter their race, income, or ZIP code. Congress must push back against any efforts to do otherwise.”

Background:

In September 2025, the Trump administration announced it would cancel MSAP grants to school districts in Chicago, New York City, and Fairfax County, Virginia, after the districts declined to change policies related to transgender students and diversity programs. Yesterday’s action by the Department declares the program unconstitutional as presently administered.

title: Heinrich Demands Answers on Trump Administration’s Push to Build Data Centers on Public Lands

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
Heinrich: “I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration’s actions to develop data centers on public lands.”

WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, raised the alarm on the Trump administration’s push to develop AI data centers on public lands, demanding answers from Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Director Steve Pearce on the agency’s actions to greenlight data center buildout.

“I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration’s actions to develop data centers on public lands,” Heinrich began.

Heinrich’s letter follows his online post earlier today stating simply, “No data centers on public lands. Period.”

Heinrich’s letter to Pearce comes after multiple actions from the Trump administration to develop data centers on public lands, including the June 2026 BLM approval of the 88-acre Townsite Data Center in Boulder City, Nevada. While the project was paused by the Department of the Interior’s Board of Land Appeals in September 2026, its approval was initially spurred by a 2025 Trump Executive Order that expedited the permitting of data center development on public lands.

BLM is now reportedly considering at least 15 proposals to build data centers or related infrastructure on public lands, covering more than 17,000 acres of public lands and stretching across six Western states. According to the Salt Lake Tribune, BLM asked state directors to identify public lands ready for data center development — something the Department of the Interior’s leadership told officials is a high priority.

“When BLM makes decisions about public land, it should always consider the best interest of the public and the communities that will be directly impacted by its decision,” Heinrich wrote.

“BLM should listen to the voices of the American people and carefully consider the many uses of public land before hastily greenlighting data center buildout on public lands,” Heinrich continued.

In the letter, Heinrich specifically requests a complete list of all authorities BLM is using to support data center development on public lands, all data center-related development proposals BLM is considering on public lands, and the public lands BLM has identified that are eligible for data center development.

Read the full letter here and below.

Director Pearce:

I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration’s actions to develop data centers on public lands.

In June 2026, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) approved the first data center on public lands—the sprawling 88-acre Townsite Data Center located in Boulder City, Nevada. At the time, BLM amended an existing right-of-way grant for a solar and battery-storage project to allow for the development of the data center. On September 1, following an appeal by Boulder City, Nevada, and environmental groups, the Department of the Interior’s Board of Land Appeals paused development of the data center, citing BLM’s decision to approve the project without conducting a new National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review. The Board found that Boulder City and the environmental groups “made a persuasive showing that BLM violated NEPA and acted arbitrarily or capriciously when it determined that the data center project is ‘substantially the same’ as the solar plant project for purposes of its NEPA analysis.”

BLM’s decision to approve the Townsite Data Center followed an Executive Order signed by President Trump in July 2025 that expedited the permitting of data centers on public lands. In September, the President signed another Executive Order that grants Secretary Burgum additional independent authorities over energy production on public lands. BLM is now reportedly considering at least 15 proposals to build data centers or related infrastructure on public lands. The development proposals cover more than 17,000 acres of public lands and stretch across six western states. According to a report, BLM recently asked state directors to identify public lands ready for data center development and the Department of the Interior’s leadership told officials that the topic is high priority.

When BLM makes decisions about public land, it should always consider the best interest of the public and the communities that will be directly impacted by its decision. The Multiple Use – Sustained Yield principle of public land management requires the BLM to consider the other uses of public land when considering whether to site a data center in any specific location. BLM should listen to the voices of the American people and carefully consider the many uses of public land before hastily greenlighting data center buildout on public lands.

In light of questions and concerns about BLM’s review of data center development proposals on public lands and related actions, I request you provide the following information by November 20, 2026:

A complete list of all authorities BLM is using to support data center development on public lands. Please include the specific precedent and legal rationale.

A complete list of all data center related development proposals BLM is considering on public lands. For each proposal, please include the specific entity that is backing the project; the precise location of the project; the total acreage of federally owned land under review for development; the precise use of the federally owned land under review for development (e.g., for transmission lines, roads, or physical data center structures); whether the review will entail a NEPA review, or in the case of an existing right-of-way grant, a new NEPA review; and whether the proposal will have a public comment period.

A complete list of all public lands BLM has identified that are eligible for data center development.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this request. Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact my staff at (202) 224-4971.

Sincerely,

title: NEW DATA: Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act Will Hold Data Centers Accountable, Lower Electricity Bills by $50-78 Annually, Save $54 Billion in Health-Related Costs, and Lead to Cleaner Air and Healthier Communities

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M.– New independent analyses released this week from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), Rhodium Group, and Grid Strategies LLC find that Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.) Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) would lower household electricity bills by $50 to $78 annually by 2040, reduce power sector emissions by approximately 20 percent, and avoid $54 billion in cumulative public health damages.

The analyses also find that the legislation would accelerate the connection of clean energy projects to the grid and require data centers to pay billions more toward the transmission infrastructure needed to serve their electricity demand.

“Americans are tired of paying more in utility bills while projects that could lower costs sit stuck in the planning phase for years,” said Heinrich. “These independent analyses show exactly what we stand to gain by fixing our broken permitting system: lower electricity bills, cleaner air, healthier communities, and more reliable energy infrastructure. BAAJA will help get more affordable energy connected to the grid while making sure massive energy consumers like data centers pay up. We should be building the infrastructure America needs, not making families foot the bill for permitting delays.”

BAAJA will deliver lower costs and cleaner air for Americans:

Lower electricity bills: Reduce household electricity bills by $50 to $78 annually by 2040, representing a 3–5 percent decrease in electricity prices, according to Rhodium Group.

Reduce pollution: Cut cumulative power sector CO₂ emissions by approximately 20 percent between 2028 and 2035 compared with current law, according to SEIA.

Save billions in health costs: Reduce cumulative public health damages by an estimated $54 billion, according to SEIA.

Accelerate clean energy: Enable an additional 167 Gigawatt Alternating Current (GWac) of net solar capacity additions between 2028 and 2035 compared with current law, according to SEIA.

Connect more clean energy to the grid: Drive an additional 17–249 Gigawatts (GW) of clean energy resources to connect to the grid through 2040, according to Rhodium Group.

Increase clean energy generation: Increase solar and wind generation to 37.4 percent of total power generation, compared with 19.6 percent under the current permitting regime, according to SEIA.

Avoid massive amounts of emissions: Avoid as much as 1.5 gigatons of cumulative emissions through 2040, according to Rhodium Group — equivalent to almost 35 million gasoline-powered cars off the road or taking 39 coal plants offline for a decade.

BAAJA will also make data centers pay their fair share:

Recover $55 billion in transmission costs: Grid Strategies estimates that changes to federal transmission pricing policy under BAAJA could result in data centers contributing approximately $55 billion toward transmission costs over the next decade.

Collect $35 billion more from data centers: That represents approximately $35 billion more than data centers would otherwise pay under current policy.

title: 165K Jobs Gained in October Beating Expectations, Unemployment Rate Drops to 4.1 Percent
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Joint Economic Committee released its Monthly Employment Update. In October, jobs increased by 165,000 jobs (+159K private sector, +6K government), blowing past expectations of 59,000. At the same time, the unemployment rate ticked down slightly from 4.2 percent to 4.1 percent, while the labor force participation rate ticked up by 0.1 percentage points to 61.9 percent. The broadest measure of unemployment (U-6, which adds underemployment to unemployment) increased by 0.3 percentage points to 7.9 percent.

Revised numbers from September show 31,000 more jobs gained increasing from 29,000 initially reported to 60,000. August numbers were also revised, ending with 24,000 more jobs to end with 186,000 jobs added.

From September to October, the best performing sectors were professional and business services (+70K) and private education and health services (+53K). The worst performing sectors were leisure and hospitality (-13K) and construction (-3K).

From October 2025 to October 2026, the best performing sectors were private education and health services (+525K) and professional and business services (+269K). The worst performing sectors were information (-119K) and financial activities (-99K).

Year over year, for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls, average nominal weekly earnings increased by 3.72 percent while average nominal hourly earnings increased by 3.12 percent. For production and nonsupervisory employees on private nonfarm payrolls, average nominal weekly earnings increased by 3.62 percent and average nominal hourly earnings increased by 3.31 percent.

In September, job openings, a measure of labor demand, decreased by 333,000. The total number of nonfarm job openings was 7.52 million, up from 7.08 million in August. The rate increased by 0.2 percentage points to 4.5 percent. The best performing sectors were state and local government (+108K) and professional and business services (+106K). The worst performing sectors were private education and health services (-20K) and financial activities (-19K).

For the full Employment update and to see more details on the employment situation in each state, visit: https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/employment-update.

title: National Debt Reaches $40.55 Trillion, Increased $2.46 Trillion Year over Year Increasing at an average rate of $4.69 Million Per Minute
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Joint Economic Committee released its latest Monthly Debt Update.

As of November 4, 2026, total gross national debt is $40.55 trillion. Relative to one year ago, total gross national debt is $2.46 trillion higher; relative to five years ago, it is $11.64 trillion higher. Over the past year, the rate of increase averaged $6.75 billion per day, $281.45 million per hour, $4.69 million per minute, or $78,179.17 per second. The increase in gross national debt over the past year amounts to $7,190.37 per person or $18,240.99 per household. Total gross national debt amounts to $118,587 per person or $300,840 per household.

Assuming the average daily rate of growth over the past three years continues, the U.S. will reach $41 trillion by approximately January 15, 2027. At that rate, an increase of another trillion dollars would be reached in approximately 160 days.

As of October 2026, the average interest rate on the total marketable national debt is 3.570 percent. One year ago, it was 3.393 percent; five years ago, it was 1.455 percent. This means that, today, the U.S. is paying more just in interest payments than it was even one year ago, and significantly more than it was five years ago.

Interest rates have a significant impact in how much the U.S. pays on debt. The total amount of interest paid to trust funds over the past 12 months was $291.75 billion, an average of $24.31 billion per month. Net interest as a share of outlays is forecast by the Congressional Budget Office to be 13.95 percent in FY2026, 14.25 percent in FY2027, and 14.94 percent in FY2028.

Please see the full Monthly Debt Update for greater detail of the nation's debt profile.

title: Heinrich, Whitehouse, Capito, Lee Release Substitute Amendment to Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairwoman of the EPW Committee; Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the ENR Committee; released a Substitute Amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA). The Substitute Amendment includes clarifying, conforming, and technical edits to reflect feedback received since BAAJA’s introduction in September.

“I’ve worked hard to incorporate the feedback we’ve heard from Tribes and New Mexicans into this SubstituteAmendment, and I’m proud to join my colleagues in releasing it today. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help lower energy costs, strengthen Tribal consultation, and create more good-paying jobs. It also makes sure data centers pay for the energy they use and the grid upgrades they cause, instead of passing those costs on to New Mexico families. Americans can’t afford to wait for lower electricity prices. We need to pass this bill now,” said Heinrich.

“I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves BAAJA and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received. Now’s it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build big things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs,” said Whitehouse.

“This substitute amendment preserves the foundation of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, while making targeted changes based on feedback from our members and stakeholders to further build support. I’m thankful for my colleagues’ efforts to strengthen this legislation, the contributions from members of the House, and the support of countless organizations from across the country. I urge the swift passage of BAAJA to make life more affordable for American families,” said Capito.

“We have spent months working across party lines on both sides of Capitol Hill and with President Trump to deliver permitting reform that makes it easier to build in America. This substituteamendment reflects that work and brings us closer to getting the job done. Our permitting system takes too long, costs too much, and leaves too much uncertainty for the people trying to build what our country needs. We have an opportunity to lower costs for American families, and get America building again. It’s time to finish what we started,” said Lee.

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairman of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the ENR Committee; and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the EPW Committee, released a substitute amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA). The substitute amendment includes clarifying, conforming, and technical edits to reflect feedback received since BAAJA’s introduction in September.

“We have spent months working across party lines on both sides of Capitol Hill and with President Trump to deliver permitting reform that makes it easier to build in America. This substitute amendment reflects that work and brings us closer to getting the job done. Our permitting system takes too long, costs too much, and leaves too much uncertainty for the people trying to build what our country needs. We have an opportunity to lower costs for American families, and get America building again. It’s time to finish what we started,”ENR Committee Chairman Lee said.

“This substitute amendment preserves the foundation of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, while making targeted changes based on feedback from our members and stakeholders to further build support. I’m thankful for my colleagues’ efforts to strengthen this legislation, the contributions from members of the House, and the support of countless organizations from across the country. I urge the swift passage of BAAJA to make life more affordable for American families,” EPW Committee Chairman Capito said.

“I’ve worked hard to incorporate the feedback we’ve heard from Tribes and New Mexicans into this Substitute Amendment, and I’m proud to join my colleagues in releasing it today. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help lower energy costs, strengthen Tribal consultation, and create more good-paying jobs. It also makes sure data centers pay for the energy they use and the grid upgrades they cause, instead of passing those costs on to New Mexico families. Americans can’t afford to wait for lower electricity prices. We need to pass this bill now,” ENR Committee Ranking Member Heinrich said.

“I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves BAAJA and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received. Now’s it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build big things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs,” EPW Committee Ranking Member Whitehouse said.
