title: Grassley Opens Executive Business Meeting on Four District Court Nominees
text:
Prepared Opening Statement by Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa

Chairman, Senate Judiciary Committee

Executive Business Meeting

Tuesday, November 10, 2026

Good morning. On today’s agenda, we have 18 nominations and one bill. We’ll vote on four district court nominees: Daniel Ballou, Richard Bennett, Courtney Coker and Kyle Reardon.

The remaining nominations and the bill will be held over for future consideration. Before we turn to today’s agenda, I’d like to say a few words.

The American Bar Association (ABA) continues to find itself in hot water – and with good reason. Although it claims to be an unbiased organization, it routinely takes public positions on divisive political, legal and social issues.

I won’t repeat the laundry list of the ABA’s rampant partisan activities. Indeed, I’ve run through that litany on many occasions this Congress. But I’ll remind you that the ABA has repeatedly advanced hostile positions towards the Second Amendment and immigration enforcement, and it has promoted harmful abortion and liberal gender ideologies.

The ABA’s political agenda has – of course – tainted its credibility in rating judicial nominees.

It’s well documented that – historically, speaking – a poor ABA rating has reflected a bias against conservatism. And there are dozens of examples of that across Republican administrations.

Like a broken clock, the ABA strikes midnight again, baselessly labeling a Republican president’s nominees as “minority Not Qualified.”

Although the ABA squandered its credibility long ago, I feel compelled to address this issue again because it affects multiple nominees pending before us today and in the coming weeks.

So, let’s take a look at...Judge Ballou, nominated to the Eastern District of Kentucky. He’s been a state judge for nearly a quarter of a century. It’s hard to imagine how any nominee could be more qualified for a judgeship than a current judge with that much experience. The ABA provides no justification for its rating of minority Not Qualified. It’s the fox guarding the hen house, telling us to trust it...

The ABA’s ratings lack any transparency. They’re illogical, inconsistent and plainly tainted by political bias. I’d say that they should be taken with a grain of salt, but that’d be giving them too much credit.

In spite of the ABA’s baseless attempts to discredit recent nominees, the Senate has confirmed nearly 60 highly qualified Article?III judges so far this Congress. I look forward to today’s votes so that we can get to work confirming more.

Now I’ll turn to Senator Durbin for his remarks.

title: Grassley Opens Judiciary Committee Nominations Hearing to Consider Circuit, District and Executive Nominees
text:
Prepared Opening Statement by Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa

Chairman, Senate Judiciary Committee

Nominations

Tuesday, November 10, 2026

I’d like to welcome everyone to today’s hearing. Today, we’ll have two panels.

The first panel features Todd Butler, who is nominated to serve on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit.

Our second panel has three district court nominees: Samuel Adkisson, for the Eastern District of Tennessee; Philip Axt, for the District of North Dakota; and Bradford Kelly, for the Eastern District of Louisiana.

Our second panel will also feature Arthur Kleinschmidt, who is nominated to serve as the Assistant Attorney General for the Office of Justice Programs.

Because we have a number of introducers and a lot to get through today, I’m going to be brief to keep us on schedule.

Today’s nominees feature a wide array of backgrounds. Mr. Butler has extensive experience in private practice. Mr. Adkisson and Mr. Kelley are public servants at the federal level. And Mr. Axt serves at the state level as North Dakota’s Solicitor General. They’re all exceptional attorneys.

On multiple occasions, I’ve noted that the president continues to nominate individuals with military backgrounds. I think that disciplined experience is an asset to the federal bench. Mr. Kelley and Mr. Axt both served in our nation’s military. And I thank them for their service.

Dr. Kleinschmidt also has an inspirational story. As a clinician, he’s dedicated years to helping Americans in addiction counseling. He’s managed many grants, including those that help victims of the opioid crisis. He’s a leader in that field.

I look forward to hearing from all of our nominees today.

I’ll now turn it over to Ranking Member Durbin.

title: ICYMI: Grassley in Wall Street Journal: Senate Republicans Must Advance and Confirm as Many Pending Judges as Possible
text:
The GOP’s Narrow Window to Confirm Judges

By Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa)

November 10, 2026

Wall Street Journal

GOP lawmakers will have their work cut out for them next year fighting socialism’s creeping influence in the legislative branch. I’m confident my party will rise to the challenge. But first, Senate Republicans can safeguard our nation’s founding principles for generations to come by confirming President Trump’s remaining judicial nominees to lifetime appointments on the federal bench.

As the chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee, I am committed to advancing constitutionalist judges. The committee already has a proven record of efficiency and success this Congress. Under my leadership, the Judiciary Committee has moved judicial confirmations at the fastest pace since the Reagan administration.

Democrats clearly intend to use their newfound power next Congress to wage an obstruction campaign. Blocking Mr. Trump’s nominees to the federal courts was one of Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s stated motivations for taking back the Senate. The incoming Democratic chairman of the Judiciary Committee has called for a “hard reset on the nominations process.” The stakes are far too high for Republicans to take their feet off the gas now.

I’ve scheduled two hearings within an eight-day span this month to consider district and appellate nominees. You can expect Democrats to bellyache over the committee’s lame-duck schedule, but no one should fall for their theatrics. This isn’t unprecedented.

The Judiciary Committee has scheduled nomination hearings within two weeks of each other over three dozen times since the Obama administration. Nearly 70% of those hearings were scheduled by Democratic chairmen. And both Republican and Democratic chairmen have previously scheduled hearings for nominees less than 28 days after receiving their nomination materials. Ultimately, the chairman has discretion to set the committee’s schedule.

By year’s end, Mr. Trump will have confirmed over 300 lifetime judges across his two terms. I will have shepherded about half of those judges as Judiciary chairman during Mr. Trump’s first and second terms. The other half owe their success to the chairmanship of my late colleague, Sen. Lindsey Graham (R., S.C.).

Republicans can be proud of the work we’ve done so far to restore the Founders’ vision to the federal judiciary. With a limited window left, we must use the lame-duck session to advance and confirm as many pending judges as possible.

Bolstering the federal judiciary is necessary for the American people to see justice served.

title: Ernst Celebrates America’s Veteran Small Business Owners

committee.name: Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship

text:
Read the release on Sen. Ernst's website HERE.

The week of November 9 through November 13, 2026, will honor veteran small business owners.

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), Chair of the Senate Small Business Committee, is leading a bipartisan resolution with 38 of her colleagues, alongside Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-Illinois), recognizing the week of Nov. 9-13, 2026 as National Veterans Small Business Week.

This week honors the service of our veterans and their entrepreneurial dedication to their communities. As a veteran herself, Senator Ernst recognizes the important role veteran small business owners play in their communities and the opportunities they create for their fellow Americans. Owning a small business is just one of the many ways veterans continue to give back.

“Beyond serving our nation on the battlefield, veterans have established millions of small businesses that create jobs and make a meaningful impact on our economy. I am proud to celebrate their accomplishments this week,” said Chair Ernst.

“Veteran small business owners are among the most hardworking, resilient individuals our great nation has to offer,” said Sen. Duckworth. “Our heroes deserve our full support when they transition back into civilian life, including if they decide to become entrepreneurs. My Veterans Small Business Enhancement Act has helped thousands of Veteran entrepreneurs start and grow their small businesses, and Congress must keep working to honor and support the Veteran small business community.”

Read the resolution here.

Background:

In 2023, Ernst’s Stop Stolen Valor for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Contractors Act, which reduces fraud and stolen valor in federal contracting, was signed into law.

Earlier this year, Senator Ernst hosted her annual Entrepreneur Expo in Ames to help veteran entrepreneurs learn about federal, state, and local government contracting opportunities and federal innovation programs.

title: Smith, Meeks, and Reed Condemn Kushner and Witkoff Efforts to Undermine Ukraine and NATO
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee, and Gregory W. Meeks (D-NY), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, released the following statement condemning Special Envoys Jared Kushner’s and Steve Witkoff’s ongoing efforts to undermine Ukraine and the NATO alliance.

“Ukraine continues to inflict massive casualties on the Russian Army and cripple the Russian economy, while U.S. Special Envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff continue to undermine Ukraine’s ability to negotiate a just and lasting settlement in Putin’s brutal and illegal invasion. As if that weren’t bad enough, they are also undermining NATO, the most successful alliance in history. Their parroting of Kremlin talking points on renegotiating European security and possibly pulling back from Eastern Europe is totally unacceptable to the continued viability of NATO and the national security of the United States.

“This is in addition to the constant pressure from Kushner and Witkoff for Kyiv to surrender sovereign Ukrainian territory, including its fortress belt – key defensive positions preventing a rapid advance westward. They have repeatedly bypassed, ignored, and undercut the U.S. Intelligence Community and State Department. Their Trumpian transactional approach, in which they are treating a nation’s fight for survival like a real estate deal, threatens global stability. They and Trump are working for Putin, not for the benefit of the people of the United States.

“They are also ignoring the message those same American people just delivered to the White House and the Republican Party. The voters have made clear, to a historic degree, their repudiation of the Trump Administration’s blatant corruption and laser focus on self-enrichment ahead of the American interest. Even before this repudiation, Congress and the American people overwhelmingly supported Ukraine and NATO, not only because it is smart, but because it is right. Congress and the American People also understand that Putin responds only to strength. Negotiating away all the pressure from him while undercutting Ukraine has not and will never be successful. Pushing a post-war security agreement that seeks to destroy NATO’s post-Cold War mandate of a ‘Europe whole, free, and at peace,’ benefits only Russia and threatens grave consequences for us and the rest of the world.”

“The Administration has claimed to be in favor of ‘peace through strength.’ The president should inform Kushner and Witkoff that surrendering in Ukraine and appeasing Putin will result in neither peace nor strength.”

title: HEWD Ranking Member Adams Raises Alarm Bells About Sports Betting on College Campuses

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON – Higher Education and Workforce Development (HEWD) Ranking Member Alma Adams (NC-12) delivered the following opening statement at today’s HEWD Subcommittee hearing entitled, “The Rise of Sports Gambling on College Campuses.”

“Let me start with the people this hearing is about: students. They are young adults. Many are living away from home for the first time, carrying debt, and holding a phone that now doubles as a casino.

“My colleagues are right to be worried about sports gambling. College students are especially susceptible to drugs and alcohol, and now gambling is becoming a problem too. Gambling addiction is tied to depression, anxiety, financial ruin, and in the worst cases, suicide. This is a public health crisis unfolding on campuses across America.

“But if we are serious about protecting students, we have to be honest about how we got here.

“For decades, sports betting was illegal in most of this country, with narrow exceptions. Then states were given the power to make their own choices, and they built rules: age limits, licensing, consumer protections, and restrictions on betting involving college athletes. Those laws reflect the judgment of voters and their elected representatives.

“Prediction markets have blown a hole straight through them. By calling a bet an ‘event contract,’ companies like Kalshi and Polymarket claim they aren’t gambling operations at all, but financial exchanges, so state law doesn’t apply. Call it whatever you like. When a college student can wager on a game from his phone, in a state that prohibits it, that is sports betting by another name.

“Congress gave the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) responsibility for overseeing these markets. The CFTC is supposed to be the cop on the beat. The NCAA has asked it to suspend college sports prediction markets until real safeguards are in place. Instead, the cop seems to have left the beat.

“So, we have to ask ‘why?’.

“My colleagues on the House Judiciary Committee are investigating a firm called 1789 Capital. Donald Trump Jr. became a partner days after the 2024 election. The firm took a stake in Juul, and the FDA then approved Juul’s products. The firm also owned a piece of Polymarket. A week after the Justice Department closed its investigation, the CFTC approved a deal that let Polymarket back into the U.S. market.

“I want to be careful. These are questions under investigation, and Mr. Trump Jr. will have a chance to answer them. But the pattern is hard to ignore: the regulator steps back, and the President’s family profits.

“And the ones left unprotected are students.

“The through-line here is predation. Predatory products, aimed at young people, shielded from state law, and overseen by a regulator that is asleep at the wheel.

“Regardless of who profits, students pay. Their grades, their savings, their mental health, and sometimes even their lives.

“We should put students’ safety and well-being ahead of anyone's financial interests, especially the President’s family. That means restoring states’ ability to enforce their laws, demanding real age verification, requiring the CFTC to do its job, and answering the questions my colleagues have asked.

“I look forward to discussing how colleges, regulators, and sports leagues can work collaboratively to protect young adults from the tremendous potential harms of sports gambling and prediction markets.

“Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I yield back.”

###

title: Huffman, Colleagues Demand Answers on Trump Admin Effort to Gut Endangered Wildlife Protections
text:
Lawmakers warn administration’s changes would leave protected species vulnerable to foreseeable deaths and habitat destruction

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.) and Don Beyer (D-Va.), and Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) led 37 other Democratic lawmakers in demanding answers from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the Trump administration’s attempts to gut core Endangered Species Act (ESA) protections by reinterpreting what the agencies consider “incidental take” and “harm” in memoranda to federal employees.

The lawmakers warned the reinterpretation would strip protections from wildlife killed or injured by otherwise lawful activities, even when those deaths and injuries could be foreseen. Under the administration’s interpretation, the law’s prohibition on killing or injuring protected wildlife would apply only when someone deliberately targets a protected species. The lawmakers warned this would undermine decades of safeguards that allow economic activity to proceed while requiring commonsense steps to prevent wildlife deaths and injuries.

“For decades, the ESA has provided a framework for allowing economic activity to proceed while requiring reasonable measures to avoid and minimize harm to threatened and endangered species. These memoranda would undermine that framework by removing incentives to prevent foreseeable wildlife deaths and injuries,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter challenges two identical internal memos issued September 14 by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration General Counsel John Luce. The memos direct staff to interpret “take” — which includes killing or injuring protected wildlife — as covering only intentional actions targeting those animals. The lawmakers are demanding an explanation of the legal basis for that interpretation and whether activities that could foreseeably kill or injure endangered species still require permits.

The directives came as the Trump administration eliminated the longstanding regulatory definition of “harm,” which covered habitat destruction that kills or injures protected wildlife. Both changes took effect the same day, threatening protections for endangered animals and the places they need to survive.

“Any reinterpretation that could eliminate protections for these species is a serious and troubling departure from that framework and would undermine the law’s implementation,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers requested responses by November 30, 2026, including what protections would remain for species threatened by habitat destruction and whether states and Tribes were consulted. They also asked whether Interior would suspend implementation until it publicly explains its legal reasoning and assesses the consequences for endangered wildlife.

“The Services must abandon this approach and preserve the ESA’s longstanding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife and the communities that depend on them,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: Baumgartner Holds Hearing on the Rise of Sports Gambling on College Campuses

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
Today, Higher Education and Workforce Development Subcommittee Vice Chair Michael Baumgartner (R-WA) delivered the following statement, as prepared for delivery, at a hearing titled “The Rise of Sports Gambling on College Campuses”:

“Since a landmark Supreme Court decision paved the way in 2018, many states have rushed to legalize sports betting. What was once an industry on the margins—confined to Las Vegas or Atlantic City—is now legal in 39 states. Online sportsbooks and prediction market apps have placed miniature casinos in the palms of our hands, making placing a bet as easy as checking the weather.

“The sports betting industry has exploded as a result. Prior to the Supreme Court’s decision, Americans wagered just under $5 billion a year through regulated sportsbooks. Last year, it was $167 billion, more than a 3,000 percent increase in less than a decade. More than one in four Americans now have an active account with an online sportsbook.

“Nowhere has the surge of online betting been more pronounced than college campuses. Young people, and young men in particular, gamble at outsized rates. According to an NCAA survey, 67 percent of students living on campus had bet on sports, and 16 percent had shown problem gambling behaviors such as ‘chasing losses’ or spending more money on bets than they planned. Six percent of students reported they had lost more than $500 in a single day. Those figures are from 2023 and are likely even higher today.

“Gambling poses serious risks for everyone, but especially college students. They exhibit problematic gambling behavior at more than twice the rate of the general population. And the earlier young people start gambling, the greater the odds they will develop a gambling disorder later in life, even years or decades later.

“Academic and financial consequences for America’s college students are already here. An undergraduate survey released last month found that 31 percent of male students and 25 percent of female students know someone who had experienced ‘financial distress or academic fallout from online wagering losses.’ Students who had gambled online were 10 percent more likely to report having struggled to pay for basic expenses such as medication, transportation, and housing than students who had never gambled. Another survey alarmingly found that more than one in five students had even used financial aid to place bets.

“Even as sports betting has become a growing problem on campuses, most colleges are not treating it as such. Dr. James Borchers, chief medical officer for the Big Ten Conference, has said gambling has risen to the top of the list of concerns for schools, alongside or even above alcohol. Yet almost half of male undergraduates say their college is ‘underresponding’ to the harms of gambling at their schools. A recent survey of college administrators found that only 3 percent said their institution had updated its financial literacy or orientation materials to provide resources and education around gambling.

“Many colleges already have systems in place to educate students about alcohol and substance use. The same is not yet true for gambling. Right now, the only population on campus required to receive gambling education is student-athletes, because the NCAA requires it. The general student body is largely left without the same information and resources.

“Fortunately, some campuses are leading the way and beginning to address this problem. Today, we’ll hear from our expert witnesses about the research on gambling among college students and innovative ways schools are beginning to educate students on the risks of gambling.”

title: House Passes Financial Services Committee’s Bipartisan Retirement Fairness Bill
text:
Today, the House passed H.R. 1013, the Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act, by a vote of 295-128. Led by Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity Chairman Frank Lucas (OK-03), this bipartisan bill expands retirement investment options for the millions of people working in public schools, community health clinics, and churches who rely on 403(b) plans.

By removing outdated regulatory barriers, the bill permits 403(b) plans to invest in Collective Investment Trusts (CITs) and insurance company separate accounts, cost-effective investment options already available through 401(k) plans. This legislation promotes competition and creates more opportunities for hardworking Americans to grow their retirement savings.

Chairman French Hill (AR-02) said, “Public school teachers, first responders, and nonprofit employees dedicate their careers to serving others, yet outdated laws limit their retirement investment options and can leave them paying higher ees. H.R. 1013 fixes this problem by giving these workers access to the same cost-effective options available in 401(k) plans. I thank Capital Markets Subcommittee Chairman Ann Wagner for her longstanding leadership and Congressman Frank Lucas for his work to advance this bipartisan bill.”

Watch Chairman Hill's floor remarks here.

title: Chairman Babin, Ranking Member Lofgren Applaud Senate Passage of Bipartisan Weather Act Reauthorization

committee.name: House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology

text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, House Science, Space, and Technology Committee Chairman Brian Babin and Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren praised the Senate’s passage of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (S. 3923), introduced by Senator Ted Cruz and a bipartisan group of Senate colleagues.

Chairman Babin and Ranking Member Lofgren issued the following statements:

"Reliable weather forecasts and timely warnings are essential to protecting American lives and property," said Chairman Brian Babin. "Last year's devastating floods in Texas served as a tragic reminder of the need to better predict severe weather and communicate critical information to communities in harm's way. The Weather Act Reauthorization represents an opportunity to modernize our nation's forecasting capabilities and strengthen emergency preparedness. Building on the legislation the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee advanced last September, the Senate-passed bill reflects a bipartisan, bicameral compromise and a shared commitment to protecting American communities. I thank Chairman Cruz, Ranking Member Lofgren, Rep. Lucas, and our colleagues in both chambers for their hard work in reaching this agreement. I look forward to continuing our efforts to get this legislation across the finish line."

"This is a long time coming," said Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren. "The Weather Act Reauthorization will give NOAA the support it needs to carry out its critical mission. I want to thank Chairman Babin, my former Committee partner, Mr. Lucas, and the dedicated staff on both sides of the aisle for getting this to the finish line. The World Meteorological Organization just released its State of the Climate update, emphasizing that the supersized El Niño we are experiencing is expected to bring record heat, flooding, and drought conditions for the next year. Now more than ever, more observations and data are needed to bolster our nation's forecasting capabilities to protect lives, property, the economy, and national security. We have to ensure that NOAA has the tools, staffing, and infrastructure to help support communities prepare for and respond to disasters. This bill will help us do that. I hope the president will see the importance of this legislation and sign it into law soon."

Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee Chairman Ted Cruz and Ranking Member Maria Cantwell also emphasized the importance of the legislation following its passage:

"Today, the Senate took a pivotal step toward ensuring Americans are prepared for severe weather," said Chairman Ted Cruz. "Texans know all too well the devastation storms can bring. The lives lost in the July 4, 2025, Texas floods are a heartbreaking reminder of what is at stake. The Weather Act brings together over a dozen bipartisan bills to modernize radar systems, deliver more accurate and timely forecasts, and improve warnings so families and first responders have more time to act, no matter where they are and no matter the time of day. These improvements will help protect property and, more importantly, save lives in Texas and across the country."

"Americans are facing increasingly dangerous and costly weather disasters, and better forecasts give communities more time to prepare and get out of harm’s way," said Ranking Member Maria Cantwell. "The Weather Act will advance next-generation weather radar, modernize lifesaving warning systems, and improve forecasts for atmospheric rivers and wildfires, like the devastating fires that forced thousands to evacuate in Spokane last month. Today’s Senate passage brings us one step closer to giving forecasters, emergency managers, and communities the tools they need to save lives and protect property."

The Senate-passed legislation builds on the bipartisan Weather Act reauthorization bill advanced by the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee in September 2025. The agreement also incorporates priorities championed by House Republicans, including efforts to modernize NOAA Weather Radio, improve fog forecasting, and address gaps in weather radar coverage.

title: Committee on Small Business Celebrates Seven Committee Bills Passed on the House Floor
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed seven bipartisan bills under suspension unanimously out of the chamber. Chairman Roger Williams (TX-25) issued the following statement on the legislation.

“Today, the House delivered another win for Main Street by passing seven bipartisan bills to strengthen American small businesses,” said Chairman Williams. “These critical measures protect entrepreneurs from foreign cyber threats, bring production back to America, unlock access to capital, and ensure greater accountability at the SBA. Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, and Congress must continue clearing the way for them to succeed. The House has acted. Now it’s time for the Senate to get these bills across the finish line and onto President Trump’s desk.”

---

H.R. 10329, Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026 — introduced by Chairman Williams (R-TX) and Rep. Tran (D-CA)

This bill requires the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA), in coordination with relevant federal agencies, to produce educational materials to help small businesses defend against threats from foreign adversaries, including China, Russia, and North Korea. The materials must address cybersecurity risk, intellectual property and supply chain security, and risks associated with predatory investment and licensing arrangements. The materials would be updated annually to ensure small businesses have current information on emerging foreign threats.

H.R. 10355, Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act — introduced by Rep. Mejia (D-NJ) and Del. King-Hinds (R-CNMI)

This bill requires the SBA to establish procedures ensuring that its disaster field operations centers provide consistent and current outreach materials on the SBA disaster loan program and disaster assistance eligibility requirements.

H.R. 10371, Ensuring SBA Implementation of GAO Recommendations Act of 2026 — introduced by Rep. McIver (D-NJ) and Ranking Member Velázquez (D-NY)

This bill requires the SBA’s Associate Administrator for Veterans Business Development to implement policies that ensure the SBA complies with existing congressional reporting requirements on veterans in SBA programs.

H.R. 10353, SBIC Reporting Modernization Act of 2026 — introduced by Reps. Finstad (R-MN) and Morrison (D-MN)

This bill requires the SBA to publish quarterly, rather than annual, reports on the performance of the Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) program.

H.R. 10238, Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act of 2026 — introduced by Reps. Wied (R-WI), Van Duyne (R-TX), Del. King-Hinds (R-CNMI), and Latimer (D-NY)

This bill requires the SBA to provide small businesses with cybersecurity information and best practices, as well as guidance to help contractors meet Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) compliance requirements.

H.R. 9718, Reshoring American Manufacturing Act of 2026 — introduced by Reps. Wied (R-WI), Van Duyne (R-TX), Ellzey (R-TX), and Olszewski (D-MD)

This bill codifies the SBA’s Make Onshoring Great Again Portal, which provides small businesses with information, contacts, and resources to support the onshoring of manufacturing operations to the United States.

H.R. 10375, 504 Modernization and Small Manufacturer Enhancement Act of 2026 — introduced by Ranking Member Velázquez (D-NY) and Chairman Williams (R-TX)

This bill modernizes the SBA’s 504 lending program by adding workforce development to the program mission, updating occupancy and leasing requirements, streamlining loan-closing procedures, and clarifying that the 7(a) “credit elsewhere” requirement does not apply to the 504 program.

title: Promises Made, Promises Kept: House Republicans Deliver Historic Healthcare and Benefits Expansion to Millions of Veterans and American Families on Veterans Day
text:
On Veterans Day, House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs Chairman Mike Bost (R-Ill.), Speaker of the House Mike Johnson (R-La.), Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.), Majority Whip Tom Emmer (R-Minn.), House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (R-Mich.), Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa), and Rep. Tom Barrett (R-Mich.), released the following statements after the House unanimously passed H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act. This pro-taxpayer, landmark veterans’ package expands rural and urban healthcare access, advances education and job opportunities, expands mental health and substance abuse treatment options, supports America’s Gold Star families, cuts red tape and improves operations at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and finally delivers the Maj. Richard Star Act to over 60,000 combat-wounded, medically retired disabled veterans.

“The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act is a historic healthcare and benefits expansion that will positively impact millions of veterans and American families. This landmark bill finally reduces the wounded veteran tax, it expands mental health options, it improves the Transition Assistance Program, it advances pro-growth policies to ensure veterans and their families can access the healthcare and benefits they are eligible for,” said Chairman Bost. “We have found a pathway to finally get these historic healthcare, benefits, and transformations done at VA for veterans and American families for the first time in years and I am committed to working with the Senate to get this bill over the finish line and to the president’s desk before the end of the year. The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act is for families like the Brileys, the Edmundsons, the young Gold Star spouse who is raising a family, the caregivers whose lives were forever changed by their loved one’s military service and provide support, and the veterans who live with the visible wounds of military service every single day. This bill will make a difference in their lives. This bill will help families make ends meet. This bill will uphold the promise. My message to our entire veteran community with the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act passing out of the House on Veterans Day is simple: House Republicans – America – has got your back.”

“From the first American soldiers who defeated the most powerful army on Earth, to the liberators of Europe during World War II, to the heroes who answered the call of duty after our nation was attacked on 9/11, American veterans have played an indispensable role in the history and unmatched success of our republic. For their sacrifice and service, we have a duty to uphold the promise this country made to the men and women who pledged their lives to defend it,” said Speaker Johnson. “The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act keeps that promise by strengthening health care and mental health services, expanding education and economic opportunities, modernizing veterans’ benefits, and supporting the caregivers and military families who serve alongside our veterans. This legislation delivers for every veteran and every future man or woman who will answer the call to put on the uniform, and we are grateful to Chairman Bost and the Veterans’ Affairs Committee for their work to get this transformational package across the finish line.”

“This Veterans Day, House Republicans are reaffirming our commitment to those who served. The House passed a package of more than 60 bills to strengthen veterans’ healthcare, improve access to VA benefits and services, and expand economic opportunities. The Take Care of America's Veterans Act ensures that the American heroes who fought for our country receive the care and benefits they earned – without burdensome red tape. House Republicans are committed to leaving no veteran behind,”said Leader Scalise.

“We have a responsibility to ensure our veterans have the support, resources, and care they’ve earned. The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act will have an immediate impact on our veteran community by expanding access to mental health care, increasing benefits for combat-injured and disabled veterans, cutting red tape that interferes with timely access to medical care, and enhancing benefits for the surviving families of those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedom,” said Majority Whip Emmer. “Chairman Bost and the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs have worked tirelessly on this legislation, and I thank them for their work and share their commitment of taking care of our nation’s veterans.”

“When someone volunteers to defend our country, we make them a promise. If they come home wounded, if they need health care, if their family needs support, America will be there. This bill helps ensure America keeps its word,” said Chairwoman McClain.

The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act includes over 60 bipartisan provisions to provide the largest healthcare and benefits expansion to veterans, their families, and their survivors in decades, including a range of policy proposals led by the following key members:

"Our veterans gave everything for this country, and they earned the very best care it can provide. This package delivers it. It puts doctors, not bureaucrats, back at the center of veterans' health care and expands access to treatment both inside the VA and in the community,"said Dr. Miller-Meeks. "It cuts the red tape that has kept veterans waiting far too long for the care they need, and it stands behind the caregivers who serve our heroes day and night, often at great sacrifice to themselves. As a physician and a 24-year Army veteran, I can think of no greater honor than fighting for those who wore our nation's uniform. To every veteran and every family who has carried the weight of that service: we see you, we thank you, and we will never stop working to keep our promise to you."

“The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act combines dozens of bipartisan bills to make critical reforms that will help the VA meet veterans’ needs. This includes the long-overdue Major Richard Star Act that provides veterans injured in combat with full retirement pay and eight of my bipartisan bills that will help reduce health care wait times, improve customer service, expand financial support for disabled veterans and Gold Star families, and more,” said Rep. Barrett.

In addition to the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, the House also passed H.R. 8552, the Veterans’ Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act, this week.

title: Senators Warren and Coons Direct Lutnick, Rubio and Miller to Preserve NVIDIA Records Following Reports of Foreign Intelligence Operation Targeting CEO Jensen Huang

committee.name: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

text:
“This incident raises significant concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export controls and protect our national security.”

Read Letter Here (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – Following alarming reports that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected spy for China’s intelligence service, U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, and Chris Coons (D-Del.), Ranking Member of the East Asia, the Pacific, and International Cybersecurity Policy Subcommittee of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, sent a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Secretary of State and National Security Advisor Marco Rubio, and White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller directing the Trump Administration to preserve all documents, communications, records, and other materials related to NVIDIA’s exports of advanced AI chips to China and related national security risks.

“We also request that you preserve all records and materials specifically related to this reported intelligence operation, confirm in writing by November 17 that preservation directives have been issued across your respective offices, and brief Members of Congress regarding the risks this operation may have posed to our national security,” the Ranking Members wrote.

The letter follows recent reporting that senior Trump Administration officials were aware of intelligence suggesting that the NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang had a close personal relationship with an executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced NVIDIA AI chips since June 2024. The executive was reportedly a suspected Chinese intelligence operative who may have passed sensitive information about NVIDIA technology to Chinese intelligence services. Megaspeed is also reportedly under investigation by the Department of Justice for potentially diverting advanced AI chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls. A Commerce Department investigation into the company was reportedly altered following communications with NVIDIA representatives.

In the letter, the senators raised serious concerns about the Administration’s handling of these reported concerns and its ability to enforce export controls and protect American national security.

“Reports suggest that officials within the government – including at the White House, State Department, and Commerce Department – were aware of concerns about NVIDIA, its relationship with Megaspeed, and the suspected Chinese intelligence operation, yet did not move to block the continued flow of advanced AI chips to Megaspeed or other companies affiliated with the suspected operative,” Warren and Coons noted. “Questions also remain regarding whether or not prudent defensive counter-intelligence action was taken or national security recommendations were overruled.”

To inform congressional oversight of export control policy and foreign relations and consideration of related legislation, the senators called for the preservation of records involving communications between NVIDIA executives and senior Trump Administration officials, investigations into potential smuggling of NVIDIA’s advanced AI chips, and decisions to weaken or suspend export controls on advanced AI technology. The senators also requested a congressional briefing on the national security risks posed by the suspected intelligence operation.

title: Shaheen, Booker, Coons, Merkley, Van Hollen Demand State Department Action Amidst Escalating Conflict in Ethiopia
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, Cory Booker (D-NJ), Ranking Member of the Africa and Global Health Policy Subcommittee, Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio urging diplomatic engagement to address the fighting between the Ethiopian military and armed groups as well as escalating tensions with Eritrea.

In the letter, the Democratic Senators on the Africa Subcommittee detail the events in Tigray between the Ethiopian government and the armed groups in the region, including a strike on U.S.-funded humanitarian assistance and deteriorating diplomatic ties between Ethiopia and its neighbors. The Senators states that these events could lead to a multi-front conflict that could destabilize the broader Horn of Africa, Red Sea, our partners in the Gulf and vital shipping lanes. In the letter, the Senators urgeSecretary Rubio to help protect Americans, ramp up diplomacy in the region to address political and territorial disputes, surge humanitarian assistance and discourage other actors from military intervention in the conflict.

“Hostilities between Ethiopia’s federal government and opposition forces have shattered the fragile peace in Tigray established by the 2022 Pretoria Agreement, which ended a devastating two-year war between the federal government and Tigrayan forces. That conflict resulted in an estimated 600,000 deaths and approximately 120,000 victims of conflict-related sexual violence,” wrote the Senators.

“The growing threat of long-range attacks against Ethiopian military targets and Ethiopian airstrikes in civilian areas could place Americans in the crossfire of an expanding conflict. We urge the Department to ensure that Americans in Ethiopia have the information and assistance necessary to reach safety,” continued the Senators.

“The State Department should work with the Department of Homeland Security to urgently reinstate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for eligible Ethiopian nationals residing in the United States. Renewed fighting raises serious concerns about the safety of returning Ethiopian nationals. Reinstating TPS would provide critical protection to eligible individuals already in the United States who cannot safely return home, consistent with the program's purpose of protecting foreign nationals from removal when extraordinary and temporary conditions make return unsafe,” concluded the Senators.

Full text of the letter is available HERE and provided below.

Dear Secretary Rubio:

We write to urge sustained and coordinated diplomatic engagement to address fighting between armed groups and the Ethiopian military and escalating tensions with Eritrea. Hostilities between Ethiopia’s federal government and opposition forces have shattered the fragile peace in Tigray established by the 2022 Pretoria Agreement, which ended a devastating two-year war between the federal government and Tigrayan forces. That conflict resulted in an estimated 600,000 deaths and approximately 120,000 victims of conflict-related sexual violence.

Since August, there have been clashes in Tigray, and the Ethiopian government has launched a series of drone strikes, including a September 20 strike that hit a Catholic Relief Services aid convoy carrying U.S.-funded humanitarian assistance. Ethiopia faces multiple, overlapping conflicts and the prospect of a new war between Ethiopia and Eritra appears high. Fighting between the Ethiopian military and Fano forces continues across Amhara, while an insurgency persists in parts of Oromia. Eritrean forces are reportedly present in Tigray, and Ethiopia and Eritrea have cut diplomatic ties. Ethiopia has also expelled an Egyptian diplomat amid accusations that Egypt is supporting the rebel alliance. Egypt has in turn responded by expelling a senior Ethiopian diplomat from Cairo. The war in neighboring Sudan presents an additional risk of regional escalation, with Ethiopia reportedly supporting the Rapid Support Forces and accusing the Sudanese Armed Forces of providing support to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

The situation could lead to a multi-front conflict that would risk destabilizing Ethiopia the broader Horn of Africa, the Red Sea, our partners in the Gulf, and vital shipping lanes. The United States should bring new diplomatic energy and policy tools to bear before the conflict escalates further.

We respectfully ask that you:

Assist Americans in need of emergency support. The growing threat of long-range attacks against Ethiopian military targets and Ethiopian airstrikes in civilian areas could place Americans in the crossfire of an expanding conflict. We urge the Department to ensure that Americans in Ethiopia have the information and assistance necessary to reach safety.

Ramp up U.S. diplomacy to support an immediate ceasefire and renewed mediation. U.S. diplomatic engagement has lacked the urgency, visibility, and coordination commensurate with the threat of another devastating civil war in Ethiopia and regional conflict. The Pretoria Agreement, reached with significant diplomatic support from the United States, stopped the last war in Tigray. However, it failed to resolve many of the underlying political and territorial disputes and excluded key actors involved in both the previous and current conflicts, including the Fano and Oromo Liberation Army. The United States should urgently support a renewed political dialogue that brings all relevant actors to the table and reflects the changed circumstances of the current conflict. In particular, any discussion of a military acquisition of the Port of Assab should be off the table and we urge the State Department to avoid offering Port acquisition as a diplomatic tool during any negotiation. It should be made clear that any attempt by the Ethiopian government to forcibly access the Port of Assab will not be supported or accepted by the United States.

Protect civilians and ensure humanitarian access. Use all available diplomatic and policy tools to press parties to protect civilians, end the use of drones and heavy weapons in civilian areas, protect farmland and harvests, maintain communications access, and safeguard civilian infrastructure that enables safe and unimpeded humanitarian assistance. Further, comprehensive and regular humanitarian assessments must be conducted and made public to understand the full extent of the need on the ground.

Delay of arms sales to Ethiopia. In May, the Administration lifted its policy of denying arms exports to Ethiopia under International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), and in September allowed the Ethiopia-related sanctions regime to expire. The United States should not allow new arms sales to Ethiopia while hostilities continue.

Prevent further regionalization of the conflict. Use U.S. diplomatic leverage with Eritrea, Egypt, Sudan, and other regional actors to discourage military intervention, the provision of weapons or other material support to armed groups, and other actions that could widen the conflict. The United States should make clear that Ethiopia should not be the arena for a regional proxy war and should work with regional partners to prevent further escalation across the Horn of Africa.

Surge Humanitarian Assistance. El Niño is driving devastating droughts in East Africa. In Ethiopia, rainfall deficits this summer exceeded 50 percent of average, setting up poor harvests. Coupled with renewed fighting, mass displacement, and disruptions to humanitarian access, these conditions threaten to push vulnerable communities toward catastrophe. The Bureau of Disaster and Humanitarian Response should urgently scale up emergency food assistance, nutrition interventions, and other lifesaving humanitarian support to avert the worst outcomes.

Reinstate Temporary Protected Status. The State Department should work with the Department of Homeland Security to urgently reinstate Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for eligible Ethiopian nationals residing in the United States. Renewed fighting raises serious concerns about the safety of returning Ethiopian nationals. Reinstating TPS would provide critical protection to eligible individuals already in the United States who cannot safely return home, consistent with the program's purpose of protecting foreign nationals from removal when extraordinary and temporary conditions make return unsafe.

We look forward to your response.

title: Peters, Schumer, Jeffries and Garcia Statement on Sham Nomination Process for Next GAO Leader ➞

committee.name: Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Gary Peters, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and Chuck Schumer, Senate Democratic Leader, and U.S Representatives Hakeem Jeffries, House Democratic Leader, and Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, issued the following statement after Chairman Rand Paul initiated a sham process to recommend nominees to serve as the next Comptroller General of the Government Accountability Office (GAO) for a 15-year term:

“This afternoon, Chairman Rand Paul’s office requested submissions of candidates to serve as the next Comptroller General of GAO with a deadline of less than 24 hours. This is clearly a sham to enable President Trump to appoint a handpicked nominee to lead Congress’ watchdog. We cannot allow President Trump to install a fox in the henhouse at an agency Congress relies on to provide independent, nonpartisan oversight, and expose waste, fraud, and abuse across the Trump Administration.

“Counter to the last time a GAO Comptroller was selected in 2010 in a yearlong, bipartisan process, Republican leaders have never convened the Commission for meetings, and the Commission has not interviewed a single candidate for this critical role, despite repeated requests to begin the process over the last two years. Every Member of Congress who values independent oversight and good stewardship of taxpayer dollars should call this out for what it is – a transparent effort to ram through another Trump crony at the 11th hour, and undercut Congress’ ability to conduct effective oversight of the Trump Administration.”

GAO is Congress’ nonpartisan watchdog, conducting research, investigations and audits that support Congressional oversight of the Executive Branch. By statute, a bipartisan, bicameral Commission is central to the process of selecting a new Comptroller General. The 10-member Commission recommends at least three candidates, and the President chooses a nominee from the Commission’s recommendations. In the past, the Commission engaged in an extensive process, seeking a wide range of applicants and reviewing and interviewing candidates in a bipartisan manner. The bipartisan Commission is made up of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the majority and minority leaders of the House and Senate, the Chair and Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and the Chair and Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. All three times the Commission process has occurred in the past, the president has selected a nominee with bipartisan support.

title: Smith, Courtney Express Deep Frustration Over Failure to Notify Congress of USS South Dakota Command Triad Relief
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representatives Adam Smith (WA-09), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee, and Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, and sent a letter to the Department of the Navy expressing their deep frustration over the Navy’s failure to notify Congress of the relief of the USS South Dakota (SSN 790) Commanding Office, Executive Officer, and Chief of the Boat in October 2026. To view the letter, click here.

FULL LETTER TEXT

Dear Acting Secretary Cao and Admiral Caudle:

We write to express deep frustration over the Navy’s failure to notify the House Armed Services Committee of the relief of the Commanding Officer, Executive Officer, and Chief of the Boat of the USS South Dakota (SSN 790) on October 14, 2026.

On November 11, 2026, a reporter requested comment on the dismissal of SOUTH DAKOTA’s command triad, allegedly attributed to a grounding incident. Though nearly a month after the relief of the command triad, no notifications of the personnel actions or the underlying incident had been made to the House Armed Services Committee. On November 12, 2026, an article was published on the incident, including confirmation from the public affairs office for Commander, Submarine Force Atlantic that the commanding officer of SOUTH DAKOTA was relived from his role on October 14, 2026.

The Department of the Navy’s failure to communicate these incidents to Congress is unacceptable. The committee and Department maintain long-standing customs for information sharing, that though not expressly written in statute, have included notifications for various types of at-sea incidents, accidents, and dismissals of members of the command triad. In the wake of the collisions affecting USS Fitzgerald (DDG 62), USS John S. McCain (DDG 56), and the grounding incidents involving USS Hartford (SSN 768) and USS Connecticut (SSN 22), clear and timely communication with Congress was necessary to make informed decisions to ensure personnel safety and readiness of the fleet. Even after these events, Congress relied on continued good-faith communication with the Department, as opposed to codifying notification

requirements. Failing to provide timely notifications to Congress is counterproductive to good policymaking and undermines the Department’s stated goals of transparency and accountability and put leadership judgement into question.

To date, the Department of the Navy has not provided the committee with an official notification of the details of the CO’s dismissal. The Navy’s lack of transparency leave many outstanding questions about not only what occurred, but the impact of the events leading the triad’s dismissal on the structural health of SOUTH DAKOTA, the well-being of the crew, and whether the incident laid bare any systemic issues with training to standard procedures that must be addressed. As a result of the Navy’s failure to communicate, what should have been a standard exercise in information sharing has instead raised questions about the Navy’s commitment to transparency and its commitment to a productive working relationship with Congress.

We request the following information to be provided not later than November 20, 2026:

What events led up to the relief of the entire SOUTH DAKOTA command triad on October 14, 2026?

Was their dismissal a result of a grounding or other mishap at sea? If so, provide details of the circumstances of the grounding or other mishap at sea.

If a grounding or mishap occurred, what is the preliminary cost assessment of damages?

If a grounding occurred, what are the details on the structural damages to SOUTH DAKOTA?

If a grounding occurred, what is the expected timeline for maintenance following the grounding of SOUTH DAKOTA?

If a grounding occurred, how many injuries were incurred and what were the extent of injuries?

7. What is the reason for the decision not to notify Congress, in contradiction of past standard practice?

title: Pallone and Wyden Call on Trump Administration to Immediately Delay Implementation of Medicaid Paperwork Requirements

committee.name: House Committee on Energy and Commerce

text:
Washington, D.C. – House Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) wrote to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz asking the Trump Administration to immediately delay implementation of the Medicaid paperwork reporting requirements set to go into effect on January 1, 2027.

“CMS must immediately exercise its statutory authority and available enforcement discretion to give states additional time to implement work reporting requirements and protect eligible beneficiaries from losing coverage,” Pallone and Wyden wrote to Administrator Oz. “It is clear that CMS must permit all states, consistent with applicable law, to delay denials and terminations of coverage attributable to work reporting requirements until their eligibility systems, verification processes, and beneficiary protections have been fully implemented and tested.”

The letter comes amid mounting uncertainty for states just weeks before the implementation deadline. Last month, a federal court ruled CMS unlawfully narrowed the law’s exemption for medically frail individuals, using a standard so restrictive that even a cancer diagnosis might not qualify. Rather than accept the ruling, Administrator Oz stated the Trump Administration will appeal the decision, leaving states without a final answer on a core policy before the paperwork requirements go live. Pallone and Wyden argued that CMS’ actions and continued legal challenges make it even harder for states to meet an already impossible timeline and urged CMS to grant good faith exemptions to every state that requests one.

The lawmakers also raised alarm that CMS leadership is actively discouraging states from seeking the good faith exemptions Congress built into the law, despite knowing many states are still not ready to implement the new requirements. Pallone and Wyden called on CMS to publicly release state readiness assessments, exemption requests and decisions, and, once requirements take effect, state-level data on coverage denials and terminations.

“Repealing the devastating Medicaid cuts enacted under H.R. 1, including work reporting requirements, will be a top priority of Democrats in the 120th Congress. Until Congress acts, however, CMS has a responsibility to carry out the law as Congress established it, and to ensure that implementation does not unnecessarily jeopardize coverage for eligible beneficiaries,” the Democratic Committee leaders continued. “CMS must recognize these challenges and exercise the authority Congress provided to give states the time and flexibility they need. Failing to permit states to delay implementation despite known operational deficiencies will worsen preventable coverage losses for which Congressional Democrats will hold the Trump Administration accountable.”

title: Gov Watchdog Report Finds Federal Government Failing to Make Coal Companies Clean Up Their Mines
text:
Operators’ bonds fell short at more than half of recently reclaimed mines, leaving American taxpayers to pick up the tab

Washington, D.C. – A new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report, requested by Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Reps. Donald Beyer (D-Va.), Morgan McGarvey (D-Ky.), and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), and Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.), found that states are already paying to clean up coal mines that operators left behind, and the federal government is failing to stop it.

Of 5,247 coal mining permits nationwide, fewer than half have produced coal since 2000, and only 35 percent are in reclamation. As coal companies continue to exit the market, the risk grows that states, Tribes, and American taxpayers will be stuck with cleanup costs that operators can’t or won’t cover.

The watchdog found that several factors have slowed reclamation, including staff cuts at the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement (OSMRE) and limited capacity among state regulators. From 2024 through May 2026, OSMRE’s workforce shrank by 35 percent, weakening the agency’s ability to provide technical assistance, monitor programs, and conduct national studies. Federal regulatory grants to states and Tribes, which oversee 98 percent of coal mining permits, fell by $4.9 million between 2021 and 2026. For more than half of the permits reclaimed between 2019 and 2024, the operator’s bond didn’t cover the full cost of cleanup, which forced states to pay the rest with other funds.

GAO also found that OSMRE does not adequately track or report progress toward its reclamation goals. The agency’s performance measures don’t account for how long it takes to reclaim a site after the coal stops, so they can’t flag which sites may become a financial liability or an environmental risk. OSMRE also hasn’t issued its required annual report to the President and Congress since 2020.

Without accurate measures of reclamation liabilities or regular reporting, Congress lacks the information it needs to judge whether federal oversight is working and whether reforms are needed. Meanwhile, states and Tribes face growing financial risk as coal production, and the revenue that supports reclamation programs, keeps declining.

To address these challenges, GAO recommends that the Department of the Interior and OSMRE:

Conduct strategic workforce planning.

Develop performance measures to track progress toward completing reclamation and returning sites to beneficial post-mining uses.

Speed up reviews of proposed amendments to state and Tribal regulatory programs.

Resume publication of the required annual nationwide performance report.

Read the GAO's full report here.

Background

Coal demand in the United States has fallen by more than 50 percent since 2008. As production drops, communities across coal-producing regions face more unreclaimed mine sites that can threaten environmental quality, hinder economic redevelopment, and leave taxpayers vulnerable to future cleanup costs.

Established by the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977, OSMRE is responsible for making sure coal mining operations protect nearby communities and the environment. The law requires mine operators to reclaim disturbed lands and provide financial assurances, known as bonds, to ensure reclamation can be completed if operators fail to meet their obligations.

title: House Passes Major Richard Star Act, Ending the Wounded Veterans Tax
text:
WASHINGTON – The House of Representatives today passed the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102) by a vote of 392 to 18, ending a six-year fight to stop the Pentagon from clawing back retirement pay from combat-injured veterans.

The bill eliminates the dollar-for-dollar offset that forces roughly 59,000 medically retired, combat-injured veterans to give up military retirement pay for every dollar of VA disability compensation they receive. Retirees who served 20 years collect both. These veterans, forced out early by their wounds, do not.

“Six years ago, Major Star asked Congress to fix this. He died before we could,” said Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39). “Today the House did what a bipartisan majority has wanted to do for years. It took a discharge petition and 218 signatures, and it took veterans who refused to quit, but combat-injured veterans will finally keep what they earned. I thank every Democrat and Republican who signed and every veterans’ organization that stayed in the fight.”

"We did it! After more than six years of fighting, the House has passed my bipartisan bill, the Major Richard Star Act," said Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25). “This is a historic victory for combat-wounded veterans and their families. It ends the wounded veteran tax, so combat-injured veterans receive both the retirement pay and the disability compensation they earned. Our veterans deserve a government that fights just as hard for them as they fought for us. Now the Senate must act. We will not stop until every veteran receives the justice and fairness they have earned.”

“Every Congress since I got here, I’ve signed on to this bill, and every Congress veterans were told to wait,” said Rep. Chris Pappas (NH-01), a cosponsor since 2019. “Combat-injured veterans kept their promise. Today Congress finally kept ours.”

“Today, against the will of the House Republican leadership, we passed a bill to help tens of thousands of my fellow veterans," said U.S. Navy veteran Rep. Chris Deluzio (PA-17). "Right now, veterans who had to retire because of their battle wounds are being denied their full retirement pay and VA disability compensation. By passing the Major Richard Star Act, we are saying that it is finally time to right this wrong and stop blocking these hard-earned veteran benefits. The Senate should pass this measure and send it to the President to sign."

Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL) introduced the bill in 2020. Major Richard Star, a U.S. Army Reserve soldier, advocated for it publicly while battling cancer and died on Feb. 13, 2021, at age 51. Reps. Bilirakis and Ruiz have reintroduced the bill in each Congress since.

The road to passage:

2020: Rep. Bilirakis introduces the bill in the 116th Congress.

2021: Reintroduced after Star’s death. In September, the House Rules Committee blocks it as an NDAA amendment because it lacked an offset.

2023: The bill passes 290 House cosponsors and is added to the Consensus Calendar, but still did not get a floor vote.

2025: Reintroduced as H.R. 2102 and S. 1032 and eventually drew more than 330 House cosponsors and 79 in the Senate.

May 21, 2026: Takano files a discharge petition, H.R. 1247, to force a vote.

June 10, 2026: Republican leaders introduce the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a package that folds in a lesser version of the Star Act alongside dozens of other provisions. Takano, Ruiz, and major veterans organizations including Disabled American Veterans oppose it over its funding structure and the cuts and caps it carries.

Sept. 15, 2026: Rep. Nancy Mace (R-SC) provides the 218th signature.

Nov. 12, 2026: The House passes the Major Richard Star Act.

The Major Richard Star Act is backed by a broad coalition of veterans and military service organizations, including Veterans of Foreign Wars, Disabled American Veterans, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Jewish War Veterans, Marine Corps League, Reserve Organization of America, Student Veterans of America, Wounded Warrior Project, Veterans Justice Alliance, The American Legion, Military Officers Association of America, Vietnam Veterans of America, National Guard Association of the United States, Blue Star Families, Fleet Reserve Association, Elizabeth Dole Foundation, Team Rubicon, Blinded Veterans Association, Non Commissioned Officers Association, National Military Family Association, Air Force Sergeants Association, Association of the U.S. Army, U.S. Army Warrant Officers Association, Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors, National Defense Committee, Mission Roll Call, and dozens of other veterans service and advocacy organizations.

The Senate companion, S. 1032, led by Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), awaits action.

title: House, Senate Ranking Members Lead Over 200 Democrats in Fight to Overturn Trump Admin’s VA Abortion Ban
text:
WASHINGTON – House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39), joined by Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Sen. Patty Murray (D-WA), and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), led more than 200 House and Senate Democrats in filing an amicus brief in Minority Veterans of America v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration’s abortion ban at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The lawsuit, pending before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, seeks to overturn VA’s ban on abortion care and counseling. In the brief, the lawmakers argue the Trump administration’s 2025 policy banning abortion counseling and abortion care in almost all cases rests on a flawed legal premise.

“VA’s Final Rule rests on a faulty interpretation of federal law that has significant negative consequences for our nation’s veterans. The issues presented in this case potentially reach roughly 462,000 women veterans of reproductive age who are enrolled in VA healthcare, along with an estimated 112,000 women of reproductive age enrolled in the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA),” the members wrote.

The members continued, “For them, the Final Rule means a VA physician is prohibited from discussing the full range of a patient’s options during a pregnancy, prohibited from providing the full range of healthcare available to pregnant women, and is prohibited from intervening when a pregnancy threatens the patient’s health or is the result of rape or incest.”

VA’s abortion ban, implemented by the Trump administration in 2025, prohibits abortion counseling and care for veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries, even in cases of rape, incest, or if a veteran’s health is endangered. The lawmakers argue in the brief that VA’s erroneous interpretation of federal law means these women now cannot receive abortion care or counseling even in the most harrowing circumstances. They also argue the Veterans’ Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 1996 allows VA to provide any medical services the Secretary “determines to be needed,” and that the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, which VA used to justify its abortion ban, does not restrict the Secretary’s authority to add abortion care to its medical benefits package.

In the House, the brief was signed by 165 Democratic U.S. Representatives. In the Senate, it was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators.

A Congressional Review Act (CRA) resolution is an oversight tool Congress can use to overturn final rules issued by federal agencies with a simple majority vote. The CRA resolution to overturn the Trump administration’s policy ending abortion counseling entirely and abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment did not receive a vote in the House, but it garnered the support of 155 Democratic cosponsors. In March, all present Democratic Senators voted in support of Senator Blumenthal’s version of the resolution. The vote failed 48-50 due to lack of adequate Republican support, leaving VA’s abortion ban in place.

In September 2022, VA began to offer abortion counseling to all pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries, and abortion care in cases of rape, incest, or life or health endangerment of the veteran or CHAMPVA beneficiary. This was in response to the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization ruling, which created urgent risks to the lives and health of pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries in states that banned or otherwise severely restricted access to abortion. VA’s dangerous abortion ban means that veterans nationwide now face those same risks.

More than 462,000 veterans of reproductive age are enrolled in VA healthcare, and more than 112,000 women of reproductive age are enrolled in CHAMPVA. More than half of these women live in states that have enacted abortion bans or restrictions.

The amicus brief can be read in full here.

title: Neal, Wyden Begin to Investigate Trump Administration’s Scheme to Take Cut of Nvidia AI Chip Sales to Chinese Companies

committee.name: House Committee on Ways and Means

text:
WASHINGTON, DC— Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) today demanded the Trump Administration retain all records relating to its scheme to allow—and take a cut of—the sale of advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies with links to the Chinese government and military, using a trade law intended to protect U.S. national security.

Neal and Wyden are beginning to investigate amid reports that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang engaged in a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, leading to Huang’s resignation on Thursday. According to press reports, both Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Donald Trump were briefed about Huang’s relationship, but granted approval to export advanced AI chips to China.

“The Trump Administration’s ostensible attempt to mask an unconstitutional export tax as a national security tariff action—benefitting both Nvidia and the Chinese government—raises serious concerns within our Committees’ jurisdiction over matters relating to taxation and tariffs,” Neal and Wyden wrote. “Congress wrote Section 232 to give the President a tool to take action against imports he has determined to pose a national security threat; Trump’s use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining U.S. national security and putting Americans at risk.”

Under the scheme, Nvidia chips manufactured in Taiwan could be sold to Chinese companies if they were first imported into the United States for a security review, which would require payment of a 25% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, a trade law designed to address imports that threaten national security. Then the Commerce Department would grant Nvidia an export license to sell the chips to Chinese companies.

According to reports, the Commerce Department suspended its investigation into suspected smuggling into China of certain Nvidia chips following outreach from the company. Nvidia and Huang donated at least $26 million to Trump’s pet projects.

Neal and Wyden requested the Commerce Department preserve all records related to:

The Commerce Department’s investigation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 into imports of semiconductors and resulting actions, including tariffs;

The Department’s consideration and approval of export license applications submitted by Nvidia; and

The Department’s communications with and regarding Nvidia, Jensen Huang, or any of their agents or representatives.
