title: Graves and Larsen Statements on the Passing of NBAA’s Ed Bolen

committee.name: House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

text:
Washington, DC – Statements of Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chairman Sam Graves (R-MO) and Ranking Member Rick Larsen (D-WA) on the passing of National Business Aviation Association (NBAA) President and CEO Ed Bolen:

Graves: “The aviation world yesterday lost a tremendous advocate in Ed Bolen. For decades, Ed’s voice and expertise were invaluable to this industry, leaders in both Houses of Congress, and presidents of both parties in the development of U.S. aviation policy – especially all policies important to the general aviation community. I am personally thankful for Ed’s thoughtful input on many of the aviation issues and legislation that came out of our committee over the years. I will truly miss Ed, who was a fellow pilot from the Midwest and a good friend, and I extend my deepest condolences to all of his family and friends.”

Larsen: “I offer my deepest condolences to the Bolen family after the tragic loss of Ed Bolen yesterday. Ed was a tireless and enthusiastic advocate for American aviation and his positive impact on the industry will not be forgotten. He will be remembered fondly by the entire aviation community.”

title: Chairman Scott, Bipartisan Senators Urge HHS to Expand Incentives for American-Made Essential Medicines
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging Chairman Rick Scott joined U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn, and a bipartisan group of senators in urging the Trump administration to boost federal policy incentives for hospitals to buy and use American-made essential medicines over foreign competitors.

In a letter to Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert Kennedy Jr. and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the senators called the proposal a critical first step and asked the agencies to go further in the final rule by:

Covering the entire FDA Essential Medicines List;

Letting providers choose the payment that fits their purchasing cycles; and

Paying higher incentives for finished drugs made in America with U.S.-made advice ingredients and key starting materials.

The senators highlighted the dangers of overreliance on China and India for pharmaceuticals, resulting in both national security threats and drug shortages – including shortages of chemotherapy drugs that forced some providers to ration treatment.

The senators wrote, “To secure health care infrastructure for the benefit of national security, patients, and providers, HHS should implement clear reimbursement incentives for utilizing U.S.-made essential drugs. This strategy activates existing, untapped domestic manufacturing capabilities and incentivizes fresh capital investment in American production, further protecting patient care from the dual threats of chronic drug shortages and global supply chain disruptions.”

U.S. Senators Adam Schiff, Ted Budd, and Andy Kim also signed the letter.

BACKGROUND:

In October 2025, Senate Aging Committee Chairman Scott and Ranking Member Gillibrand released an investigative report titled “Protecting Seniors’ Access to Essential Medications: Securing the Foreign Generic Pharmaceutical Supply Chain.” The report focused on America’s dangerous overreliance on foreign-made generic drugs, which are largely imported from China. Chairman Scott has been a leading advocate for American drug supply chain transparency and reform.

The Consumer Labeling for Enhanced API Reporting and Legitimate Accountability for Base Entity Listings (CLEAR LABELS) Act, introduced by Chairman Scott and Ranking Member Gillibrand in January 2026, addresses these concerns by adding country of origin labeling requirements to the U.S.’s prescription drug supply chain.

Chairman Scott previously sent a letter to Administrator Oz urging CMS to buy American-made medical devices and pharmaceutical drugs, rather than Communist Chinese products that can be used to surveil and harm Americans. The Chairman has been the Senate’s leading advocate that no federal funding should be used to purchase devices or pharmaceuticals made in China when domestic supply is available.

Read the letter HERE or below.

Dear Administrator Oz and Secretary Kennedy:

We write today highlighting the need to reduce our country’s over-reliance on foreign drug manufacturing, including through a proposed Medicare payment incentive for hospitals and clinics that use domestically manufactured essential medicines.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) released a proposal in the FY 2027 Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) proposed rule outlining potential approaches to incentivize hospitals to procure domestically manufactured essential medicines. We appreciate that CMS’s proposal recognizes how Medicare payment policy can align hospital purchasing decisions to better support domestic medical manufacturing and supply chain resiliency. This is a critical first step, and we encourage you to strengthen this proposal with additional policy levers, outlined below.

In recent years, numerous shortages of essential medicines have demonstrated that vulnerabilities within our pharmaceutical supply chain carry immediate clinical consequences, leaving patients and providers with limited options for essential generics and acute-care medications. For example, shortages of essential generic chemotherapy agents have demonstrated the fragility of pharmaceutical supply chains and their direct impact on patient care, forcing providers in some areas to ration treatment.

To mitigate our strategic dependence on foreign manufacturing hubs like India and China and protect patients from potentially life-threatening care disruptions, we urge the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to utilize targeted reimbursement incentives for health care facilities like those proposed in the FY 2027 OPPS proposed rule. This approach will help drive purchasing toward high-quality domestic facilities under U.S. regulatory jurisdiction, effectively tap into existing domestic production capabilities, and clearly communicate the federal commitment to strengthening onshore pharmaceutical manufacturing.

As you move toward final rulemaking on this proposal, we respectfully urge you to consider the following:

Expand the Incentive to Cover the Entire Essential Medicines List (EML): The Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) Essential Medicines List identifies medicines that are critical to national health care infrastructure and supply chain resiliency. Each of the medications on the EML represents a vital resource for health care providers and therefore must be available in adequate amounts to satisfy the health care needs of a population. Limiting the incentive to only a subset of the EML would distort purchasing decisions and leave clinically important medicines without meaningful support.

Predictable, Timely, and Adequate Payments: CMS outlined several potential payment methodologies in the proposal. Both methodologies would reflect providers’ use of qualifying products. We encourage CMS to permit health care providers to elect whichever payment methodology is easier for its specific institutional needs in order to ensure a streamlined payment mechanism that permits providers to receive these funds in a predictable manner that aligns with their purchasing cycles.

U.S.-Manufactured Pharmaceutical Products, including U.S. Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) and Key Starting Materials (KSM): Bolstering U.S.-made pharmaceutical products, including U.S.-made API and KSM, is vitally important to the resiliency of American supply chains. Therefore, a payment incentive should recognize and reward domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing, with incentives for use of finished-dose products manufactured in the United States using Trade Agreement Act (TAA)-compliant API and higher incentives for US-manufactured finished doses that also use domestic API and KSM.

To secure health care infrastructure for the benefit of national security, patients, and providers, HHS should implement clear reimbursement incentives for utilizing U.S.-made essential drugs. This strategy activates existing, untapped domestic manufacturing capabilities and incentivizes fresh capital investment in American production, further protecting patient care from the dual threats of chronic drug shortages and global supply chain disruptions.

Thank you for your leadership and consideration. We stand ready to work with you to bolster the resilience of the American health care system.

###

title: Warren Statement on Reporting on EXIM’s Backing Off Investments in Kazakh Mining Project Backed by Trump Sons

committee.name: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, released the following statement on reports that US government lenders, including the Export-Import Bank (EXIM), are planning to deny $1.6 billion in financing for a Kazakh mining project in which President Donald Trump’s sons are investors:

“This reporting, coupled with EXIM's troubling lack of transparency, raises serious questions as Republican and Democratic members of the Banking Committee work to reauthorize the Bank's charter. EXIM's leadership has failed to establish clear safeguards to ensure the Bank never becomes another vehicle for corruption benefiting President Trump and his family. It's time for Congress to act to ensure the bank serves our businesses and our economy, not the Trump family’s bottom line.”

Ranking Member Warren has repeatedly pressed EXIM leadership for answers about potential corruption, conflicts of interest, and the misuse of taxpayer funds. Warren has warned that Congress must ensure strong safeguards against corruption and conflicts of interest as lawmakers work to reauthorize the Bank's charter.

In June, Warren pressed EXIM President and Chairman John Jovanovic to provide complete responses to questions about the Bank's ethics safeguards, including whether Trump family-linked entities had sought or received EXIM financing.

In July, Warren probed EXIM and other federal agencies over reports that a Trump family-backed Kazakhstan mining venture was seeking nearly $2 billion in federal assistance, including up to $900 million from EXIM.

title: AFL-CIO and Nation’s Largest Building Trades Endorse Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
Broad coalition of national and local labor organizations representing hundreds of thousands of skilled workers supports legislation projected to create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs

WASHINGTON — The AFL-CIO has endorsed U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), joining a broad coalition of national and local labor organizations representing the skilled workers who build, operate, and maintain America’s energy infrastructure.

The AFL-CIO’s endorsement adds to growing support from across organized labor, including the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW), International Association of Iron Workers, International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers (SMART), International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, International Brotherhood of Teamsters,International Union of Operating Engineers (IUOE), Laborers’ International Union of North America (LIUNA), North America’s Building Trades Unions (NABTU), United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters, Pipeliners Local 798, and the New Mexico Building and Construction Trades Council. These organizations represent the electricians, ironworkers, sheet metal workers, boilermakers, Teamsters, operating engineers, laborers, plumbers, pipefitters, and other skilled tradespeople who will build the next generation of America’s energy infrastructure.

The labor support comes as an independent analysis from Employ America estimates that BAAJA will create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs through 2040 by making it easier to build and maintain new energy infrastructure, including wind, solar, battery storage, and transmission projects.

BAAJA will lower energy costs for working families, provide greater certainty for energy infrastructure projects, and help ensure American workers are on the job building the infrastructure our country needs.

Independent analyses find that BAAJA will:

Create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs through 2040;

Require data centers to pay for increased grid and energy costs they create, estimated at $55 billion over the next 10 years;

Save $19 billion in residential electricity bills over the next 14 years;

Nearly double the amount of solar and wind that can connect to the grid; and

Avoid 1.5 gigatons of CO₂ emissions, the equivalent of taking 39 coal plants offline for a decade.

BAAJA will lower energy costs for working families, provide greater certainty for energy infrastructure projects, and help ensure American workers are on the job building the infrastructure our country needs.

title: “Democrats, Take the Deal” — New York Times and Washington Post Editorial Boards Endorse Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act

committee.name: Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

text:
WASHINGTON — The editorial boards of The New York Times and The Washington Post have endorsed U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.) Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), recognizing the legislation as a significant opportunity to lower energy costs, accelerate the development of clean energy, modernize the nation’s energy infrastructure, create good-paying jobs, reduce emissions, and hold data centers accountable.

Today, The New York Times endorsed the legislation, highlighting its potential to deliver lower electricity costs and reduce emissions while advancing long-overdue permitting reform: “The bill’s supporters recognize that it is merely a first step toward a much broader agenda to reduce carbon emissions and lower energy costs. But anyone who cares about climate change should cheer this bill. And a party that just won an election on affordability should not pass up a chance to start delivering immediately.”

In its November 9 editorial, The Washington Post Editorial Board called the legislation “a major step toward historic permitting reform,” writing that making it easier to build energy infrastructure “would greatly boost” wind and solar industries. The board also noted that the legislation is projected to reduce carbon emissions and highlighted the support it has received from climate organizations including the Environmental Defense Fund, Evergreen Action, and Citizens’ Climate Lobby.

The endorsements come as a growing body of independent research and analysis reinforces the legislation’s benefits for American families, workers, and the clean energy industry.

New independent polling shows overwhelming public support for BAAJA, even after voters hear opposition arguments.

A new national poll from Third Way found that 79% of voters support BAAJA, with 66% continuing to support the legislation even after hearing arguments against it. Support cuts across party lines, with voters responding particularly strongly to provisions that lower electricity bills, create jobs, improve critical infrastructure, and ensure data centers pay their fair share.

Independent analyses demonstrate BAAJA will deliver significant savings for American families and hold data centers accountable.

Grid Strategies estimates that BAAJA will require data centers to pay approximately $55 billion in transmission costs over the next decade — $35 billion more than they would pay under current policy — helping protect other electricity customers from shouldering the costs of data center expansion.

Analysis from the Center for Climate and Energy Solutions and Greenline Insights projects that BAAJA could save households $19 billion on electricity bills through 2040.

The Corporate Energy Buyers Association has also outlined how the legislation will help reduce electricity costs for American consumers and businesses.

Independent research shows BAAJA will accelerate clean energy development and significantly reduce emissions.

Columbia University’s Center on Global Energy Policy developed an analysis comparing how BAAJA would affect permitting timelines for different types of energy projects.

The Solar Energy Industries Association estimates that BAAJA would enable solar and wind to supply 37.4% of U.S. electricity generation by 2035, compared to 19.6% under current permitting conditions. Its analysis also projects approximately 20% lower power-sector carbon emissions, 51% less net new gas capacity, and $6 billion in lower cumulative electricity costs between 2028 and 2035.

Rhodium Group has independently analyzed the legislation’s impacts on emissions and the broader U.S. energy system.

The Corporate Energy Buyers Association has also detailed the legislation’s potential to increase clean energy generation and reduce emissions.

BAAJA will create over one hundred thousand good-paying American jobs.

A new analysis from Employ America estimates that BAAJA could create up to 105,600 industrial jobs through 2040. Those jobs would come from building and maintaining new wind, solar, battery, and transmission infrastructure, as well as reducing energy costs for American manufacturers.

The legislation has also been endorsed by a broad coalition of labor, energy, and business stakeholders.

The full text of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is available here.

title: Wyden and Alsobrooks Seek Evidence of RFK Jr. Lies from Children’s Health Defense
text:

Washington, D.C. – Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and Senator Angela Alsobrooks, D-Md., opened an investigation into evidence that Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., lied to Congress about his travel to Samoa prior to a measles outbreak that killed 83 Samoans, mostly children.

“We are beginning an investigation into evidence that Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. unlawfully lied to Congress on multiple occasions,” the senators wrote. “In Samoa and in the United States, unvaccinated children have died tragic and preventable deaths during measles outbreaks. I also intend to hold Secretary Kennedy accountable for any false statements made to Congress, a crime that undermines the Senate’s ability to fulfill its constitutional duties.”

During his confirmation hearing, Robert Kennedy told senators that his 2019 trip to Samoa had “nothing to do with vaccines.” However, there is a growing body of evidence that this statement was patently false. title: Wyden and Neal Begin to Investigate Administration Scheme to Take Cut of Nvidia AI Chip Sales to Chinese Companies; Trump and Commerce Department Reportedly Ignored Warnings About Former CEO’s Relationship with Alleged Chinese Spy
text:
Top Democrats on House and Senate Trade Committees Request Commerce Department Retain All Relevant Records Regarding Nvidia Chip Sale Decisions

Read the full letter here

Washington, D.C. – Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and House Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal, D-Mass., today demanded the Trump Administration retain all records relating to its scheme to allow—and take a cut of—the sale of advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies with links to the Chinese government and military, using a trade law intended to protect U.S. national security.

Wyden and Neal launched their investigation amid reports that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang engaged in a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, leading to Huang’s resignation on Thursday. According to press reports, both Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Donald Trump were briefed about Huang’s relationship, but granted approval to export advanced AI chips to China.

“The Trump Administration’s ostensible attempt to mask an unconstitutional export tax as a national security tariff action—benefitting both Nvidia and the Chinese government—raises serious concerns within our Committees’ jurisdiction over matters relating to taxation and tariffs,” Wyden and Neal wrote. “Congress wrote Section 232 to give the President a tool to take action against imports he has determined to pose a national security threat; Trump’s use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining U.S. national security and putting Americans at risk.”

Under the scheme, Nvidia chips manufactured in Taiwan could be sold to Chinese companies if they were first imported into the United States for a security review, which would require payment of a 25% tariff under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962, a trade law designed to address imports that threaten national security. Then the Commerce Department would grant Nvidia an export license to sell the chips to Chinese companies.

According to reports, the Commerce Department suspended its investigation into suspected smuggling into China of certain Nvidia chips following outreach from the company. Nvidia and Huang donated at least $26 million to Trump’s pet projects.

Wyden and Neal requested the Commerce Department preserve all records related to:

the Commerce Department’s investigation under Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act of 1962 into imports of semiconductors and resulting actions, including tariffs;

The Department’s consideration and approval of export license applications submitted by Nvidia; and

the Department’s communications with and regarding Nvidia, Jensen Huang, or any of their agents or representatives.

title: Wyden and Pallone Call on Trump Administration to Immediately Delay Implementation of Medicaid Paperwork Requirements
text:
Washington, D.C. – Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and House Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr., D-N.J., wrote to Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz asking the Trump Administration to immediately delay implementation of the Medicaid paperwork reporting requirements set to go into effect on January 1, 2027.

“CMS must immediately exercise its statutory authority and available enforcement discretion to give states additional time to implement work reporting requirements and protect eligible beneficiaries from losing coverage,” Wyden and Pallone wrote to Administrator Oz. “It is clear that CMS must permit all states, consistent with applicable law, to delay denials and terminations of coverage attributable to work reporting requirements until their eligibility systems, verification processes, and beneficiary protections have been fully implemented and tested.”

The letter comes amid mounting uncertainty for states just weeks before the implementation deadline. Last month, a federal court ruled CMS unlawfully narrowed the law’s exemption for medically frail individuals, using a standard so restrictive that even a cancer diagnosis might not qualify. Rather than accept the ruling, Administrator Oz stated the Trump Administration will appeal the decision, leaving states without a final answer on a core policy before the paperwork requirements go live. Wyden and Pallone argued that CMS’ actions and continued legal challenges make it even harder for states to meet an already impossible timeline and urged CMS to grant good faith exemptions to every state that requests one.

The lawmakers also raised alarm that CMS leadership is actively discouraging states from seeking the good faith exemptions Congress built into the law, despite knowing many states are still not ready to implement the new requirements. Pallone and Wyden called on CMS to publicly release state readiness assessments, exemption requests and decisions, and, once requirements take effect, state-level data on coverage denials and terminations.

“Repealing the devastating Medicaid cuts enacted under H.R. 1, including work reporting requirements, will be a top priority of Democrats in the 120th Congress. Until Congress acts, however, CMS has a responsibility to carry out the law as Congress established it, and to ensure that implementation does not unnecessarily jeopardize coverage for eligible beneficiaries,” the Democratic Committee leaders continued. “CMS must recognize these challenges and exercise the authority Congress provided to give states the time and flexibility they need. Failing to permit states to delay implementation despite known operational deficiencies will worsen preventable coverage losses for which Congressional Democrats will hold the Trump Administration accountable.”

Read the full letter here.

title: Shaheen, Tillis Condemn Renewed Restrictions on Ukraine’s Satellite Communications, Pledge Further Congressional Oversight
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Thom Tillis (R-NC) released the following statement after Ukrainian officials reported renewed restrictions on Starshield, the military communications service that relies on SpaceX’s Starlink network:

“It is outrageous that, just weeks after service was restored, Ukrainian officials are once again reporting restrictions on Starshield, crippling Ukraine’s ability to intercept Russian drones across the front line. At a time when the Trump Administration claims to be working toward peace, it is impossible to understand how undermining Ukraine’s ability to defend itself gets us closer to that goal. With Putin continuing to target Ukrainian civilians and energy infrastructure ahead of winter, these restrictions put Ukrainian lives and American personnel in Ukraine at risk.

“Ukraine’s military has determined that these disruptions are systematic restrictions, and SpaceX admitted last month that it limited Ukraine’s service. SpaceX has yet to offer any explanation for these latest disruptions. These repeated restrictions raise further dire questions about why Ukraine is being deliberately deprived of the capabilities it needs to defend itself.

“The Trump Administration and SpaceX must restore these capabilities immediately. Ukraine is negotiating in good faith to end this war. Russia has shown no such good faith. While President Trump’s envoys travel to Moscow, Putin continues attacking innocent civilians, including bombing a center in Kremenchuk serving children with special needs. Just last week, Putin killed 55 civilians as they were attempting to get humanitarian aid.

“Congress must determine who ordered or approved these disruptions and hold those responsible accountable. The Pentagon and SpaceX must preserve all records, turn over the contracts and communications that Congress needs to establish the facts and put safeguards in place so this never happens again. A just and lasting peace requires pressure on Putin, not cutting off Ukraine’s defenses.”

title: Grassley-Durbin Bankruptcy Legislation Becomes Law, Benefiting American Small Businesses and Families
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Ranking Member Dick Durbin’s (D-Ill.) Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act has become law. The bipartisan legislation supports American small businesses and families by reinstating modern debt limits for Subchapter V and Chapter 13 bankruptcy, restoring access to critical reorganization tools.

“The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act is now the law of the land, ensuring our nation’s bankruptcy code works for Americans, not against them,” Grassley said. “By restoring modern debt limits and eliminating barriers to reorganization, this bipartisan bill provides American small businesses and families the tools they need to regain their financial footing. I thank Senator Durbin for his partnership in getting our bill across the finish line, as well as my colleagues in the Senate and House of Representatives for their support.”

“Bankruptcy is often a painful last resort for small business owners. This bill restores a quicker and cheaper pathway for entrepreneurs to settle debts, keep the lights on, and keep serving their neighbors. It also expands eligibility for Chapter 13 bankruptcy to help more families manage rising costs, stay in their homes, and get back on their feet. Following unanimous passage in the Senate and House, I’m thrilled the President signed our bipartisan bill into law,” Durbin said.

The bipartisan legislation is cosponsored by Sens. John Cornyn (R-Texas), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Chris Coons (D-Del.).

Bill text can be found HERE.

Background:

The Grassley-Whitehouse Small Business Reorganization Act, signed into law in 2019, established Subchapter V within Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code. The bipartisan legislation streamlined the bankruptcy process, reduced procedural burdens on small business owners and lowered filing costs. Legislation signed into law in 2020 allowed more small businesses to qualify for these procedures by increasing the upper debt limit for Subchapter V to $7.5 million.

In 2022, the Grassley-Whitehouse Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment and Technical Corrections Act was signed into law, extending the $7.5 million debt limit for small businesses filing under Subchapter V and establishing a new debt limit of $2.75 million for individuals and families filing under Chapter 13. However, when the Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment and Technical Corrections Act expired in 2024, the debt thresholds for both programs reverted to lower levels.

The Grassley-Durbin Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act permanently restores the Subchapter V debt limit to $7.5 million and the Chapter 13 debt limit to $2.75 million.

title: Grassley, Johnson Seek Declassification of All Crossfire Hurricane Records to Secure Lasting Transparency
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations Chairman Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) are urging President Donald Trump to declassify all government records related to the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) weaponized Crossfire Hurricane investigation.

Trump signed an Executive Order in March 2025 approving the declassification of Crossfire Hurricane materials. Yet, key governments emails, hundreds of transcripts from Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Inspector General interviews and a 400-page DOJ Inspection Division investigation report remain classified.

“We appreciate your strong efforts to bring transparency and accountability to Crossfire Hurricane and its related investigations. For approximately a decade, we’ve investigated Crossfire Hurricane and have sought possession of a wide array of government records to expose the facts and evidence once hidden from the American public. The more we’ve investigated the matter, the more information has come to light exposing the political rot that infected that operation from the get-go,” the senators wrote.

“Your administration possesses a treasure trove of records that prove out weaponization against Republicans, including you and your family, which we’ve investigated for many years. These records need to see the light of day, consistent with your declassification Executive Order and the overriding public interest,” the senators concluded.

Read the full letter HERE and below.

November 10, 2026

VIA ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION

The Honorable Donald J. Trump

President of the United States

The White House

Dear President Trump:

We appreciate your strong efforts to bring transparency and accountability to Crossfire Hurricane and its related investigations. For approximately a decade, we’ve investigated Crossfire Hurricane and have sought possession of a wide array of government records to expose the facts and evidence once hidden from the American public. The more we’ve investigated the matter, the more information has come to light exposing the political rot that infected that operation from the get-go. We write today about records that have yet to be declassified that should be based upon your declassification Executive Order and for public transparency.

First, on August 17, 2026, we wrote to the DOJ, FBI, and ODNI concerning a December 2019 email from Tony Riedlinger, then an FBI Section Chief, to FBI Supervisory Special Agent Joe Pientka that contained a description as well as an attached document. The email and attachment, when read together, appear to corroborate existing public evidence that you were the target of a political hit and the basis of evidence that would lead a person to reasonably make that conclusion appears to have been known to the DOJ and FBI for some time. Yet, those agencies proceeded with weaponized investigations again you.

We’ve requested that the DOJ, FBI, and ODNI declassify the email and attachment to the fullest extent possible under the law, but that has yet to be done.

Second, the DOJ has produced an approximately 400-page DOJ Inspection Division investigation report related to Crossfire Hurricane but it too is classified. This report provides additional context separate from the Justice Department’s Inspector General report on Crossfire Hurricane, including additional interviews with personnel involved in Crossfire Hurricane. The report also provides additional context about the questionable beginnings of Crossfire Hurricane that ought to be made known to the American people. Even though the approximately 400-page report was produced to our SCIF in classified form, it still contains redactions. After all these years of weaponization in Crossfire Hurricane, that document should be declassified for the public.

Finally, since 2023, we’ve requested from the Justice Department Inspector General the full set of the transcripts that office created as part of its investigation titled “Review of Four FISA Applications and Other Aspects of the FBI’s Crossfire Hurricane Investigation.” The Inspector General at that time failed to produce those records. On March 17, 2025, we wrote to DOJ and FBI requesting that they work with the DOJ Office of the Inspector General to produce unredacted transcripts of interviews connected to that report. It is our understanding that during its review, the DOJ OIG interviewed more than 170 individuals and of those, 165 interviews were transcribed. To date, we have received 58 transcripts with redactions, two memoranda of investigation summarizing follow-up interactions after initial interviews, and one document labeled a memorandum of record also summarizing an interaction after an initial interview. The rest of the transcripts have yet to be produced with some still classified. We appreciate the new Inspector General and current DOJ and FBI leadership working to produce transcripts that previous leadership failed to produce. However, it’s been years, and these records have taken too long to reach Congress and the public. We urge your administration to produce the rest in short order and without unnecessary redactions.

Your administration possesses a treasure trove of records that prove out weaponization against Republicans, including you and your family, which we’ve investigated for many years. These records need to see the light of day consistent with your declassification Executive Order and the overriding public interest.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

title:
Blumenthal, Murray, Schumer, Takano Lead More Than 200 Democrats in Fight to Overturn the Trump Admin's Draconian Abortion Ban at VA
More than 200 Senate and House Democrats filed an amicus brief challenging the Trump VA’s ban on abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), and House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (D-CA) led more than 200 Senate and House Democrats in filing an amicus brief to Minority Veterans of America v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s abortion ban at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The lawsuit, pending before the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, seeks to overturn VA’s ban on abortion care and counseling. In the brief, the lawmakers argue the Trump Administration’s 2025 policy banning abortion counseling and abortion care in almost all cases rests on a flawed legal premise.

“VA’s Final Rule rests on a faulty interpretation of federal law that has significant negative consequences for our nation’s veterans. The issues presented in this case potentially reach roughly 462,000 women veterans of reproductive age who are enrolled in VA health care, along with an estimated 112,000 women of reproductive age enrolled in the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA),” the members wrote.

The members continued, “For them, the Final Rule means a VA physician is prohibited from discussing the full range of a patient’s options during a pregnancy, prohibited from providing the full range of health care available to pregnant women, and is prohibited from intervening when a pregnancy threatens the patient’s health or is the result of rape or incest.”

VA’s abortion ban, implemented by the Trump Administration in 2025, prohibits abortion counseling and care for veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries—even in cases of rape, incest, or if a veteran’s health is endangered. The lawmakers argue in the brief that VA’s erroneous interpretation of federal law means these women now cannot receive abortion care or counseling even in the most harrowing circumstances. They also argue the Veterans’ Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 1996 allows VA to provide any medical services the Secretary “determines to be needed” and that the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, which VA used to justify its abortion ban, does not restrict the Secretary’s authority to add abortion care to its medical benefits package.

In the Senate, the amicus brief was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators. In the House, the brief was signed by 165 Democratic U.S. Representatives.

In March, all present Democratic Senators voted in support of Senator Blumenthal’s Congressional Review Act (CRA) resolution to overturn the Trump Administration’s policy ending abortion counseling entirely and abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment. A CRA resolution is an oversight tool Congress can use to overturn final rules issued by federal agencies with a simple majority vote. The vote failed 48-50 due to lack of adequate Republican support, leaving VA’s abortion ban in place. While the CRA resolution did not receive a vote in the House, it garnered the support of 155 Democratic cosponsors.

In September 2022, VA began to offer abortion counseling to all pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries, and abortion care in cases of rape, incest, or life or health endangerment of the veteran or CHAMPVA beneficiary. This was in response to the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization ruling, which created urgent risks to the lives and health of pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries in states that banned or otherwise severely restricted access to abortion. VA’s dangerous abortion ban means that veterans nationwide now face those same risks.

More than 462,000 veterans of reproductive age are enrolled in VA health care, and more than 112,000 women of reproductive age are enrolled in CHAMPVA. More than half of these women live in states that have enacted abortion bans or restrictions.

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Outlines Plans to Empower Committee Democrats and Strengthen Committee Collaboration in the 120th Congress
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the following statement after convening a strategy meeting with Committee Democrats to discuss legislative priorities, strengthen collaboration, and chart a path forward for the 120th Congress.

“Following our historic Democratic victory, we have an extraordinary opportunity to deliver meaningful change for the American people. One of the greatest strengths of the House Financial Services Committee is the wealth of experience, expertise, and perspectives our Members bring from communities across the country. Each Member understands the unique challenges facing their constituents, and those perspectives are essential to shaping a Committee that delivers meaningful results for the American people.

“That is why I brought Committee Democrats together to hear directly from my colleagues about how we can strengthen our work, empower our Members, and build on our record of delivering tangible results. Our discussion was productive, candid, and focused on how we can make this Committee even more effective.

“Following these conversations, and informed by the recommendations of my colleagues, including a list of thoughtful and reasonable recommendations compiled by Ranking Member Bill Foster, I intend to build on our Committee's strong foundation by taking several steps under my leadership as Chairwoman in the 120th Congress to ensure we are working together as effectively as possible to advance our legislative and oversight agenda, including:

Building on Committee Collaboration: Incorporate Subcommittee Chair staff into relevant Committee planning discussions to foster collaboration, support coordination, and advance shared legislative and oversight priorities.

Subcommittee Chairs and Members to be Informed Ahead of Oversight Actions: Continue working closely with Members on key oversight initiatives, including discussions involving subpoenas where appropriate, to advance a strong, unified oversight agenda.

Subcommittee Chairs to Choose the Topics for 50% of their Subcommittee Hearings, in Consultation with the Chair: Further incorporate Subcommittee Chairs' expertise and recommendations into hearing priorities as part of the Chairwoman's broader Committee agenda.

Subcommittee Chairs to Choose at Least One Witness for Each Subcommittee Hearing: Continue drawing on recommendations from Subcommittee Chairs to identify knowledgeable witnesses who can strengthen hearings and advance the Committee's priorities.

Consult Subcommittee Chairs on Markup Agenda and Floor Votes: Build on existing collaboration with Subcommittee Chairs on markups, legislative priorities, and floor strategy to move forward an ambitious agenda under the Chairwoman's leadership.

Chairwoman Waters to Aid Vulnerable Democratic Members and Shepherd Their Legislative Priorities Through Committee: Continue working with Members, including a special focus on those representing competitive districts, to elevate their legislative priorities and identify opportunities to deliver results for their constituents.

Ensuring Resources to Deliver Success: Provide Subcommittee Chairs with ample resources to deliver on behalf of the Committee and the American people, including resources to recruit and retain top talent.

“I thank my Democratic colleagues, including Ranking Member Foster, for their recommendations that reflect their collective experience and ideas, and I am committed to adopting them and putting them into action.

“As we look ahead to the 120th Congress, I am excited about what we can accomplish together. From making housing more affordable and protecting consumers from predatory financial practices to holding Wall Street accountable and ensuring our financial system works for everyone, we have important work ahead of us. I intend to build on our successes, empower our Members to deliver for their constituents, and lead a Committee that is not afraid to take on the toughest challenges facing the American people. We have a lot of work to do, and I am ready to get it done.”

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Puts Trump Administration on Notice, Demands Preservation of Federal Records Ahead of Democratic Majority
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Financial Services Committee, sent formal preservation notices to 23 federal agencies and offices directing officials to preserve documents and communications dating back to January 20, 2025, as House Democrats prepare to reclaim the majority in the 120th Congress.

The notices mark an important step in preparing the Committee to conduct rigorous oversight of the Trump Administration's actions affecting the safety, soundness, and security of America's financial system, including the institutions that operate in and depend upon it as well as the government entities that support and defend it.

The notices, sent to 23 federal agencies and offices, are intended to safeguard records relating to the Administration's actions and decisions affecting the nation's financial system and ensure that the Committee is prepared to exercise its full oversight authority under Democratic leadership.

Recipients include: the U.S. Department of the Treasury, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the National Credit Union Administration, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, the U.S. Department of Justice, Criminal Division, the Office of Management and Budget, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Federal Housing Finance Agency, the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, the Defense Production Act Office, the Export-Import Bank of the United States, the Minority Business Development Agency, the National Economic Council, the Super Intelligence Task Force, the Bureau of Engraving and Printing, and the U.S. Mint.

Specifically, the preservation notices direct federal agencies to:

Preserve all responsive records dating back to January 20, 2025, including newly created documents and communications.

Prevent the destruction, modification, removal, or transfer of records, including emails, text messages, memoranda, reports, recordings, and other electronic communications.

Ensure records remain accessible, including those held by current or former employees, contractors, representatives, or third parties within the agencies' control.

Account for missing or unavailable documents, including explanations of the circumstances surrounding their disappearance, destruction, or transfer.

Provide written certification by December 11, 2026, confirming compliance with the preservation requirements.

The notices represent an early step in Waters' preparations to lead the House Financial Services Committee in the 120th Congress and lay the groundwork for robust oversight of the Trump Administration's actions affecting consumers, financial institutions, housing, and the broader economy.

title: @EdWorkforceCmte Holds North Carolina Field Hearing on Workers' Rights

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
Today, Rep. Mark Harris (R-NC) delivered the following statement, as prepared for delivery, at a field hearing in Charlotte, North Carolina titled “Workers in Charge: Restoring Choice and Accountability in the Workplace”:

“Good morning, and welcome to Charlotte, North Carolina.

“I want to thank my colleagues for joining us here in our great state, as well as our witnesses for taking the time to participate in today’s hearing.

“We are here today because every American worker deserves a voice in the workplace and the freedom to choose whether or not to be represented by a union. Our federal labor laws were intended to protect workers’ rights. But today’s hearing will examine whether those laws truly give workers a meaningful say in the unions that represent them and whether union leadership is acting in the best interests of its members.

“Throughout this Congress, Committee Republicans have advanced proposals to strengthen worker choice, improve union transparency, and hold union leaders accountable to their members. Our priority has been clear: put workers first, not union bosses. Unfortunately, my colleagues across the aisle see it the other way around.

“For years, Democrats have catered to powerful union leaders, often at the expense of the hardworking Americans those unions are supposed to represent.

“Committee Republicans believe workers should have the right to decide whether they want union representation through a private, secret ballot-election. And that decision should reflect the will of a majority of all workers, not simply a majority of those who cast a ballot. It is ironic that the same party that prides itself on protecting democracy seems unwilling to apply that principle when it comes to union elections.

“We also know that workers benefit when businesses succeed, grow, and create jobs. In order to create those jobs, businesses need stability and predictability in labor law to make those investments. They need to know what the rules are today and what they will be tomorrow so they can plan for the future.

“Unfortunately, we have seen repeated swings in labor policy whenever Democrats hold the majority at the National Labor Relations Board, often with little regard for the consequences for workers and businesses. Too often, those changes have served the interests of union leadership rather than the people those leaders represent.

“And what are the consequences when federal policies give union leaders more power while leaving workers with less of a say?

“Under current federal law, unions are not required to allow their members to vote on major decisions, including whether to approve contracts or authorize strikes. Yet these decisions can have major consequences for workers and their families, affecting their paychecks, benefits, working conditions, schedules, and job security.

“When so much is at stake for workers and their families, they deserve a voice in these decisions. Greater transparency and meaningful member participation help ensure that union members understand how their unions operate and that they have a say in the decisions being made on their behalf.

“Unfortunately, come January, Democrats will pass bills that take away any influence workers have in the collective bargaining process and on the contracts that shape their lives.

“The Faster Labor Contracts Act, or FLCA, would put government arbitrators—not workers or business owners—in charge of writing labor contracts, without giving workers an opportunity to vote on the outcome. Perhaps a more fitting name for the FLCA would be the Filling Labor’s Coffers Act because the result will be fuller pockets for union leaders and less power for the workers they represent.

“Committee Republicans have taken our oversight responsibility seriously. We have investigated reports of misconduct involving union leadership, including abuses of power, antisemitism, and the employment of a convicted child sex offender.

“Our Democrat colleagues should be doing the same. Instead, they continue to push for bills like the FLCA and the Protecting the Right to Organize Act to do the bidding of unions.

“We look forward to hearing from our witnesses today about the challenges facing American workers and businesses and what we can do to address those challenges.

“As we look ahead to next Congress, Committee Republicans remain committed to a simple principle: workers deserve more choice, a stronger voice, and greater accountability from the unions that represent them. We will continue fighting to ensure that workers, not union bosses, have a meaningful say in decisions that affect their lives and livelihoods.”

title: House Oversight Committee Releases Memorandum on Insider Trading Risks in Prediction Markets

committee.name: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

text:
WASHINGTON­—The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform released a staff memorandum on its investigation into insider trading activity among government officials, military personnel, and individuals with security clearances who have been making trades on prediction market platforms using non-public information for personal profit. As part of the Committee’s investigation, it obtained nearly 1,700 pages of documents and communications and received five bipartisan staff briefings from prediction market platforms on their efforts to detect and report suspicious activity linked to insider trading.

“Americans are rightly concerned about public corruption. Congress has a duty to ensure our laws adequately prevent insider trading, hold bad actors accountable, and prohibit government officials and employees from profiting from nonpublic information. We launched an investigation into insider trading on prediction market platforms and are encouraged by their efforts to prevent, detect, and report illegal activity. Congress must consider additional reforms to prevent public corruption and restore the American people’s trust in government,” said Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.).

Below are key findings and recommendations from the memorandum:

It is paramount that individuals with security clearances or access to non-public government information are prohibited from exploiting prediction markets for personal gain: Prediction markets have discovered suspicious trading activity on their platforms indicative of insider trading. Political candidates and those close to major policy decisions have also engaged in potential insider trading on prediction market platforms.

Insider trading laws apply to contracts on prediction markets: Current federal insider trading laws and regulations apply to prediction markets just as they would securities and derivatives. In 2010, Congress amended the Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) to prohibit fraud and manipulation in derivatives markets. Section 4c(a)(3) of the CEA, as amended by the Stop Trading on Congressional Knowledge (STOCK) Act, prohibits federal agency employees, Members of Congress, congressional employees, and judicial officers and employees from using nonpublic information derived from their positions to trade commodity futures, options, or swaps. Section 4c(a)(4) of the statute also prohibits a covered individual from providing insider information to non-covered third parties who assist or enter into such trades.

Prediction markets play a key role in detecting and preventing suspicious trades and ensuring market integrity: Four of the five platforms provided substantial documentation and/or briefed the Committee on internal control structures and sophisticated proprietary technologies designed to detect and prevent insider trading through suspicious trade patterns. Most of the reported incidents of insider trading within prediction markets were initially detected and reported to regulators and law enforcement by the markets themselves.

Prediction market platforms Polymarket and Kalshi have continually made robust improvements to their insider trading surveillance detection protocols: Polymarket recently hired a former law enforcement expert to oversee a team of employees to manage insider trading prevention detection efforts and implemented a sophisticated surveillance software protocol known as “PolyGraph,” in partnership with the analytics company Chainalysis.

Further statutory restrictions on federal government personnel are necessary: Whether it is an outright prohibition on trading on prediction markets or restrictions on some subset of contracts like government-related contracts, applying these restrictions to officials in all branches of government would strengthen ethical expectations that government personnel should not personally and financially benefit from access to non-public information associated with their work as government servants, and would eliminate even the appearance that government personnel are exploiting non-public information received in an official capacity for financial gain.

Congress should consider further reforms to prevent public corruption and restore public trust: Congress should consider legislation that further restricts the types of event contract markets that federal government personnel, Members of Congress, and congressional staff can participate in, regardless of whether they are trading on insider information. The Committee also recommends that Congress encourage prediction market platforms and regulatory agencies to share information necessary to enforce restrictions on insider trading, enabling the markets to continue to detect and prevent it.

Read the staff memorandum here.

We can revitalize our manufacturing base, and outcompete China with our skilled workforce and American ingenuity.”

“Over decades, the CCP has identified strategic industries and technologies, and sought to dominate them. Unfortunately, America’s workers, communities, and security have paid the price. As China intensifies its efforts to win the innovation competition and monopolize key supply chains, we must learn from the past and invest in the future,” said Khanna.

In addition to the case studies, the report makes the following findings:

China has built a state-directed economic system designed to concentrate capital, resources, technology, and global market share in strategically important industries.

China engages in a whole-of-society effort when it seeks to dominate certain important global industries, combining a series of interlocking measures to accelerate the growth of targeted industries.

China seeks to make the world dependent on Chinese manufacturing, while it eliminates its own foreign policy supply chain dependencies.

title: NEW REPORT: Merkley Unveils Child Care Investigation Exposing Safety Lapses, Drain of Public Resources in Private Equity-Backed Centers
text:
Report Identifies Four Key Findings that Validate Public Concern Over Private Equity’s Increased Role in Child Care Industry

WASHINGTON, D.C. – As the cost of child care continues to skyrocket, U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, released a first of its kind investigation on the effect that private equity involvement in the U.S. child care industry has on child safety. The investigation analyzed publicly available information and licensing data from three states—California, Texas, and Virginia—and focused on the two largest for-profit child care companies by capacity: KinderCare Learning Companies (KinderCare) and Learning Care Group (LCG), and their private equity backers, Partners Group and American Securities, respectively. Collectively, KinderCare and LCG have a combined licensed capacity to enroll over 375,000 children throughout the U.S.

Merkley asked both companies, and their private equity backers, to provide information and documents, such as financial records, ownership structure, tuition and cost trends, safety standards, and employment practices, to better understand the effects of private equity investment in the child care industry. All four companies responded with brief narratives and no underlying records.

“From housing to health care and now child care, private equity firms are taking control of American industries that working families rely on and running them into the ground. Wall Street’s profits-over-people playbook fails families every time, and now we have evidence that private equity is raking in bundles of cash while making child care less safe,” said Ranking Member Jeff Merkley.

“These private equity-backed child care centers refused to provide records while publicly available data from their centers show clear evidence of more complaint-triggered inspections and more serious safety violations than centers not backed by private equity; all while collecting millions of taxpayer dollars. It’s outrageous.

“Families deserve affordable, high-quality care without compromising their children’s safety. Congress must act now to curb predatory private equity practices and ensure all children have the resources they need to thrive,” Merkley concluded.

The report established four major findings, a link to the full report is available at the end of this release:

KinderCare and Learning Care Group rely heavily on public funding.

Approximately one-third of KinderCare’s and LCG’s total revenue is from public funding programs, including subsidies. KinderCare collected roughly $1 billion in subsidy-supported tuition in fiscal year 2025.

KinderCare’s and Learning Care Group’s private equity backers and owners, including Partners Group and American Securities, respectively, extracted over $1.25 billion in dividends, leaving the child care companies with substantial debt.

KinderCare and LCG have borrowed more than $1.25 billion to pay dividends to their owners: $620 million at KinderCare and at least $636 million at LCG. These obligations reduce financial flexibility and make it more important to know how the companies balance debt service and investor payments against child safety, staffing, and affordability—information the companies did not provide as requested.

Across three states, KinderCare and Learning Care Group have more frequent, more serious, and more persistent safety problems than centers not backed by private equity.

Based on Democratic staff analysis of child care licensing and violation records in California, Texas, and Virginia, KinderCare and LCG centers were cited more often, more seriously, and more repeatedly than for-profit chains with no private equity backer (“non-PE chains”) and all other centers.

The two companies drew complaint-triggered inspections at roughly twice the non-PE chain rate and up to four times the rate of all other centers and accumulated high-risk violations at up to three times the non-PE chain rate.

All four companies refused to provide key records.

Despite repeated requests, KinderCare, LCG, Partners Group, and American Securities did not provide the documents and data needed to determine how public subsidies and tuition revenues are allocated among safety, operating costs, workforce investments, debt payments, and returns to investors.

Merkley has been calling attention to the poisonous role of private equity in American life, from housing to youth sports. Merkley led the charge to kick hedge funds out of the housing market as large institutional investors gobble up homes in communities across the United States, driving up both purchase prices and rents for single-family homes. His initiative to limit institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes was included in the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which became law this year. Also this year, he cosponsored the Let Kids Play Act, legislation to stop Wall Street from pricing kids out of sports. The proposed legislation from Sen. Chris Murphy (D-CT) bans private equity firms from taking over youth sports, shutting down the vulture practices they use to jack up costs, and getting money back to the families who have been ripped off. Merkley also previously cosponsored the Corporate Crimes Against Health Care Act, the Take Back Our Hospitals Act, and the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act to fight back against private equity abuses in health care.

The full report, titled Who Profits from Child Care?, is HERE.

title: Wyden, Senate Democrats Demand Answers on Oz Actions to Dismantle Medicaid Fraud Prevention
text:
Senators Seek Information About CMS Compliance with Federal Fraud Prevention Laws

Text of the Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and five Senate Democrats today launched an inquiry into the Trump administration’s politically motivated campaign against state Medicaid programs, after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) withheld billions of dollars from Democratic-led states while dismantling the federal infrastructure designed to detect and prevent fraud.

“The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place,” the senators wrote. “That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.”

The letter, sent to CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, comes as the Trump administration has threatened state health programs with severe funding cuts based on flawed data. CMS recently moved to withhold over billions in funding from California and Minnesota without providing any evidence of wrongdoing to the states. At the same time, the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) decertified state Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) in Hawaii and New York. Public reporting, including an investigation by the Associated Press, revealed that the administration’s fraud claims against New York relied on a basic math error, while other withholding actions have sparked lawsuits from states like Minnesota.

Rather than working with states to fix issues, CMS has replaced on-site reviews and dedicated oversight staff with a public relations “War Room” and unproven artificial intelligence pilots. The letter points out that the administration is violating federal law by failing to maintain the minimum required funding and staffing levels for the Medicaid Integrity Program, which was created by Congress to help states fight fraud.

Senators Alex Padilla, D-Calif., Adam Schiff, D-Calif., Jeff Merkley, D-Ore., Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., and Ed Markey, D-Mass. signed the letter with Wyden.

The text of the letter is here.
