title: Chairman Risch Opening Remarks at Nominations Hearing on November 19
text:
WASHINGTON - U.S. Senator Jim Risch (R-Idaho), chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, today gave the following opening remarks at a full committee nomination hearing. Witnesses included Mr. Elliott Hulse, to be Chief Executive Officer of Millennium Challenge Corporation, Mr. Austin Holmes, to be Ambassador to the Republic of Haiti, and Mr. Asa Pitt, to be United States Representative to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Chairman Risch gave the following remarks:

“Thank you to the three of you for your willingness to step up and take on these obligations. And, importantly, to your families. We all know the families play an important role here. They have as much of a challenge, sometimes, as the nominees do.

“Starting with you, Mr. Hulse, to be nominated to the Millennium Challenge Corporation. It was established to provide a transparent and accountable model of development to break the cycle of aid dependency and enable countries to grow their own way out of poverty. 23 years on, we know that this model works. If confirmed, I look forward to working with you to ensure MCC continues to deliver for the American people.

“Mr. Holmes, as I’m sure you do, I appreciate this Administration’s ongoing efforts to confront gangs, curb insecurity, and increase international burden sharing in order to stop mass migration and prevent further violence and disruption. Continuing this work will be critical as ambassador to Haiti, and I hope to hear your plans to do so.

“And finally, Mr. Pitt. The Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons plays a critical role in keeping the development, production, stockpiling, and use of chemical weapons around the world at bay.

“From Russia’s actions in Ukraine to the remaining chemical weapons around the globe, you will have an important role to play in advancing American national security interests if confirmed. I hope that under your leadership, the OPCW remains an efficient, effective, and credible organization to prevent the development and use of these horrific weapons. And with that, I will recognize our ranking member, Senator Shaheen.”

title: October Unemployment Fell in 17 States plus DC, Remained Unchanged in 23, Increased in 10
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Joint Economic Committee released its monthly State Employment Update, outlining the employment situation in all 50 states and the District of Columbia. In October, among the 50 states and the District of Columbia unemployment fell in 18, rose in 10, and remained unchanged in 23.

The highest unemployment rate was 5.4 percent in the District of Columbia, and the lowest was 2 percent in South Dakota. Nationally, the unemployment rate fell by 0.1 percentage points to 4.1 percent, and the labor force participation rate rose by 0.1 percentage points to 61.9 percent.

Compared to the national unemployment rate of 4.1 percent, in October, one state matched the national average, while 30 states were lower, and 20 states and the District of Columbia were higher.

Also, in October, payroll jobs rose in 38 states and fell in 11. The largest payroll job percent increase was 0.5 percent in Indiana and Kansas. The largest payroll job percent decline was 0.2 percent in Colorado and West Virginia.

For the full report, and to see more details on the employment situation in each State and the District of Columbia visit: https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/employment-update#seu

title: VIDEO: Grassley Hears from Mothers Who Lost Children to Deadly Kratom
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) this week met with parents whose children were killed or harmed by botanical kratom and kratom-related substances, including 7-OH. The meeting follows Grassley’s recent letter to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) urging the agencies to reconsider proposed changes to kratom-related substances’ emergency scheduling order, which would allow deadly kratom products to remain widely sold in gas stations and convenience stores across the country.

“We know that kratom is an opioid that kills people. We have to have strong enforcement of that. I’m sorry for the stories that I’m going to hear, but I’m happy that we have these moms working on this very serious problem that we have with drugs in America. It’s tragic what’s happened to not only these moms, but other families all over the country,” Grassley stated ahead of the meeting.

A fact sheet on kratom and its emergency scheduling order is available HERE.

Wednesday’s meeting attendees included:

Rebecca Strang of Georgia, who lost her son, Robert, at the University of Mississippi in September 2026;

Tia Rustici of Idaho, who lost her daughter, Kielee, in 2025;

Susan Eppard of Michigan, who lost her son, Matthew, in 2021; and

Dean Francis, the founder of End Kratom Addiction, who nearly lost his son, Cameron, to a decade-long battle with kratom addiction.

Following the meeting, Strang, Rustici, Eppard and Francis delivered public remarks. Download video of the mothers’ remarks, filmed by the Foundation for Drug Policy Solutions, HERE. Download video of Grassley’s remarks HERE.

VIDEO

“I'm here today for Robert, because I am determined to find a purpose for my pain, and for Robert's life… My position is very clear: all kratom products should be banned. We have to stop putting profit and industry interests ahead of people's lives. It's time to look beyond who stands to profit and focus on who stands to suffer. Robert's life mattered, and his death matters,” said Rebecca Strang. Full remarks available HERE.

“Something that is sold in the gas station next to the candy bars, something that's marketed as safe, is what destroyed my daughter. Kielee was not using street drugs. She was not drinking alcohol. Most importantly, she was not using 7-OH or synthetics. She was using powder kratom… I cannot bring my daughter back, but if telling her story can help save another parent from being where I am, I will never stop talking,” said Tia Rustici. Full remarks available HERE.

“My 22-year-old son Matthew died from natural botanical kratom leaf powder. According to his toxicology, he had no street drugs, no prescription drugs and no alcohol in his system. The autopsy showed he was perfectly healthy and should have lived out a full life… Kratom leaf is an opioid, and it should be banned throughout the United States… My son should have lived,” said Susan Eppard. Full remarks available HERE.

“These three moms shouldn't have to be here. They live with a pain that very few people will ever understand. But they're here to do everything they can to prevent other families across this nation from the hell and the torment that they endure on a daily basis. All of this is due to the greed of a nefarious industry that exploits loopholes in our dietary supplement laws to masquerade a highly addictive and deadly drug as a plant-based herbal supplement... I want to thank Senator Grassley today for being the fighter that he is to help stop this national nightmare... But no one deserves more credit for today than these three moms who traveled here and openly are sharing their stories in order to protect mothers,” said Dean Francis. Full remarks available HERE.

Photos from the meeting and media availability are available HERE. Photos of Robert Strang, Kielee Rustici and Matthew Eller are available HERE, courtesy of their mothers.

title: Chairman Moran Introduces Improvements to the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), chairman of the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, recently introduced an amended version of the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act. These changes include preserving the standalone disability rating for tinnitus, restoring VA’s authority to pursue future ratings changes without Congressional action, and removing the increases to certain VA home loan fees. Sen. Moran’s amendment also includes a more than $400 million investment in state veterans’ homes to better serve veterans in more than 25 states and removes the current limit on special pay waivers for certain VA clinicians to make it easier for VA to recruit and retain doctors and nurses.

“After receiving feedback from veterans, advocacy organizations, and my colleagues on both sides of the aisle, I have made changes to the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act to address concerns and better serve veterans and military families everywhere,” said Sen. Moran. “This legislation would help tens of millions of veterans, caregivers, survivors, military families and VA staff members throughout the country receive the benefits and help they deserve. The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act is the only way to deliver these benefits to their doorstep. We must pass it now, without any further delay.”

The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act includes 60 different pieces of legislation introduced by Republican and Democrat lawmakers in the Senate and in the U.S. House of Representatives. It includes some of the most widely supported bills in Congress, including the Major Richard Star Act and the Love Lives On Act. It also includes the Veterans’ ACCESS Act, which would expand access to life-saving mental health care and addiction treatment for veterans at risk of suicide or overdose deaths, as well as the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act, which would increase benefits to the most severely disabled veterans and their families.

More information about the changes to the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act can be found here.

title: Ranking Member Scott Statement on DOL’s Proposed ESG Rule

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the Department of Labor (DOL) issued a proposed new rule rolling back a sensible Biden-era regulation permitting retirement plan fiduciaries to consider environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors, such as climate change and labor standards, when evaluating investments. The proposed rule also eliminates the Biden-era standard allowing retirement plan fiduciaries to consider collateral benefits of investments as “tiebreakers” when financial returns are expected to be the same.

“Climate change, labor standards, and other ESG factors have an increasing effect not only on workers, families, and businesses, but also on the long-term value of investments. Considering whether a real estate investment will literally be underwater because of sea level rise is not ideological – it is fact. It is reasonable for plan fiduciaries to be permitted to consider such factors and be able to adopt them if they don’t reduce investment returns.

“It is particularly striking that the Trump Administration is seeking undermine retirement plans’ ability to consider ESG factors at the same time it is racing to finalize a rule giving a legal safe harbor to plans investing in risky and volatile investments, such as crypto. They have got it entirely wrong. The Trump Administration’s proposed ESG rule should be rescinded, and I look forward to asking DOL officials about this rule and its efforts to undermine workers’ retirement security early next Congress.”

Background:

In October 2020, Democrats sent aletter to the first Trump Administration denouncing its initial proposed rule to ban fiduciaries from considering environmental, social, and governance factors.

On June 2, 2026, Today, Ranking Member Scott, Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Ranking Member Bernie Sanders (I-VT), and Senate Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs Ranking Member Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) urged the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) to rescind its proposal to allow private equity, digital assets, private credit, and other “alternative assets” to be included in 401(k) plans.

title: Ranking Member Scott, Student Defense Call on Congress to Establish a Whistleblower Program to Strengthen Federal Student Aid Fraud Prevention

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
WASHINGTON— Today, Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, and Student Defense urged Congress to help curb fraud within the Federal Student Aid program by creating a whistleblower program to incentivize timely reporting of information about possible violations of laws and regulations governing student aid funding. With roughly $131 billion disbursed annually in Federal Student Aid dollars, fraud not only wastes taxpayer resources but also imposes substantial administrative and investigative costs on the U.S. Department of Education.

In aproposal released today, Student Defense argues that current oversight and fraud prevention mechanisms are insufficient given the size of the Federal Student Aid program and the history of abuses, drawing comparisons to Congressionally created whistleblower programs in securities, commodities, tax, anti-money laundering contexts.

Student Defense’s proposal says, “those other systems show a clear federal policy judgment: insiders are often the first to detect complex fraud, and properly designed monetary awards can increase high-quality reporting, improve recoveries, and deter misconduct that would otherwise remain hidden.”

The proposal argues financial incentives would motivate admissions and financial aid officers, professors, enrollment staff, and others to submit tips, which, in turn, could increase financial recoveries to the government and deter misconduct. Insiders often have visibility on enrollment manipulation, attendance falsification, identity misuse, incentive-compensation workarounds, and ‘ghost student’ schemes long before regulators do.

Rep. Scott and Student Defense are calling on Congress to establish incentives and anti-retaliation for student aid whistleblowers, to be coupled with strong anti-retaliation protections, akin to existing programs within the SEC, CFTC, IRS, and Department of Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network. The proposal notes, “the goal is simple: strengthen deterrence, improve fraud detection, and better protect both students and taxpayers.”

“Because of the Trump Administration's relentless attacks on the Department of Education, students and families are struggling to access the information and resources they need to make informed decisions about their future and secure financial aid for their education. Specifically, in March, the Government Accountability Office reported that after the Administration fired nearly half its staff, the Office of Federal Student Aid (FSA) had stopped key oversight of student loan servicers. To make matters worse, FSA has recklessly gutted the very offices tasked with overseeing colleges, exposing students to shady and deceptive practices. Without proper oversight, students and borrowers might receive inaccurate information from schools, servicers, or contractors, putting an affordable education further out of reach and making it harder for those with loans to make appropriate decisions regarding repayment plans they should choose,” said Ranking Member Scott. “FSA oversees the $1.7 trillion student loan portfolio and needs robust, incentive-backed whistleblower protections. This proposal will help uphold and improve the integrity of FSA and protect students, families, and taxpayers from fraud.”

“We know from existing federal administrative programs that whistleblower incentives, paired with strong whistleblower protections, are an effective tool to ferret out complex financial fraud. With the scope of the taxpayer and student investment in higher education, there is no reason why the same approach shouldn’t be applied for federal student aid fraud,” said Dan Zibel, Co-Founder and Chief Counsel of Student Defense. “Students and taxpayers both pay the price for fraud schemes. They can waste federal dollars, leave students vulnerable to unnecessary debt, and undermine the integrity of our higher education system.”

To read Student Defense’s proposal, click here.

title: Ranking Member Huffman’s Plan for a Better Permitting Deal
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) announced a series of legislative fixes in the Committee’s jurisdiction to the Senate’s permitting reform bill that he and other Democrats are demanding in order to support passage in the House of Representatives.

“Like most members of Congress, I support responsible permitting reform. I want our government’s approval processes for all types of projects to be faster and better for everyone involved – for companies who build things, workers who need jobs, and communities who deserve a say in projects that impact them. And I’m willing to support significant changes to make that happen.

“But there’s a lot more going on in BAAJA than just streamlining the permitting system. As drafted, this bill is the most sweeping rollback of environmental laws we’ve ever seen – dramatically weakening protections for public lands, clean air and water, endangered wildlife, and sacred tribal sites.

“And Republicans now want to rush it through the House and get it to President Trump’s desk before the end of the year.

“I stand with a growing majority of Democrats who are drawing a principled line and refusing to be jammed – we will not support BAAJA unless there are fixes to the most glaring problems. We support responsible permitting reform – and there’s just too much at stake here for a rush job, just to get a deal done before the next Congress takes over.

“The American people, including the people’s House, deserve a say in this bill, and House Democrats – especially after the recent election – are going to insist on that.”

Watch Ranking Member Huffman lay out his plan.

Background

Ranking Member Huffman outlined five critical fixes in the jurisdiction of the Natural Resources Committee needed to earn his support for the Senate-passed permitting bill:

Respect Tribal sovereignty. Preserve Tribal consultation obligations, treaty rights, and the ability to enforce those rights in court.

Protect communities’ access to justice. Ensure people can challenge illegally approved projects and judges can stop damaging construction before the harm is done.

Close “forever permit” loopholes. Preserve future administrations’ ability to address illegal approvals and adopt health and environmental safeguards without forcing taxpayers to compensate corporations.

Protect endangered wildlife. Ensure decisions about endangered species follow the best available science.

Protect public lands and sacred places. Preserve protections for America’s special places like the Boundary Waters, Chaco Canyon, and America’s Arctic, and block giant AI data centers on public lands.

Full video transcript below:

“Let’s talk about where things stand in the final three weeks of this Congress on BAAJA, a huge 500-page permitting reform bill that passed the Senate last week. I want to be clear on exactly what is in this bill, why I oppose it in its current form, and how we can fix it – either now, if the bill’s supporters will negotiate reasonable changes, or six weeks from now, when Democrats hold the gavels in the next Congress.

Like most members of Congress, I support responsible permitting reform. I want our government’s approval processes for all types of projects to be faster and better for everyone involved – for companies who build things, workers who need jobs, and communities who deserve a say in projects that impact them. And I’m willing to support significant changes to make that happen.

But there’s a lot more going on in BAAJA than just streamlining the permitting system. As drafted, this bill is the most sweeping rollback of environmental laws we’ve ever seen – dramatically weakening protections for public lands, clean air and water, endangered wildlife, and sacred tribal sites.

The bill fundamentally changes federal reviews and approvals for all types of projects – not just power lines, but everything from data centers to pipelines and LNG terminals, uranium mines, ICE detention centers, and even President Trump’s vanity projects.

And it dramatically curtails the ability of impacted communities to engage in the review process – including native American tribes, sportsmen who hunt, fish and recreate on public lands, and conservation groups. And when they do, it makes it virtually impossible to force changes or to stop harmful projects in court, even when laws are broken.

Now, in a normal legislative process, especially for a huge complex bill like this, you would see public hearings with testimony from experts and careful deliberation. And legislators would have a chance to vote on amendments to fix major problems. But the Senate didn’t allow any of that with BAAJA – which is why two-thirds of Senate Democrats voted No.

And Republicans now want to rush it through the House and get it to President Trump’s desk before the end of the year.

I stand with a growing majority of Democrats who are drawing a principled line and refusing to be jammed – we will not support BAAJA unless there are fixes to the most glaring problems. We support responsible permitting reform – and there’s just too much at stake here for a rush job, just to get a deal done before the next Congress takes over.

Some have suggested that Democrats are just opposed to reaching ANY deal with Republicans and the Trump administration. And that’s not true – certainly not on this issue.

So let’s be specific. The most controversial and problematic parts of BAAJA fall under the jurisdiction of the Natural Resources Committee, which I hope to be chairing when the new Congress convenes a few weeks from now. I will tell you the specific changes that would remove my opposition and get me, and I believe many other Democrats, to “yes” as soon as next week.

Respecting Tribal Nations comes first. When a project threatens a Tribe’s water, treaty rights, or sacred sites, the federal government has obligations it must honor. The changes to the NHPA and CWA in BAAJA strip tribal nations of their seat at the table and their rights in court. That has to change.

The same goes for other impacted communities who deserve a fair chance to voice concerns about projects that could be harmful to them and – if the government breaks the law in approving a data center, mine, a pipeline or other project – to sometimes challenge that decision in court. BAAJA not only makes it much harder for impacted communities to bring a case, it blocks judges from issuing orders to change or stop a project even if it’s found to be illegal. That must change.

BAAJA also has loopholes that create “forever permits.” In other words, the permits the Trump administration hands out to their buddies over the next two years – even if they are found to be destructive or illegal – could be locked in for good. The extreme, unpopular policies and corruption we’ve seen from this administration are going to end when Donald Trump leaves the White House two years from now. But on energy and environmental policy, BAAJA essentially legislates a third term for Trump by tying the hands of future administrations regarding Trump’s decisions and putting taxpayers on the hook for massive damages if new health or environmental safeguards are placed on polluting projects.

BAAJA includes a radical rollback of the Endangered Species Act that goes far beyond anything that could be justified in the name of permit streamlining. The ESA is our most important safeguard for protecting America’s wildlife and habitat endangered species need to survive. BAAJA provisions that undermine the independence and quality of the science to skew ESA decisions against protection of wildlife must be removed.

Finally, data centers on public lands. I don't think there should ever be data centers on public land, but it's a real threat. This administration is pushing over a dozen giveaways of public land for huge data centers. At a minimum, if Donald Trump is going to propose data centers on our public lands that belong to all of us, there has to be a full and complete environmental review with a chance for everyone to participate in that process, and for those who may be impacted by it to challenge it in court.

The changes I’ve outlined won’t solve every problem with the bill. But we deserve at least this much to protect the basic interests of our environment, tribes, and communities all over the country.

We have specific legislative text ready to go to make these changes happen, and that is being shared with the sponsors of BAAJA. If the bill’s backers are open to compromise and will work with us on these changes – we can still pass the bill in this Congress, despite the terrible process that brought us to this point.

But if they continue the “take it or leave it” ultimatum approach, I’ll do everything I can to stop this bad deal. And six weeks from now, when Democrats are in charge, we will get to work on a strong, responsible permitting reform that everyone can get behind.

The American people, including the people’s House, deserve a say in this bill, and House Democrats – especially after the recent election – are going to insist on that.

So, for those who want to pass BAAJA now, I’ve told you how to fix it and I’m ready to work with you to make that happen. But if it can’t happen in the remaining three weeks of this Congress, that’s not the end of the story. Because if BAAJA doesn’t pass, I guarantee you House Democrats will keep working on this and we’ll deliver a much better deal – responsible permitting reform that helps build the things we need faster and more affordably without throwing tribes, local communities and the environment under the bus.”

###

title: Velázquez Leads Committee Democrats Questioning SBA’s Decision to Eliminate Public Comment Requirements
text:
WASHINGTON —House Small Business Committee Ranking Member Nydia M. Velázquez (D-NY) and 11 Democratic committee colleagues are raising concerns and questioning the Small Business Administration’s (SBA) decision to eliminate longstanding public notice and comment requirements for regulations affecting small businesses.

In a letter to the Administrator sent on November 19, 2026, the lawmakers sounded the alarm about an August 31 final rule rescinding its longstanding practice of following the Administrative Procedure Act's (APA) notice-and-comment requirements for certain regulations. These requirements give small businesses and other stakeholders an opportunity to review and provide feedback on proposed rules before they take effect. Although the APA exempts certain regulations involving loans, grants, benefits, and contracts, the SBA had voluntarily followed these procedures for more than 50 years.

The lawmakers warned that the decision will make it harder for small businesses to have a say in federal policies that directly affect their operations.

“This coverage recognized that public comment periods provide Americans, small businesses, and industries affected by rulemaking with a meaningful opportunity to shape the policies that impact both their day-to-day operations and long-term success, and to help ensure government officials are making informed decisions,” wrote the lawmakers. They continued that the change “does not instill confidence that the final rules will reflect the real-world impact of the changes on the small business community.”

The letter calls on the SBA to withdraw the rule and requests information about how the agency will determine which future regulations will be subject to public comment. Specifically, the lawmakers seek details about the criteria SBA will use to solicit public input and any guidance provided to agency employees regarding those decisions.

The lawmakers also challenged the SBA's rationale and justification for eliminating these requirements. According to the agency's own estimates, the change would save approximately $28,000 annually, representing just 0.008 percent of the SBA's salaries and expenses budget.

In addition to Ranking Member Velázquez the letter was also signed by Representatives Morgan McGarvey (KY), Hillary Scholten (MI), LaMonica McIver (NJ), Gilbert R. Cisneros Jr. (CA), Kelly Morrison (MN), George Latimer (NY), Derek Tran (CA), Lateefah Simon (CA), Johnny Olszewski Jr. (MD), Maggie Goodlander (NH), and Analilia Mejia (NJ).

The full letter can be viewed here.

The letter follows introduction of Velázquez’s the Maintaining Small Business Engagement Act of 2026. The legislation would codify the previous rules and require the SBA to continue providing small businesses with the opportunity to weigh in on policies affecting their operations.

Velazquez’s legislation has the support of the following organizations:

“Small businesses have historically had a voice in the regulatory process through public comment periods,” said Alexis D'Amato Falvey, Senior Director of Federal Government Affairs for Small Business Majority. “The U.S. Small Business Administration’s (SBA) unilateral decision to issue rules without any input from small businesses denies entrepreneurs a seat at the table and an opportunity to inform the policies that impact their livelihoods. We support the Maintaining Small Business Engagement Act because it would protect entrepreneurs' ability to remain involved in the regulatory process and hold SBA accountable to the Main Street businesses it was created to serve.”

“The Maintaining Small Business Engagement Act ensures small businesses and public stakeholders have an opportunity to make their voices heard when SBA issues new rules. Robust public participation and small business input allows agencies to better ascertain the benefits of its proposals and ensures decisions are made with diverse perspectives in mind,” said Katie Tracy, director of regulatory policy and advocacy at Public Citizen.

“It is critically important that small businesses and the public participate in SBA’s rulemaking process,” said Rachel Weintraub, executive director of the Coalition for Sensible Safeguards. “The Maintaining Small Business Engagement Act is key to enabling this participation that will strengthen SBA proposals.”

“The regulatory process is often complicated, and commenting on proposed changes can be time-consuming and burdensome for small business owners. That does not mean they should lose the opportunity to weigh in on proposed regulatory changes as they arise. Women Impacting Public Policy (WIPP) applauds Congresswoman Nydia Velázquez for introducing the Maintaining Small Business Engagement Act, which would preserve that right by reversing a Small Business Administration (SBA) rule that rescinds notice-and-comment requirements for regulations affecting small businesses. Women business owners deserve a voice in the regulatory process,” said Women Impacting Public Policy (WIPP).

“Small businesses rarely have the means to respond quickly to a notice-and-comment, but they deserve to have their voices heard on regulations that could affect their businesses. Without a seat at the table, an agency could create regulations that impede small business growth. NAWBO supports the Maintain Small Business Engagement Act because it preserves this right. Our small business owners need time to process, think, and craft a response that reflects up-to-date information on the impacts,” said Jen Earle, CEO of the National Association of Women Business Owners (NAWBO).

“We support Rep. Nydia Velazquez efforts to ensure that small businesses have a voice in public policies and rulemaking impacting their businesses. Good governance is not one sided. It requires good listening skills to hear constituents with sometimes divergent views in an open, transparent manner in order to form the basis of program implementation and effectiveness,” said Roger A. Campos, Founder & Chairman of MBRT Business RoundTable.

“Small businesses rely on transparency and predictable opportunities to review and comment on agency rules that directly govern their eligibility and contracting opportunities. Given that the SBA's primary mission is to advocate for and support small businesses, it is perplexing why the agency would actively seek to reduce its ability to hear directly from the very community it exists to serve. We strongly oppose this final rule and urge the Administration to maintain mandatory public participation and encourage Congress to codify notice and comment requirements to protect small business participation across federal procurement,” said the Board of Directors of the HUBZone Contractors National Council (HCNC).

title: Chairman Walberg on DOL Rule to Protect Workers' Retirement Savings

committee.name: House Committee on Education and Workforce

text:
Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-MI) issued the following statement today on the proposed rule “Loyalty and Exclusive Purpose Rule in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights,” which strengthens protections for workers' retirement savings by clarifying that investment decisions must be based on financial interests, not environmental, social, and governance (ESG) or other political agendas:

I support the Department of Labor’s efforts to reinforce this basic principle and protect the retirement security of hardworking Americans.”

title: ICYMI: DHS Secretary Mullin, DNI Clayton, & FBI Deputy Director Raia Testify on Worldwide Threats to the Homeland 25 Years After 9/11
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. –– This week, the House Committee on Homeland Security, led by Chairman Andrew R. Garbarino (R-NY), convened its annual Worldwide Threats hearing to examine the evolving national security challenges facing the United States. Twenty-five years after the September 11 terrorist attacks, the hearing focused on the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) readiness to address the growing threats posed by foreign terrorist organizations as technology evolves, critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, and aggression from nation-states like China, Iran, and Russia. Witness testimony was provided by DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Jay Clayton, and Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Christopher Raia.

During the hearing, Members heard testimony on recent reporting warning of potential Iran-backed terrorist plots targeting the homeland, ongoing information technology (IT) disruptions, deployment of counter-drone capabilities, and DHS’s capacity to address emerging cyber threats as artificial intelligence (AI) expands the scope and speed of intrusions.

In his opening statement, DNI Clayton outlined the intelligence community’s efforts to detect and disrupt threats from foreign adversaries, addressed concerns regarding potential cyberattacks, and highlighted the importance of FISA 702 in the intelligence mission:

“I want to address the several unrelated issues that have recently caused service disruptions. I understand the timing of these incidents can raise questions, and it should. The American people should ask us these questions. But based on what we know today, after a great deal of diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack. The intelligence community continues to monitor and stay alert to any possibility of malicious cyber activity threatening the U.S. networks and our law enforcement partners.”

“It is clear that our foreign adversaries are more sophisticated and more determined than ever to bring harm to the American people and our way of life. I want to mention FISA 702. It should not expire. It is the single most indispensable tool we have to protect both Americans in the homeland and our troops abroad. This is the same authority that we rely on to provide early warnings to this body of foreign threats, members of the administration, and members of Congress. No other program can replicate the speed and effectiveness of FISA 702. Letting it expire would simply be a mistake.”

In his opening statement, Deputy Director Raia highlighted the FBI’s counterterrorism success under the Trump administration:

“In the past 21 months, the FBI has arrested nearly 1,300 terrorists, conducted over 1,300 counterterrorism disruptions, and seized 430 illegal firearms in counterterrorism investigations. Just last week, a joint investigation by FBI New York and Washington field offices resulted in the indictment against three Iranian-backed operatives for their alleged involvement in nearly 20 terrorist attacks and attempted attacks across Europe and the United States… Our counterintelligence efforts have resulted in 167 arrests––that’s a 53% increase in the previous 21 months––and 499 disruptions targeting espionage and other foreign hostile activities.”

Chairman Garbarino asked Secretary Mullin about the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s (CISA) workforce and its capability to fulfill its core mission, to which Secretary Mullin testified:

“Our mission is broad, and we constantly meet threats and work with…industries. Anytime they ask for assistance, we’re able to respond. During FIFA, you saw CISA was able to stand up information centers…all across the United States, work with 11 cities, work with municipalities– federal, state, and local. We were able to coordinate, and it all came through CISA. We had one incident in Miami that happened about four o’clock in the morning. Because of CISA’s coordination with the local municipality in Miami, we were able to locate the threat… We were able to neutralize what the threat was, and it wouldn’t have been possible without CISA recognizing the traffic online––to be able to see it.”

“CISA plays a critical role in everything we do, because almost all communications, all traffic we see goes through a device. And without CISA being able to be there to meet the need, we’d be dark. And I’ll say this one more time, too, Chairman. We’re able to meet those needs today, but we want to grow our capacity.”

Subcommittee on Border Security and Enforcement Chairman Michael Guest (R-MS) asked witnesses about each agency’s work to disrupt potential Iran-backed plots in the homeland:

“I want to revert back to a question Mr. McCaul brought up about the media reports––about possible Iranian actors, that they are developing plans to target senior Trump administrative officials by the use of a ‘dirty bomb,’ or by chemical weapons. These reports, of course, raise serious national security concerns. We know that under the previous administration that there were millions of individuals who entered the country illegally… Are you concerned about the possibilities of sleeper cells operating within our borders? And, if so, are we taking the necessary steps to identify, monitor, and disrupt those potential threats before those actions are put in place?”

Secretary Mullin testified:

“This is what the Department of Homeland Security was stood up for. Is it a concern? Of course. Are we fighting it and stomping it down every single day? Absolutely. Our men and women are completely dedicated to it. They showed it even when they were shut down for over 120 days last year. They still showed up for work and still carried out the mission. We have great partners with [ODNI], great partners with DOJ, and we work in a cohesive manner to go after every one of these threats.”

Deputy Director Raia testified:

“Obviously, it’s a concern for us––having read that reporting now every day for a decade. I will tell you a lot of the reporting is largely aspirational, but that does not mean we do not take it seriously. We have revamped our Iranian threat mission center to help combat that threat.”

Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology Chairman Dale W. Strong (R-AL) asked Secretary Mullin and Deputy Director Raia about the impacts of expanded authorities for state and local agencies to mitigate unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), or drones, and how these authorities are strengthening cooperation between every level of law enforcement:

“Deputy Director Raia, can you speak to the importance of Redstone Arsenal and the broader Huntsville [Alabama] community to the FBI’s mission, and the opportunities you see for continued growth and collaboration there?”

Deputy Director Raia testified:

“I think one of the biggest strides that we made in the last 21 months, not only with the FBI, but with the Department of Homeland Security and our federal partners, is in that fight against…UAS. All you have to do is look at a YouTube video and see what’s going on overseas with explosive payloads put on these [UAS]. Twenty-one months ago, I was very concerned about that technology coming over here to the United States, and I am still concerned about that threat coming here to the United States. However, in the last 21 months, based on a multitude of things, to include standing up the National Counter-UAS Training Center, where we are deputizing state, local, and other federal authorities to give them the same technology to…not only detect but mitigate all across the country and increase that throughput. We are much better postured against that threat than we were 21 months ago.”

Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) asked about the impacts of recent IT and telecommunications disruptions on Americans’ confidence in the resilience of our critical infrastructure, to which DNI Clayton testified:

“The American people are right to say, ‘Hey, you know, you in government, you in industry, what’s going on?’ … We’ve used our tools, and we have no evidence that this is a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity. That said, you make a very good point. The pace of technological advancement is increasing. It’s increasing where we have access to it at the government. It’s increasing in the private sector, and it’s increasing outside the United States. We need to be prepared for that.”

Rep. Vince Fong (R-CA) asked witnesses about the threat posed by China’s theft of American AI innovation:

“In April, the White House warned that the PRC, their entities, are conducting industrial-scale distillation in American frontier AI models, copying our capabilities without permission. Every advanced American lab that makes AI capabilities are now being reproduced in these models and then released and used openly in the world, including criminals, terrorists, hostile governments, Russia, China, Iran, North Korea––to name a few. How quickly are you both seeing frontier cyber capabilities reach PRC models and the actors who use them? And what does that mean for the time American defenders have to fix vulnerabilities before they’re exploited?”

DNI Clayton testified:

“America is still in the lead. We need to remain in the lead. You bring up an important point that Americans should recognize, and that is that industrial espionage––whether it’s state-sponsored or private-sponsored––is a threat. There are people who are seeking to steal our trade secrets, seeking to steal our exquisite compute. It’s something that we work very closely with the FBI to combat, but it is a reality. And this is about worldwide threats. One of the worldwide threats to America is industrial espionage.”

Rep. Gabe Evans (R-CO) asked Secretary Mullin about the continuation of the Trump administration’s successful border security policies:

“We’ve secured the border the last two years. But unfortunately, now we’re starting to see reporting coming out about caravans and cartels anxiously awaiting the new Congress to be seated so that they can hopefully go back to business as usual… And so, the first question to you is, can you comment on any intel or other reporting about how cartels and caravans are hoping to exploit potentially relaxed border security procedures in the next Congress?”

Secretary Mullin testified:

“Under the previous Biden administration, the cartels turned human trafficking into a multi-billion-dollar industry. And they’re selling, unfortunately, very vulnerable people a bill of goods that they can’t deliver. They will not be allowed to enter the United States underneath President Trump’s watch. Our border is secure and it will remain secure… So, for anyone that’s thinking about joining one of these caravans and allowing the cartels to extort dollars from you––you’re wasting your money.”

Rep. Matt Van Epps (R-TN) asked Deputy Director Raia about the evolution of threats from domestic terrorism:

“The terror threat landscape in the U.S. is increasingly shaped by emerging nihilistic violent extremism, or NVE. These decentralized online groups are primarily run by youth and minors who promote cycles of victimization and coercion, including self-harm extortion and mass attacks. I’m very concerned about what this is doing to our youth. At the federal level, how is the FBI approaching investigations and prosecutions tied to NVE groups, since most are minors with prosecutorial limitations?”

Deputy Director Raia testified:

“What we have done at the FBI is we’ve created the NVE fusion cell, and we’ve taken experts from our domestic terrorism folks and experts from our crimes against children folks, and we’ve put them in one room in order to create that synergy to investigate those cases. So, we’ve seen a lot of wins in that space recently. But as you said, a lot of these are minors and, as you know, the federal system is not set up for minors. So, we rely a lot on our state and local partners in not only disrupting those individuals, but also in getting some type of jail time and making sure they’re held accountable.”

title: FDA Blocked from Inspecting Clinical Trial Site at a Chinese Military Hospital

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
An excerpt from Prescription America: How to Protect Americans from a Dangerous Dependence on China for Their Medicines details how the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) denied the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) from inspecting a clinical trial site at a People’s Liberation Army (PLA) hospital. In 2021 and again in 2024, a clinical investigator at the 5th PLA Medical Center in Beijing blocked the FDA from accessing the site by requiring its inspectors to recognize the CCP’s claims over Taiwan.

“Any facility that blocks the FDA from inspecting its clinical trials cannot be trusted to develop safe medicines for Americans. It is already outrageous that Western companies are developing drugs at sites run by the PLA and even worse that the FDA is being blocked from inspections. This incident serves as a reminder of why it is critical to invest in our biotechnology sector to bring innovation back home. The FDA should never accept data from sites controlled by the PLA, and we must cut dependence on Chinese firms for our pharmaceutical supply chains,” said Chairman John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China.

In August, Moolenaar sent a letter to the FDA calling on the agency to end the use of drug trial data from China for new clinical trial or drug applications unless the FDA has inspected the trial site in the past 12 months.

In May, Moolenaar advanced language in the 2027 Department of Agriculture funding bill report that would prohibit “the FDA from accepting, reviewing, or considering any covered clinical data generated by a clinical investigation site” in China.

title: Select Committee Investigation: Major Drug Companies Reject Future Clinical Trials in Xinjiang and PLA Hospitals

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
Five major American pharmaceutical companies – AbbVie, Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly, Merck, and Pfizer – will no longer start clinical trials at sites in China run by the People’s Liberation Army. Four of the five companies are also ending clinical trials in Xinjiang, a region where the Chinese Communist Party is carrying out a genocide of the Uyghurs and other minorities. The only company not ending clinical trials in Xinjiang is AbbVie, the maker of Humira. Earlier this year, Chairman John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China sent them letters seeking information about their activities at those sites.

“Major American drugmakers are changing course and doing the right thing by halting new clinical trials at high-risk locations in Xinjiang and at Chinese military hospitals. Doing drug research at these locations raised serious ethical and national security concerns. In America, we have an unwavering commitment to openness, ethics, and scientific excellence. These core values reflect our nation, and they are everything the CCP abhors. It is common sense to ensure that our pharmaceutical research is not intertwined with the CCP’s human rights abuses,” said Moolenaar.

“It is outrageous that AbbVie will still conduct clinical trials in a region where the CCP is committing genocide. That decision does not reflect the values of its customers or even the majority of its employees, and it should immediately join its peers in ending this practice,” added Moolenaar.

title: Select Committee Releases Prescription America: How to Protect Americans from a Dangerous Dependence on China for Their Medicines

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
Today, Chairman John Moolenaar of the Select Committee on China released Prescription America: How to Protect Americans from a Dangerous Dependence on China for Their Medicines. This new Select Committee investigation looks at America’s drug development compared to China’s heavily subsidized and ethically dubious drug industry. The report offers solutions to reverse the hollowing out of the U.S. drug innovation industry, and how to stop the migration of clinical trials to China where they circumvent American regulations and ethical standards.

“America must lead the world in the development of future lifesaving measures including cancer therapies and the medicines we rely on. We cannot allow China to get ahead and control drug development or it will use that power against us. Urgent action is needed and this new investigation makes critical policy recommendations for the future of American medicine,” said Moolenaar. “The Chinese government's central role in the COVID-19 crisis, reports of dirty factories making unapproved GLP-1 drugs, and clinical trial deaths are all warning signs. When it comes to public health, we do not want our foremost adversary leading the way.”

“Biotechnology underpins U.S. economic strength, national security, and scientific leadership. Like artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors, it will shape the nation’s competitiveness for decades to come. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has made the sector a priority and is rapidly building the capacity to challenge U.S. dominance. The United States must act now to protect and strengthen its biotechnology ecosystem or risk being overtaken,” says the first page of the report.

Fast Facts

Here are key facts from the investigation:

China is executing a coordinated, state-sponsored industrial policy to dominate the global biotechnology sector.

China’s fast and cheap clinical trial system is accelerated by weak ethical safeguards.

U.S. companies are fueling China’s strategy.

The FDA incentivizes development in China.

Representatives of the Chinese government impeded the FDA from conducting inspections at sites in Xinjiang and at People's Liberation Army hospitals, where major U.S. companies including Bristol Myers Squibb and Merck have run clinical trials.

China’s innovation feeds off of fast followers and, allegedly, theft.

Policy Recommendations

The report makes 12 policy recommendations to stop the threat of the CCP surpassing America in drug development:

Stop subsidizing the CCP’s strategy to dominate biotechnology and pharmaceuticals.

Restrict FDA acceptance of Chinese clinical trial data.

Ban FDA acceptance of clinical trial data from PLA hospitals and clinical trial sites in Xinjiang.

Modernize the U.S. clinical trial system.

Ensure strong support for foundational biomedical research.

Pressure the International Council for Harmonization of Technical Requirements for Pharmaceuticals for Human Use to suspend China’s membership.

Explore centralized Institutional Review Boards.

Explore monetary incentives for companies that conduct early-stage clinical trials in the U.S.

Explore surcharges or penalties for Investigational New Drug applications for therapies that were developed from early-stage clinical trials in China.

Study patent disclosure vulnerabilities affecting American biotechnology innovators.

Ensure the FDA and its clinical reviewers are adequately staffed.

Establish a White House Biotechnology Coordinator.

title: With Greater Retirement Security on the Line, Clearer Social Security Language for Seniors Signed into Law

committee.name: House Committee on Ways and Means

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Americans planning for retirement will get clearer, more straightforward information about when to claim Social Security under legislation advanced by the Ways and Means Committee and signed into law by President Trump. The Claiming Age Clarity Act (H.R. 5284), introduced by Representative Lloyd Smucker (PA-11), requires the Social Security Administration (SSA) to replace confusing terms with plain language that will more clearly demonstrate how the age at which someone claims benefits affects the size of their monthly benefits.

Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith (MO-08) issued the following statement:

“Deciding when to claim Social Security is one of the biggest financial choices a senior will ever make. That choice should not hinge on government jargon that hides how much money is at stake. Thanks to the Claiming Age Clarity Act, Americans will now see plainly what they gain by waiting and what they give up by claiming their Social Security benefits early. This law empowers seniors, and I commend Representative Smucker for his leadership in helping folks make more informed decisions about their retirement and thank President Trump for signing this into law.”

Representative Lloyd Smucker (PA-11) issued the following statement:

“This law will make it easier for Americans who have worked hard their entire lives to make informed decisions about their Social Security retirement benefits. The confusing government terminology will now be replaced with straightforward language that better explains how the age at which someone claims Social Security affects their monthly benefit. I thank Rep. Don Beyer for joining me in introducing this legislation, our colleagues for supporting this legislation, and President Trump for signing it into law.”

The bill passed the Ways and Means Committee by a vote of 41 to 1, cleared the U.S. House of Representatives by voice vote, and passed the Senate by unanimous consent.

Claiming Age Clarity Act (H.R. 5284):

“Early eligibility age” will now be referred to as “minimum monthly benefit age” – Age 62 is the earliest a worker can claim Social Security retirement benefits. However, claiming benefits at that age permanently reduces a worker’s monthly benefit.

“Full retirement age” and “normal retirement age” will now be referred to as “standard monthly benefit age” – Workers who wait until age 66 or 67 (depending on their year of birth) to claim Social Security retirement benefits will receive their full benefit without a reduction.

Any reference to age 70 as the maximum age up to which delayed retirement credits can be accrued will now be referred to as the “maximum monthly benefit age” – Claiming benefits after age 66 or 67 (depending on year of birth) permanently increases a worker’s benefit until they reach age 70.

The bill was backed by Bipartisan Policy Center Action, AMAC Action, and AARP.

Read a fact sheet on the bill here.

title: Whitehouse Urges Swift House Passage of Permitting Reform, Data Center Accountability Bill

committee.name: Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works

text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee, today released a statement urging the House to swiftly pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA), legislation that would lower costs for American families and crack down on data centers that are raising utility costs for consumers and small businesses:

“For the last year, I’ve investigated AI companies for pursuing massive off-grid, emissions-heavy gas turbines to power their new data centers. And last month, the American people loudly asked Democrats to bring down their energy costs and end the free ride for data centers.

“BAAJA would end data center free-loading and require current and future data centers to pay for the upgrades to the grid that their huge electricity consumption requires, without passing off any of their costs to consumers, which they are currently doing. It’s a strong, bipartisan whack against an industry run amok.

“Democrats should not deny Americans the data center accountability they have demanded over ghost stories being told to try to deliberately mislead people.”

The Senate voted to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 by a vote of 62-33 late last week.

BAAJA would ensure that data centers pay the full cost of their associated transmission needs plus upgrades to the larger transmission network, rather than passing those costs on to families and small businesses. Grid Strategies estimates $55 billion in transmission costs could be collected from data centers over ten years due to BAAJA’s data center accountability language, which would represent $35 billion in additional costs to data centers from baseline policy.

The Institute for Progress on Friday released a timely report pushing back on misinformed speculation that the permitting reform legislation could spur the buildout of data centers on public lands. The report finds, “BAAJA has no direct effect on the laws that could authorize data centers on public lands, such as the Federal Land Policy and Management Act (FLPMA). Nor does the bill prohibit any FLPMA permit from being revised pursuant to applicable law or regulation, or set aside if it illegally permitted a data center on public lands.”

In March, Senators Whitehouse, Martin Heinrich (D-NM), and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) launched an investigation into eight AI companies, including xAI, OpenAI, and Meta, regarding twelve planned data center projects that would be powered by massive new off-grid gas plants. The off-grid gas plants—many of which are ten or more times the size of the average gas plant currently powering the U.S. electric grid—would emit millions of tons of greenhouse gases and tens of thousands of tons of health-harming pollutants every year. In October, Whitehouse launched a bicameral investigation into the Environmental Protection Agency’s (EPA) guidance exempting data center power plants from the Acid Rain Program (ARP).

BAAJA will deliver cheaper, cleaner energy, more well-paying jobs, lower electric bills, and responsible growth by accelerating the permitting and construction of critical energy and infrastructure projects while maintaining key environmental and historic preservation safeguards. The legislation provides greater certainty for projects that have already been permitted and financed, including by preventing the current and future administrations from arbitrarily revoking permits, while establishing clear timelines for environmental reviews and legal challenges. It also includes major reforms to expand and modernize the electric grid, and speed the development of geothermal, nuclear, and other energy projects. The legislation reflects input from members of both houses of Congress on both sides of the aisle and a diverse group of stakeholders.

The legislation has been endorsed by the AFL-CIO, North America’s Building Trades Unions, Laborers’ International Union of North America (LIUNA), Evergreen Action, and Citizens’ Climate Lobby. The New York Times editorial board has urged Democrats to “take the deal” and pass the legislation, highlighting its capacity to deliver lower electricity costs and reduce emissions.

title: Ranking Members Shaheen, Meeks Call on Trump Administration to Implement and Enforce Bipartisan Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and U.S. Representative Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding full implementation of the bipartisan Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which was signed into law on December 18, 2025.

In the letter, the Ranking Members demand answers about the Administration’s failure to fully implement the law, which Secretary Rubio championed during his time in the Senate, and question how this failure is consistent with the Trump Administration’s stated priorities of using sanctions and other tools to target Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and their support networks in our hemisphere. The Ranking Members reiterate the urgency of implementing this legislation amid Haiti’s worsening security and humanitarian situation. They also request a bipartisan classified briefing on what steps the Administration will take to ensure timely implementation and enforcement of the law.

“Under the Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which Secretary Rubio led as the Republican sponsor when he was a Senator, the State Department is required to work with the interagency to submit an annual report identifying Haitian political and economic elites with significant ties to criminal gangs who have supported, protected, or benefitted from the ongoing security crisis and describe their criminal collusion in detail,” wrote the Ranking Members.

“Despite Secretary Rubio’s declaration in May 2025 that ‘the age of impunity for those supporting violence in Haiti is over,’ the Administration also did not comply with the Act’s mandatory requirement that the political and economic sponsors of gangs be sanctioned by September 28, 2026. The Administration has not invoked the Act’s national security waiver nor provided any other rationale for its inaction,” continued the Ranking Members.

“At a time when the Haitian people are preparing to vote for the first time in over a decade, Congress, the American public and the Haitian people deserve transparency about the nature and scale of collusion between gangs and their political and economic support networks,” concluded the Ranking Members.

Full text of the letter is available HERE and provided below.

Dear Secretaries Rubio, Bessent and Hegseth:

We are writing to express our concern regarding the Administration’s failure to fully implement the bipartisan Haitian Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which passed as Section 8319 of the National Defense Authorization Act for FY26 (NDAA FY26) and was enacted into law on December 18, 2025. By failing to name and sanction the political and economic elite fueling Haiti’s insecurity, the Administration allows those responsible to evade accountability and signals that their actions carry no consequences. The Administration’s inaction undermines U.S. efforts to advance security and democratic governance in Haiti and harms U.S. national security interests.

Under the Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which Secretary Rubio led as the Republican sponsor when he was a Senator, the State Department is required to work with the interagency to submit an annual report identifying Haitian political and economic elites with significant ties to criminal gangs who have supported, protected, or benefitted from the ongoing security crisis and describe their criminal collusion in detail. The bill also mandates that the President impose sanctions on such actors within 90 days of the report, including through asset blocking and visa restrictions.

On June 30, 2026, Congress received the first annual report required by the Act. The report rightfully notes that “[c]ollusion between the politicians and economic elite with terrorist gangs threatens the Haitian people and viability of the Haitian State . . . fuel[ing] impunity, gang violence, and political instability.” It also underscores how this “collusion directly harms the U.S. interest in stabilizing Haiti to prevent mass and illegal immigration to U.S. shores . . . [and] also threatens U.S. citizens and embassy security.” However, the rest of the report and subsequent actions by your departments fail to show an intent to comply with the text or spirit of the law.

The June report, for example, listed only individuals who had already been sanctioned prior to the Act’s passage. Repackaging existing designations does not meet the Act’s requirement to identify those who finance and enable gang violence in Haiti. The report similarly fails to provide any new insight on the current nature or magnitude of criminal collusion in Haiti, the leadership structure of gangs and their involvement in firearms trafficking and human smuggling or the concrete actions the U.S. government will take to address these issues. Despite Secretary Rubio’s declaration in May 2025 that “the age of impunity for those supporting violence in Haiti is over”, the Administration also did not comply with the Act’s mandatory requirement that the political and economic sponsors of gangs be sanctioned by September 28, 2026. The Administration has not invoked the Act’s national security waiver nor provided any other rationale for its inaction.

The Administration has repeatedly failed to adequately engage with the committees of jurisdiction on implementation of the law. In communications to Congress, State Department representatives have confirmed that there is no working list of sanctionable targets in Haiti. The State Department has also been unable to explain why a classified annex on criminal collusion in Haiti, which was permitted by the legislation and would have addressed alleged concerns about the sensitivity of the information being requested, was not included in the June 30 Report or subsequently provided to Congress. To date, the Administration has failed to make leadership from the Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs, a representative from the U.S. Embassy in Port-Au-Prince, or personnel from the Office of Foreign Assets Control available for briefings with the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and House Foreign Affairs Committee on the Act’s implementation.

At a time when the Haitian people are preparing to vote for the first time in over a decade, Congress, the American public and the Haitian people deserve transparency about the nature and scale of collusion between gangs and their political and economic support networks. The consequences of the Administration’s silence on this issue are already evident, as at least one individual with ties to multiple gangs, Michel Martelly, is running as candidate for President despite the Organization of American States and other regional leaders calling for bans on gang-linked candidates. Past failures to confront these criminal networks helped the current crisis in Haiti take hold. Repeating them would undermine the Administration’s own goals of credible elections and security gains through the Gang Suppression Force. We demand the Administration take immediate and concrete steps to comply with the law, provide a bipartisan classified briefing on the Act’s implementation, and prioritize efforts to hold corrupt Haitian elites accountable.

###

title: Shaheen, Schatz Urge Secretary Rubio to Help Provide Relief to Palestinians in Gaza Following Destructive Floods
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Brian Schatz (D-HI), Ranking Member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on State and Foreign Operations urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to help provide relief to Palestinians in Gaza after heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents and killed at least four people, including three children, this month.

The Senators highlighted delays in getting supplies into Gaza, which the Board of Peace said has “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge,” and called on the secretary to urge the Israeli government to update its policies to allow for the timely delivery of aid as winter sets in.

“We urge you to use the leverage of the United States to ensure there is no obstacle to allowing sufficient rescue equipment, shelter, and other critical winter supplies into Gaza,” the Senators wrote. “For President Trump’s peace plan to work, we ask you to encourage the Israeli government to reevaluate its dual-use item restrictions and constraints on implementer registration that have prevented humanitarian organizations from delivering life-saving assistance.”

The Senators continued, “Just as we can all agree that Hamas must disarm and cannot again be allowed to govern Gaza, we surely agree that repairing tents, ensuring people don’t have to live in sewage, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”

Full text of the letter is available HERE and provided below.

Dear Secretary Rubio:

We write to urge you to use the resources, capabilities, and influence of the U.S. government to help provide relief to the hundreds of thousands of Palestinians displaced after heavy rain flooded more than 70,000 tents in Gaza, killing at least four people, including three children. Those affected need immediate relief, and we must implement a plan to prevent further suffering and death as winter sets in. Such life-saving assistance is not only in line with American values and U.S. law, but also in our national security interests as we seek a lasting peace in the region.

There is widespread agreement about the risk to Palestinians from flooding. On September 30, the United Nations’ International Organization for Migration published a risk assessment for the winter season warning that of the almost two million people in Gaza who need urgent shelter assistance, nearly one million are at risk of flooding in the coming months. On November 11, the UN Secretary-General deputy spokesperson stated that more than 150,000 tents, including approximately 117,000 from the Egyptian Relief Committee in El Arish, were waiting for Israeli permission to enter Gaza. President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace called the situation “an immediate humanitarian emergency,” characterizing the Israeli government’s response as “insufficient” and noting its delays “have exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge.”

On November 6, 2026, the Israeli government announced it was working on a “winterization plan” in coordination with the Board of Peace, the United Nations, international organizations, and donor countries. Since the implementation of the plan, Israel has provided more than 93,000 tents, 8,600 trucks carrying winter-specific items, and 16 sewage vacuum trucks have entered Gaza. While we welcome additional efforts, much more is needed to address basic human needs resulting from near-universal displacement in Gaza.

Although the Israeli government broadly recognizes that medical supplies, fuel, and shelter are needed to directly support the improvement of the humanitarian situation in Gaza, in practice, extensive review and approval processes can delay or block many supplies. Furthermore, Kerem Shalom remains the only crossing open for aid. According to the lead humanitarian response organizations, getting materials into Gaza is the main operational constraint, hampered by a “layered approval process, with frequent rejection of dual-use items, including basic fixing materials.” The Department of State and the Board of Peace have both expressed to Congress challenges from the Israeli government’s narrow definition of non-allowable dual-use items that includes wooden tent poles and other items critical for shelter. It is essential that key materials and supplies be delivered expeditiously and unimpeded, which is an explicit component of President Trump’s 20-point plan endorsed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Mr. Secretary, we urge you to use the leverage of the United States to ensure there is no obstacle to allowing sufficient rescue equipment, shelter, and other critical winter supplies into Gaza. For President Trump’s peace plan to work, we ask you to encourage the Israeli government to reevaluate its dual-use item restrictions and constraints on implementer registration that have prevented humanitarian organizations from delivering life-saving assistance. And we cannot simply be reactive to each preventable tragedy. Specifically, we urge you to press for:

Immediate clearance of the tents, tarpaulins, blankets, and other winter supplies already staged outside Gaza;

Israeli officials to enable UN provision of the nearly 50 percent of winter-specific deliveries that have been approved by the Israeli government and not delivered to Gaza;

A reevaluation of the security challenges that prevent expanded operations at additional crossings to allow humanitarian aid deliveries into Gaza, with the objective of opening additional crossings;

A published, pre-agreed list of essential humanitarian items exempt from dual-use review, with a timely appeals process; and

Restored operating access for experienced international humanitarian organizations.

Just as we can all agree that Hamas must disarm and cannot again be allowed to govern Gaza, we surely agree that repairing tents, ensuring people don’t have to live in sewage, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation. We urge you to use your power to continue to push for the disarmament of Hamas, while ensuring the humanitarian needs of Palestinian civilians are met in a timely and efficient manner. We respectfully request a response by December 4 describing the steps the Department is taking to enforce U.S. law and the 20-point plan with the secure entry of life-saving supplies.
