title: NEWS: New GAO Report Finds Defined Benefit Plans Have Dramatically Declined and Bold Action is Needed

committee.name: Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions

text:
WASHINGTON, Nov. 23 – According to a new Government Accountability Office (GAO) report commissioned by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), the percentage of private sector workers with a single-employer defined benefit plan has dropped dramatically from 27% in 1975 to just 5% in 2023. Even among workers who still have these pensions, the share in plans that have been partially or completely frozen, meaning they no longer accumulate benefits, rose from 18% in 2008 to 43% in 2022.

The collapse of traditional pensions has helped drive a growing retirement security crisis. Today, roughly 39% of all Americans are at risk of a financially insecure retirement — up from 31% of workers in 1983. More than 20% of seniors live on less than $15,000 of income a year and we have the highest rate of senior poverty of virtually every major country on Earth.

“This report confirms what we already know: We have a retirement crisis in America that is getting worse every day,” Sanders said. “At a time when nearly half of older workers have no retirement savings and a third of our seniors are struggling financially, Congress must restore traditional pension plans that greedy CEOs took away from millions of Americans. If we can provide defined benefit pension plans for Members of Congress that guarantee a reliable income in retirement, we can and we must provide that same type of financial security to every worker in America.”

The report details several factors that led to the decline of defined benefit pensions, but certainly one of the most important was the collapse in unionizing. According to the report, from 1977 through 2023, the share of private-sector workers who are covered by a union declined by 71%, and the share of private-sector workers who are active participants in defined benefit plans with at least 100 active participants declined by 82%. Similarly, in 2025 data shows that 55% of private-sector union workers participated in a defined benefit plan, compared with 5% of private-sector nonunion workers.

Congress could dramatically reverse this decline in defined benefit plans by requiring all companies to offer their workers the same type of pension that every member of Congress receives. The Pensions for All Act that Senator Sanders introduced this Congress would do just that. Specifically, this bill would require companies to:

Provide a traditional pension plan for their workers that is at least equivalent to the plan provided to new members of Congress under the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS), or

Pay into the federal retirement system at a level that ensures all of their workers receive the same amount of retirement benefits as Members of Congress.

title: Peters Criticizes Chairman Paul for Limiting Scrutiny of 13 Trump Nominees at Rushed Hearing ➞

committee.name: Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs

text:
Paul Refused to Allow Ranking Member Peters to Deliver Opening Remarks, Restricted Senators’ Time to Question Nominees for Critical National Security and Oversight Positions

WASHINGTON, D.C. – At a Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee nominations hearing, Ranking Member Gary Peters (D-MI) slammed Chairman Rand Paul (R-KY) for forcing through a rushed process on 13 nominees for critical national security and government oversight positions. The panel included the nominee to serve as Comptroller General of the Government Accountability Office (GAO), even though the Senate only received that nomination three days ago. During the hearing, Senators’ time to ask questions of the nominees was severely restricted, and senators were not permitted to ask additional rounds of questions of the nominees. Chairman Paul also refused to allow Peters to deliver his opening statement at the start of the hearing, denying the Committee’s Ranking Member the opportunity to raise serious concerns about several nominees before questioning began.

“The way this hearing is being conducted is a complete disservice to these nominees and to the American people,” said Senator Peters during the hearing. “It’s so transparent that this is a box-checking exercise. This Committee is not doing its due diligence, despite some of our members’ best efforts, because the Chairman has chosen to not carry out his responsibility to provide advice and consent on nominations.”

Peters continued: “I cannot possibly detail all the ways these nominees are being rushed through the confirmation process, but we need to talk about how shocking the process is for the nominee of the Comptroller General of the Government Accountability Office. GAO is an independent, nonpartisan watchdog that conducts investigations and audits for Congress. It’s a position that serves Congress and Congress alone. There is a bipartisan, bicameral process required by law that ensures that all Members of Congress, the people who rely on GAO to support their oversight and their accountability efforts, have a seat at the table when it comes to selecting the candidate for this important role.”

“Not only is Eric Ueland not a bipartisan choice, he is not even Congress’s choice. He was hand selected by President Trump and nominated three days ago without ever speaking to a single Member of Congress about that potential nomination,” said Peters.

“Now, I recognize Mr. Ueland is a longtime public servant, but his record as the top official of the Office of Management and Budget, an agency that routinely flouts Congressional oversight, has stonewalled GAO audits and defied Congress’s constitutional authority to direct spending, undercuts any credibility he could possibly have to lead the GAO. Someone with this partisan record deserves more scrutiny, not less,” continued Peters.

“So I urge all my colleagues to reject efforts to short circuit careful consideration of any nomination, and to instead push for a robust process that ensures the American people actually get the right people for these incredibly important jobs. The American people deserve no less. As a Congress, we should be delivering that,” concluded Peters.

WATCH: Ranking Member Peters’ comments about the sham nominations process at today’s hearing.

READ: Peters’ full opening statement as prepared for delivery.

WATCH: Peters’ Questions to GAO Comptroller General Nominee Eric Ueland.

Today’s hearing included nominees to lead the Government Accountability Office (GAO), the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Office of Government Ethics (OGE), and several agency Inspectors General offices, all positions charged with protecting national security, rooting out corruption, and ensuring independent oversight of the executive branch.

BACKGROUND ON THE GAO COMPTROLLER GENERAL NOMINATION PROCESS

As required by law, a 10-member bipartisan, bicameral Commission recommends at least three candidates, and the President chooses a nominee from the Commission’s recommendations. The bipartisan Commission is made up of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the majority and minority leaders of the House and Senate, the Chair and Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and the Chair and Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. Since 1980, when Congress established the current Comptroller General nomination process, every Comptroller General has been selected with strong bipartisan approval and no Comptroller General was serving in the executive branch as a political appointee when nominated.

Below is a timeline of the actions taken on the current Comptroller General nomination:

May 19, 2025: HSGAC minority staff reach out to HSGAC majority staff about starting the commission selection process. Despite repeated requests over the following 18 months, HSGAC majority staff never responded.

December 29, 2025: Comptroller General Gene Dodaro’s term ends.

November 11, 2026, 12:06 pm: The White House informed GAO that it planned to nominate Eric Ueland, the current Deputy Director for Management at the Office of Management and Budget, to be Comptroller General. At 12:06 p.m. GAO received an email from the White House confirming Mr. Ueland will be the nominee and providing nominations paperwork.

November 11, 2026, 1:20 pm: HSGAC Chairman Paul’s staff emailed HSGAC minority staff asking for recommendations of candidates to include on the commission’s list by 8 am the following day. House Oversight Ranking Member Garcia’s staff received the same request that afternoon. This was the first written communication from HSGAC majority to minority commission members or staff regarding the Comptroller General selection process. The other minority members of the commission did not receive any outreach from Chairman Paul asking for input.

November 12, 2026, 9:28 am: Chairman Paul noticed a hearing for “a nominee to be Comptroller General” on November 19, 2026.

November 12, 2026: Chairman Paul sent a letter to the White House recommending three Comptroller General candidates, including Eric Ueland. The letter was signed by only the majority members of the commission.

November 16, 2026: President Trump nominated Eric Ueland to serve as Comptroller General.

title: House Democrats Demand Answers from Trump on NVIDIA

committee.name: House Committee on Energy and Commerce

text:
House Democratic Committee leaders wrote to President Trump today demanding answers about what he knew and when he knew it regarding NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected agent of the Chinese government.

The letter was sent by Energy and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ), Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (D-NY), Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Jamie Raskin (D-MD), and Oversight and Government Reform Committee Ranking Member Robert Garcia (D-CA).

“We write regarding the irresponsible risks that you and those in your Administration have taken by reportedly ignoring information that the CEO of NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, may have been compromised by an agent of the Chinese government and then directly involving yourself in his reinstatement as CEO,” the Democratic Committee leaders wrote to President Trump.

Reports indicate President Trump was made aware Huang may have been compromised by an agent of the Chinese government before the news of his affair was made public. Despite being alerted to this risk, Trump invited Huang with him on Air Force One on a trip to China. Additionally, Mr. Huang apparently remains a member of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. On Monday, NVIDIA’s board of directors reinstated Huang as CEO, apparently after Trump participated in the board's meeting to advocate for his return.

Trump initially denied being informed in May about the national security risks posed by Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, but he has since stated, “They could have been mentioned. Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me.”

“Regardless of whether your memory is faulty or simply selective, the risks to the country remain. Your personal relationship with Mr. Huang and your willful blindness to the economic and national security risks posed by this scandal have put the American people at great risk,” the Democrats continued. “As Ranking Members of committees in the House of Representatives with jurisdiction over aspects of commerce, civil and criminal law, artificial intelligence, and foreign relations, it is imperative that we be informed as to what you knew and when you knew it in order to assess and take any legislative action necessary to address the risks posed by this situation.”

The Democratic Committee leaders requested answers to a series of questions, including:

When was Trump first made aware of evidence that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang was in a relationship with a suspected agent of the Chinese government, and who informed him?

Upon learning that Huang was in a relationship with a suspected agent of the Chinese government, what actions, if any, did Trump take to limit risks to America’s economic and national security?

Are Huang’s relationship with a suspected agent of the Chinese government or his lobbying of Trump or his Administration under investigation? If not, why not?

The Democratic Committee leaders also asked for all communications between Trump, the Vice President, White House officials, or senior administration officials and the NVIDIA Board of Directors between Huang's resignation as CEO on November 12, 2026, and his reinstatement on November 23, 2026.

Read the full letter HERE.

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Blasts Trump Over Dismal Housing Numbers, Demands Immediate Action to End Housing Affordability Crisis
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the statement below after new housing data was released showing the continued housing market freeze, including home sales falling to their lowest since the Great Recession and new housing starts plummeting. Mortgage rates are over 7 percent for over eight consecutive weeks, while consumer and home prices continue to increase, locking many out from buying a home.

“The recent dismal housing numbers should set off alarm bells in the White House. Home sales have plunged to their lowest levels since the Great Recession, mortgage rates remain above 7 percent, and home prices have soared more than 50 percent since the pandemic. Young Americans are stuck in their parents' basements, first-time buyers are being shut out, and families are putting their dreams of homeownership on hold.

“Yet instead of confronting this crisis, Trump is pursuing policies that threaten to make it worse. His tariffs are driving up the cost of building new homes and his Administration has slashed HUD's workforce, weakened fair housing enforcement, and put critical housing assistance at risk. These intentional decisions from the Administration make it harder to build affordable homes, protect families from discrimination, and help Americans stay housed. And while families struggle to afford a roof over their heads, the President remains preoccupied with renovations to his White House ballroom and Washington, DC golf courses. Even when Democrats and Republicans came together to pass landmark housing legislation, he refused to sign it.

“Congress has taken important steps to address this crisis, including enacting the landmark bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Now, the Trump Administration must take a hard look at the consequences of its own policies and change course. That means reversing policies that make housing more expensive and undermine critical housing assistance, fully implementing the reforms authorized under the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, and working with Congress to provide the federal funding and support needed to build, repair, and preserve homes that families can afford. The housing crisis demands a comprehensive response, and the American people deserve nothing less.”

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Demands Answers Following Jensen Huang’s Reinstatement as NVIDIA CEO Amid National Security Concerns and Trump’s Intervention
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the following statement following NVIDIA’s decision to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as Chief Executive Officer amid ongoing investigations into potential Chinese espionage, export-control violations, and reports of President Donald Trump’s direct intervention in the company’s decision.

“NVIDIA’s rushed decision to reinstate Jensen Huang before completing its investigation into potential Chinese espionage is reckless and demands immediate accountability. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the board have yet to answer serious questions about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls and the potential transfer of sensitive American technology to China. Trump’s intervention also raises serious conflicts of interest concerns given NVIDIA’s reported $25 million contribution to his White House ballroom project, Trump’s reported personal holding in NVIDIA stock (which is reportedly among his top three holdings), and more than 100 transactions involving the company’s shares. Now, his Administration is offering assurances behind closed doors to justify reinstating the company’s CEO, despite unresolved and alarming national security concerns. And given the timing of the announcement, there are reports others may have cashed in too through insider trading.

“Committee Democrats have worked across the aisle to strengthen our national security laws. We must bring that same urgency to closing export-control loopholes, strengthening enforcement, and preventing powerful corporations from undermining safeguards designed to keep advanced American technology out of China's hands. NVIDIA's political connections cannot exempt it from the law, and this Administration cannot allow corporate influence to make decisions affecting our national security.”

title: December 1st @ 2 PM : Ranking Member Maxine Waters and Committee Democrats, Hold First Hearing Following Historic Democratic Blue Tsunami to Examine Trump’s Assault on CFPB Amid Affordability Crisis
text:
As Democrats prepare to reclaim the House majority following November’s historic elections, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, announced that the full Committee will hold a Minority Day Hearing on Tuesday, December 1st at 2:00 p.m. ET. Committee Democratic Members secured this hearing when former Acting Director of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), Russell Vought, testified before the Committee in July for a long-overdue statutory hearing.

This will be the first congressional hearing led by Democrats following the historic Blue Tsunami. The hearing will expose the full extent of the damage inflicted on the CFPB by the Trump Administration and Congressional Republicans, including mass staffing cuts, slashed budget, abandoned enforcement actions, weakened oversight, and rolled-back consumer protections. Most notably, this hearing will lay the groundwork for swift action under a Democratic majority in the next Congress to rebuild the Bureau and put a strong Federal watchdog back on the beat to protect consumers in the financial marketplace.

Americans have made their concerns about affordability loud and clear, and Committee Democrats are ready to take real action to confront the threats to Americans' financial security, protect their hard-earned money, and hold bad actors in our financial system accountable.

title: Meeks Calls for Public HFAC Hearing with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang
text:

title: Ranking Members Meeks, Castro Call on Cuba to Release Political Prisoners
text:
Washington, DC — Representatives Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Joaquin Castro, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere, sent a letter to Miguel Díaz-Canel Bermúdez urging the Cuban government to release more than 200 political prisoners to help break the impasse in stalled talks between the United States and Cuba. The letter comes after reports that senior Trump Administration officials met with Cuban government officials on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in September 2026.

An excerpt of the letter is below. A copy of the letter is available here.

“We write to urge your government to release the more than 200 political prisoners whose cases have been discussed in recent exchanges between Cuba and the United States. At a moment of profound hardship for the Cuban people and an impasse in bilateral diplomacy, their release would reflect a significant humanitarian act and an important step toward a more constructive dialogue and relationship between our countries.

“We have long believed human rights is central to our policy towards Cuba. Our support for engagement has always been based on the premise that the United States can better advance its serious concerns regarding arbitrary detention, restrictions on peaceful expression and assembly, and the absence of adequate protections for due process through diplomacy. We believe that the decades of sanctions-have failed to advance these goals and that only diplomacy can help address these concerns while advancing the interests and well-being of both our peoples.

(. . .)

“Such a decision would be a sovereign act within your government’s authority, consistent with international law and the dignity and aspirations of the Cuban people. It would demonstrate confidence in Cuba’s future and strengthen the case made by those of us in Congress who believe that engagement and expanded economic opportunity offer a better path forward for both the Cuban and American people. Although no single measure can resolve the longstanding differences between our countries, this one could go a long way toward building trust and creating political space for meaningful progress that can ease the humanitarian crisis 9 million Cubans endure on a daily basis.”

title: Ranking Members Meeks, Shaheen Call on Trump Administration to Implement and Enforce Bipartisan Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act
text:
Washington, DC – Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Senator Jeanne Shaheen, Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth demanding full implementation of the bipartisan Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which was signed into law on December 18, 2025.

In the letter, the Ranking Members demand answers about the Administration’s failure to fully implement the law, which Secretary Rubio championed during his time in the Senate, and question how this failure is consistent with the Trump Administration’s stated priorities of using sanctions and other tools to target Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs) and their support networks in our hemisphere. The Ranking Members reiterate the urgency of implementing this legislation amid Haiti’s worsening security and humanitarian situation. They also request a bipartisan classified briefing on what steps the Administration will take to ensure timely implementation and enforcement of the law.

Full text of the letter is available HERE.

“Under the Haiti Criminal Collusion Transparency Act, which Secretary Rubio led as the Republican sponsor when he was a Senator, the State Department is required to work with the interagency to submit an annual report identifying Haitian political and economic elites with significant ties to criminal gangs who have supported, protected, or benefitted from the ongoing security crisis and describe their criminal collusion in detail,” wrote the Ranking Members.

title: Ranking Member Raskin Demands Records From Four Companies Linked to Don Jr.’s 1789 Capital That Received Suspiciously Well-Timed Government Favors
text:
Washington, D.C. (November 24, 2026)—Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, expanded his investigation into Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, demanding records from Hadrian Automation, Juul Labs, Polymarket, and GrabAGun. The probe examines whether the President’s son and his business partners helped steer federal contracts or regulatory decisions to companies in which they had a significant financial interest or used advance knowledge of those forthcoming decisions to make investments and profit.

“1789 Capital’s striking success in predicting both the imminent award of government contracts and the release of favorable regulatory actions to its portfolio or affiliated companies suggests that either (1) Donald Trump Jr. suddenly acquired and brought to 1789 Capital magical new clairvoyant powers that catapulted him to the position of the greatest investor of all time, or (2) we are witnessing a brazen conspiracy to use the machinery of the executive branch of government under the control of President Trump to rig both public policy and the markets in order to enrich the First Family beyond the wildest dreams of any other presidential family, not to mention the vast majority of Americans,” wrote Ranking Member Raskin.

Ranking Member Raskin opened the investigation in August after 1789 Capital repeatedly invested in companies shortly before they received major federal contracts, funding, or favorable regulatory decisions. Trump Jr. joined the firm four days after the 2024 election. Since then, assets under its management have climbed from roughly $150 million to $3 billion, and its main fund posted a roughly 200% return as of June 2026. In its September response to the Committee, 1789 Capital denied using political influence and invoked national security to defend its investments, without explaining how backing companies that create betting markets for measles cases and military operations makes the nation more secure.

The expanded investigation zeroes in on four companies tied to 1789 Capital (or its principals) that have benefited, or stand to benefit, from Trump Administration contracts, regulatory decisions, or proposed rule changes:

Hadrian Automation: In March 2026, two months after 1789 Capital acquired a stake in Hadrian, the U.S. Navy announced a “novel transaction” committing $900 million to the upstart company to manufacture submarine components. Nearly simultaneously, the U.S. Army awarded the company a manufacturing contract with a total cumulative value of $80 million. In July 2026, Hadrian CEO Chris Power gave nearly $500,000 in one day to the Republican National Committee and its legal fund. Four days later, President Trump issued an executive order aimed at increasing Pentagon reliance on domestic manufacturers, which Power called a “big win”. In August 2026, 1789 Capital increased its stake in a round that valued Hadrian at nearly $8 billion, up from just $1.6 billion earlier that year.

Juul Labs: In March 2025, 1789 Capital quietly acquired a $5 million stake in Juul, which had drawn massive backlash for developing and marketing flavors that target and appeal to teenagers. Responding to the furor, the FDA had issued in 2022 a marketing denial order which nearly bankrupted the company. Four months after 1789 Capital’s surprising investment, the FDA dramatically reversed course and authorized the marketing of five JUUL products, including menthol pods. In May 2026, The Wall Street Journalreported that President Trump pressed then-FDA Commissioner Marty Makary to move faster on flavored vapes. In August 2026, the FDA authorized three more JUUL products, and Juul announced plans to seek authorization for flavors beyond tobacco and menthol.

Polymarket: Federal regulators imposed a $1.4 million penalty on Polymarket in 2022 for operating an unregistered trading platform. In July 2025, the Justice Department and Commodity Futures Trading Commission closed their investigations into the company. Days later, Polymarket announced the $112 million purchase of a federally licensed exchange and clearinghouse, clearing a path for them back into the U.S. market. The company disclosed 1789 Capital’s investment the following month. The firm is now reportedly leading a funding round that would value Polymarket at $21 billion, up from a reported $300 million when it first invested—meaning that 1789 Capital will have seen an astonishing return of 4,900% or 50 times its original investment during President Trump’s time in office.

GrabAGun: The online firearms retailer went public in July 2025 through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company affiliated with 1789 Capital’s principals. The acquisition company’s board included 1789 Capital co-founders Omeed Malik and Christopher Buskirk, with Trump Jr. joining GrabAGun’s board following the merger. In May 2026, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives proposed a rule that would make it much easier for online retailers to ship firearms directly to customers. While GrabAGun told investors it was “uniquely positioned to capitalize on this potential opportunity,” the National Shooting Sports Foundation--the firearms industry’s largest trade association—opposed it, warning that the rule would enable firearms sales to “prohibited persons, straw purchasers, and illegal firearm traffickers.”

Ranking Member Raskin is demanding records dating back to November 1, 2024, including communications with or about 1789 Capital and records of meetings and calls with Trump Jr., Malik, Buskirk, and other firm representatives. The letters to Hadrian, Juul, Polymarket, and GrabAGun also seek term sheets, investment agreements, valuations, and due diligence files exchanged with 1789 Capital. Ranking Member Raskin directed all four companies to preserve responsive records, including messages on Signal, WhatsApp, and Telegram, and to identify any deletions and certify whether they complied with company retention policies.

“The House Judiciary Committee is committed to ensuring that public officials and their families cannot profit from and exploit inside government information and insider access. The American people demand and expect nothing less,” wrote Ranking Member Raskin.

title: Ranking Members Larsen, Carson, House Democrats to FAA: SMART Rollout Must Be Safe and Transparent

committee.name: House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure

text:
Washington, D.C.—Today, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure Rick Larsen (D-WA), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Aviation André Carson (D-IN), Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and April McClain Delaney (D-MD) and 20 Democratic Members sent a letter to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator Bryan Bedford expressing serious concern with the FAA’s nationwide expansion of the AI-powered Strategic Management of Airspace Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system. The FAA expanded SMART to Air Route Traffic Control Centers (ARTCCs) across the country starting on November 10, 2026, without prior notification to Congress, before a planned 90-day validation period in the National Capital Region could be completed, and despite a lack of clear safety and performance metrics. Recent credible reporting also suggests that the FAA may have engaged in retaliatory behavior against employees who raised safety concerns regarding SMART’s expansion.

“We are alarmed by the FAA’s announcement that its AI-powered flight routing software, dubbed SMART, was deployed across the national airspace on November 10, 2026 without any advance public disclosure or Congressional notification,” the members wrote. “…This action raises concerns regarding the transparency of air traffic control (ATC) modernization efforts and FAA leadership’s commitment to prioritizing aviation safety above all else.”

“Disturbingly…the FAA may be engaging in retaliatory behavior against employees who raised safety concerns about SMART’s rapid deployment…[which could] fundamentally undermine the FAA’s safety culture,” the members continued.

“It is unacceptable that the FAA failed to keep Congress apprised of radical changes to the scope of SMART’s deployment,” the members wrote. “We have yet to receive any substantive information proving the system was properly validated before its nationwide expansion….”

The members concluded with several questions regarding the FAA’s expansion, validation, and training processes, and demanding transparency from the FAA.

title: Chairmen Mast, Moolenaar, Crawford, And Senator Ricketts Applaud Treasury For Strengthening COINS Act Rule
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast, Senator Pete Ricketts, House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence Chairman Rick Crawford, and House Select Committee on the CCP Chairman John Moolenaar sent a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent applauding the Department's proposed rule to implement the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security (COINS) Act of 2025. The chairmen urge the administration to go further in stopping U.S. capital from fueling China's military-industrial complex.

“We applaud President Trump and Secretary Bessent’s leadership in stopping the People’s Republic of China (PRC) from exploiting U.S. capital and know-how to advance its military-industrial complex and strategic technologies,” said Chairmen Mast, Moolenaar, and Crawford. “The Department of Treasury’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to implement the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025 is a historic step toward maintaining and expanding America’s lead in the technologies that will determine leadership in this century.” They also urge the Administration to:

Deepen biotech restrictions to prevent the offshoring of U.S. drug development and target licensing deals that speed up the growth of China's biotech industry to the detriment of American biotech leadership.

Target publicly traded securities, including index funds, ETFs, and mutual funds, as well as restricting access to U.S. capital for PRC tech giants tied to the Chinese military industrial complex.

Add new sectors, including robotics, aerospace and space technologies, advanced manufacturing, and directed energy.

Prohibit foundational semiconductor investments that could give China a new supply chain chokehold over the American economy.

Address management consulting by U.S. firms that helps shape Chinese industrial policy and research priorities.

title: Endorsements Roll In for Select Committee’s Biotech Policy Recommendations

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
Endorsements from the private sector are rolling in for the policy recommendations in the Select Committee on China’s new report, Prescription America: How to Protect Americans from a Dangerous Dependence on China for Their Medicines.

The report contrasts U.S. drug development with China’s heavily subsidized, ethically questionable drug industry, and recommends policies to protect U.S. pharmaceutical innovation and keep clinical trials from moving to China to evade American rules and ethical standards. The report has gained significant endorsements from industry leaders.

JOE LONSDALE, FOUNDER AND MANAGING PARTNER, 8VC:

"The committee's report hits the nail on the head. Government leaders must fight back against China's attempt to dominate global biotech and the US drug supply chain by cheating on US regulations and stealing IP. Chinese companies licensing or selling drugs into the US should face the same treatment US companies experience in China, not a perverse double standard that favors them over US companies. At the same time, we need to accelerate US drug development by adopting other countries' best practices in FDA regulation, and bringing in top US AI talent to speed up the FDA. All involved need to raise the pace and quality of US research to deliver better treatments to patients at ever lower costs."

JASON KELLY, FOUNDER AND CEO, GINGKO BIOWORKS:

“Biotechnology is one of the most valuable and national security-relevant frontier technologies and the US is in the process of rapidly offshoring it to China. The clear recommendations in this report must be implemented quickly to protect the US frontier bio labs and save the US from a much more costly and dangerous attempt to reshore this technology when it’s too late in a conflict.”

TOM EISIMINGER JR., PRESIDENT & CEO, REGENESIS MEDICAL:

"In the Army, you learn never to let the mission depend on a supply line someone else can cut. The same discipline belongs in medicine. Too many of us are trading long-term resilience for short-term speed and savings, and the patients we serve, veterans included, are the ones who pay if that goes wrong. [Like this report], everyone in our industry should read Apple in China and learn from it: dependence builds one reasonable decision at a time, and it is far easier to protect a strategic advantage than to rebuild one after it's gone. We still have time to choose differently."

DAVID BEARSS, PHD, CEO, HALIA THERAPEUTICS:

“Through my more than 25-year career, I’ve been involved in the discovery of 18 drugs that have moved into the clinic and run trials across North America, Europe, the Middle East, India, China, Japan, and Australia. Speed and cost matter, but only if the data can be trusted. This report is a wake-up call. We welcome every country’s biotech industry, but everyone should compete on the same ethical and quality playing field. That requires full transparency for every patient dosed, whether in an investigator-initiated trial or an IND study: the data, the adverse events, the consent forms, and sites open to FDA inspection.”

KARTHIK MUSUNURI, FOUNDER, BIOTECHFIRST:

“Our nation invented the very idea of modern biotechnology. It is a national inheritance that we built, lab by lab and patient by patient, by generations who believed that a cure discovered in America is a promise kept to the world. Today that promise is at risk through a thousand quiet concessions to convenience and short-term gain. For far too long, we have steadily outsourced our sovereignty by growing ever so reliant on therapies found in other nations. Biotechnology must be a national priority and a patriotic trust. Tomorrow’s cures must be imagined, built, and delivered by Americans, for Americans. I commend the House Select Committee on China for sounding this alarm, and I urge every American to read its report and ask what inheritance we intend to leave."

JAMES BURKE, MD, HEMATOLOGIST AND ONCOLOGIST AND CHIEF MEDICAL OFFICER , KALIVIR IMMUNOTHERAPEUTICS:

“As an oncologist I have designed successful clinical programs for biotech companies which have been implemented globally. As well, I have led the treatment of patients in initial phase 1 trials through pivotal registration phase 3 studies world-wide (including in APAC and mainland China), and I support your effort and this [report] specifically. I want to add that I really feel we must go even further...If any drug developers desire to access to the US market, they must acknowledge and respect the US regulatory environment and funnel back resources to continue to preserve and build our own drug development ecosystem—not China's. I encourage more direct requirements for US based patient accrual and infrastructure expansion from any clinical trial efforts with a goal of eventually reaching the US market. We hold this leverage and we should use it. Of course, we should also look at China's push to dominate the biotech/pharma space as a wake-up call and opportunity to re-examine our drug development strategies and implement efficiencies with renewed investment to shore up weaknesses."

CHRISTOPHER LOCHER, PHD, CEO AND FOUNDER OF VERSATOPE THERAPEUTICS, INC. :

“Small-company biotech innovation in the US is slipping. US biotechs raised about $4.3B in venture capital in Q1 2026, roughly a third less than a year earlier, and more of it is going into a few $100M+ rounds. Meanwhile, US companies pay an estimated $7.5B a year to Chinese-owned CROs, and Chinese biotechs signed a record ~$60B in licensing deals last quarter. Congress can’t assume this fixes itself. No policy will be perfect, but the VCs and pharma companies fighting hardest against restrictions should disclose their own investments in China.”

SAM RASTY, PHD., GM AND HEAD OF FYNDERBIO:

“There is increasing amounts of capital from big pharma and venture capital investors flowing into early-stage Chinese biotech companies that is rivaling the capital going to private US biotechs. This trend won’t reverse itself or self-correct anytime soon unless we enact policies that embolden and re-energize the growth of the biotech industry here at home. The newly introduced bipartisan Faster Clinical Trials Act in Congress is one such measure that could help level the playing field, boost drug discovery and development in the US and speed up the attractiveness of US biotech assets for pharma and VC investors.”

title: ICYMI: House Passes Select Committee-Supported Legislation Cracking Down on China-Linked Scam Centers

committee.name: House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party

text:
In case you missed it last week, the House passed Select Committee on China-supported legislation cracking down on China-linked scam centers. H.R.5490 – the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act led by Select Committee on China Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Congressman Jefferson Shreve (R-IN) establishes a federal task force to shut down the China-linked criminal syndicates ripping off Americans and stealing their life savings.

"Thank you to my colleagues for their strong bipartisan support of this Select Committee-supported bill. Working with Congressman Shreve and our Democratic colleagues we have passed important legislation that will go after the ruthless China-linked scam centers ripping off Americans. My committee led a bipartisan investigation into these scam centers and exposed how they are stealing more than $10 billion a year from American families. The Senate should quickly advance this legislation and put it on President Trump’s desk for him to sign into law,” said Moolenaar.

In May, Moolenaar and Select Committee Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) released a bipartisan investigation into China-linked scam centers. Crime, Corruption, and Power: CCP-Linked Transnational Crime and the Rise of a Distributed Threat to U.S. National Security, exposing a China-linked scam center network that has defrauded Americans of at least $10 billion annually while fueling human trafficking, cybercrime, and illicit finance.

“These scam centers with deep links to China are a broad network of fraud, human trafficking, cybercrime, and illicit finance that are ripping off Americans and threatening our national security,” warned Moolenaar at the time. “If the Chinese government wanted to act against these criminals, it could, but it chooses not to.”

“This investigation is about standing up for the millions of Americans who have lost billions of dollars to these scams, as well as the human trafficking victims who have been lured into scam compounds by China-linked crime syndicates. Verifiable bilateral cooperation with Beijing, alongside engagement with and funding for civil society groups, is essential to getting justice and compensation for victims of CCP-linked transnational fraud and holding these scammers accountable,” said Khanna when the report was released.

The Select Committee found that the scam centers concentrated in southeast Asia, particularly in Cambodia and Burma, are part of a distributed criminal ecosystem linking cyber fraud, human trafficking, and money laundering.

Rather than direct state control or any state-backed conspiracy, the report concludes that Chinese governance and enforcement patterns have enabled the growth of these criminal networks. Their operations rely heavily on Chinese underground banking networks, cryptocurrency brokers, and shell companies to move and launder funds across borders. The report highlights the widespread use of trafficked labor, with thousands of individuals coerced into conducting scams under threat of violence inside fortified compounds.

title: Ways and Means Legislation Signed into Law to Crack Down on Counterfeit Goods

committee.name: House Committee on Ways and Means

text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — American workers, families, and businesses will have stronger protections against the importation of fake and pirated goods under bipartisan legislation advanced by the Ways and Means Committee and now signed into law by President Trump. The Counterfeit Notification Act (H.R. 4930), introduced by Representative Blake Moore (UT-01), gives U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) explicit authority to share critical information about suspected counterfeit shipments with the businesses that can help identify fake products and stop them from reaching consumers, such as U.S. innovators who have developed safe products and trusted brands. Previously, CBP lacked certainty about what information it could share with outside partners, limiting the agency’s ability to harness the expertise of American businesses to identify counterfeit goods coming into our country that rip off consumers and hurt American workers.

Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith (MO-08) issued the following statement:

“American workers and businesses should not have to compete against foreign criminals flooding our markets with cheap knockoffs, stealing American ideas, and ripping off consumers. Counterfeit goods rob American inventors of their hard work, threaten American jobs, and can put dangerous products in the hands of unsuspecting American families. For years, CBP has asked for clear authority to share information with the American businesses that can help identify fake products and keep them out of our markets. The Counterfeit Notification Act delivers clear authority to CBP officials so they can utilize the expertise of American businesses to catch counterfeiters and stop fraudulent goods from entering our country. Securing our ports of entry and standing up for the American innovators and workers who power our economy has long been a priority of the Ways and Means Committee and this Congress. Thanks to Representative Moore’s leadership and President Trump’s commitment to protecting Americans by signing this legislation into law, CBP can partner with American businesses in the fight against counterfeit goods.”

Representative Blake Moore (UT-01) issued the following statement:

“I am thrilled to see my bill, the Counterfeit Notification Act, signed into law. This bill gives CBP additional authority to stop counterfeit and pirated imports from making their way into the United States, protecting American businesses from counterfeiters, IP thieves, and black-market traders. I am proud to have worked with my Ways and Means colleagues, Representatives Adrian Smith and Brad Schneider, and Senators Grassley and Hassan to get this bill across the finish line.”

The bill passed the Ways and Means Committee by a vote of 40 to 0, passed the House by voice vote, and passed the Senate by unanimous consent.

Counterfeit Notification Act (H.R. 4930):

In FY 2025, CBP seized nearly 79 million counterfeit products. The products would have been worth $7.3 billion had they been genuine.

The law expands the information CBP can share with relevant, trusted stakeholders to include images of suspected counterfeit products and their packaging, shipping labels, tracking numbers, and invoices – details that help trace counterfeit goods back to their source.

The law expands who can receive that information to include intellectual property rights holders, e-commerce platforms, and shipping carriers. These partners can help CBP confirm whether a shipment is legitimate and remove counterfeit products from American supply chains sooner.

Read a fact sheet on the bill here.

title: Joint statement from Senators Coons, Warren, Wyden, Reed, Cantwell on Nvidia decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

committee.name: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.), Banking Committee Ranking Member Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Armed Services Committee Ranking Member Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Commerce Committee Ranking Member Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) released the following statement after Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO:

“Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, while grave questions about national security concerns and the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls remain unanswered, is deeply troubling.

“Even more alarming, President Trump has acknowledged personally intervening on Huang’s behalf, and Nvidia has acknowledged that it received ‘input from senior levels of the United States government’ in reaching its decision. The American people deserve to know why the president intervened in this extraordinary manner, whether serious counterintelligence or national security concerns were disregarded, and whose interests this intervention was intended to serve.

“This administration must immediately provide Congress with a full accounting of its role in Huang’s return. In particular:

Which administration officials engaged Nvidia or its board about Huang’s return, and what assurances or commitments did they give?

What intelligence assessments informed that advocacy, which national security agencies were consulted, and on what basis was Huang’s return judged to pose no national security risk?

When did the president, the vice president, and other senior officials first learn of Huang’s relationship and the associated counterintelligence or national security concerns, and what actions did they take?

What did the administration know about Nvidia’s compliance with U.S. export controls, including whether Nvidia or its executives engaged in potential violations of U.S. law?

What safeguards, if any, protect Americans’ security going forward?

“We expect the administration to respond fully and promptly to our Republican colleagues’ requests for classified briefings and information on this matter. Congress and the American people are owed answers, and we intend to get them, in January, if not before.

“U.S. national security must not be sacrificed to protect powerful technology executives. Protecting America’s technological leadership and preventing China’s exploitation of our most sensitive technologies are bipartisan responsibilities. The Trump administration must explain its actions to Congress and the American people and make clear whose interests it is serving.”

title: Wyden Slams Bogus HHS Fraud Report Used to Justify Stripping Protections from Unaccompanied Children
text:
Finance Ranking Member Demands Records Behind Flawed Memo Used to Justify Cuts to Legal Aid and Anti-Trafficking Protections

Text of the Letter (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., today blasted Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. over a flawed agency report being used by the Trump administration to strip legal aid and safety protections from unaccompanied immigrant children.

“The Memorandum is the clear result of a bad-faith investigation and bogus analytical foundation which lead to unsupported conclusions that call for predetermined policy changes long sought by the Trump administration,” Wyden wrote. “Children in ORR care will spend longer in federal custody, be released to fewer qualified sponsors, lose access to the counsel Congress required, and face immigration proceedings with fewer of the protections Congress enacted specifically for them.”

The report from the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR), released last month, claims to show widespread fraud among adults who sponsor unaccompanied children. In his letter, Wyden detailed how HHS relied on a cherry-picked sample that represents less than 2 percent of the more than 100,000 sponsor releases. HHS then extrapolated its findings to make sweeping claims about the entire program. The report also lists three conflicting fraud rates without explaining how HHS calculated the numbers.

Wyden also called out HHS for using a backlog of 65,000 unanswered child welfare reports as a political talking point, noting that the backlog reflects ORR’s own failure to review and respond to reports from care providers. The agency simultaneously ordered providers to stop directly reporting suspected child trafficking to the Office on Trafficking in Persons (OTIP), undercutting the very protections Congress built to keep kids safe. Wyden spotlighted this OTIP directive last month.

Lastly, the letter highlights HHS’s companion “Claim vs. Reality” document, which falsely claims that having a government contractor appear as a “friend of the court,” rather than as counsel of record, satisfies the HHS’s statutory obligation to provide legal representation to unaccompanied children.

Wyden demanded that HHS preserve all records related to the report within seven business days and provide answers about how the report was initiated and produced, how the agency plans to clear the growing backlog of unanswered child welfare reports accumulating on Trump and Robert Kennedy’s watch, and the current status of legal representation for unaccompanied minors in HHS custody.

The text of the letter is here.
