title: Ranking Member Shaheen, Senator Cruz Condemn Nicaragua’s Rejection of Unanimously Confirmed U.S. Ambassador
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Ted Cruz (R-TX) released the below statement condemning the Ortega-Murillo regime for its ongoing autocratic abuses, including its recent decision to decline to credential Natasha Franceschi, who was unanimously confirmed by the U.S. Senate to be Ambassador to Nicaragua.

Ambassador-designate Franceschi’s confirmation followed a hearing by the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee on Western Hemisphere, Transnational Crime, Civilian Security, Democracy, Human Rights and Global Women’s Issues titled “Nicaragua’s Political Crisis: Ortega’s Assault on Democracy,” where a panel of experts testified regarding the regime’s human rights violations against its own citizens.

“On September 30, the Senate unanimously confirmed Natasha Franceschi to be U.S. Ambassador to Nicaragua. The Ortega-Murillo regime’s subsequent refusal to accept Ambassador Franceschi to lead Embassy Managua is yet another example of the dictatorship’s unwillingness to engage in dialogue with international partners. The U.S. Senate acted decisively in support of Ambassador-designate Franceschi, a career diplomat with more than 25 years of experience, to represent U.S. interests in Nicaragua. By rejecting her credentials, the Ortega-Murillo regime only further isolates itself and compounds its own problems.

“The regime’s illegal detentions, torture, disproportionately violent responses to peaceful demonstrations and intolerance of a free press have aligned it with America’s adversaries, including China, Russia and Iran. We stand in support of the Nicaraguan people’s right to free and fair elections, freedom of religion, peaceful protests and freedom of speech. We urge the international community to continue pressuring the regime back toward democracy and diplomacy and away from autocracy and its growing pariah status in the world. The United States must continue to support the Nicaraguan people and democratic values.”

###

title: Ranking Members Shaheen, Durbin Lead Colleagues in Filing Amicus Brief Urging the Supreme Court to Uphold Ruling that Trump Administration Third-Country Deportation Policy is Unlawful
text:
**The amicus brief draws on Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats’ investigation earlier this year that called into question whether the Administration’s deportation agreements sufficiently protect deportees from torture and persecution**

WASHINGTON – This week, U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, led their colleagues in filing an amicus brief with the Supreme Court challenging the Trump Administration’s third-country deportation policy and urging the Court to affirm the judgment of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit.

The brief, filed in support of the plaintiffs in D.V.D. v. DHS, argues that the Administration’s third country policy violates longstanding protections established by Congress under the Immigration Nationality Act and the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998—specifically that the Administration is failing to carry out case-by-case determinations as to whether an individual may be persecuted or tortured in a third country. The brief notes that the Administration’s approach is a departure from State Department practice which included post-transfer monitoring. It draws from findings from a February 2026 report released by Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats which found that Administration has failed to meaningfully monitor whether foreign governments are complying with diplomatic assurances regarding the treatment of individuals deported to third countries.

“The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) guidance at issue in this case has transformed a narrow and rarely used practice into a standing system of unchecked global removals,” wrote the Senators. “The statutory and regulatory framework of the Immigration and Nationality Act ('INA') and Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998 ('FARRA') does not allow for blanket diplomatic assurances to serve as a green light for large-scale third-country deportations but instead contemplates an individualized, case-by-case analysis.”

“Congressional fact-finding has also revealed that the State Department is not meaningfully monitoring foreign government compliance with diplomatic assurances or enforcing agreement terms, even where evidence suggests foreign governments are violating their commitments,” continued the Senators. “Indeed, during an investigation by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee Minority staff, staff learned that the Administration had instructed U.S. officials not to engage with deportees once they were handed over to a foreign government.”

“The inescapable conclusion is that the DHS Guidance enables the Administration to use third countries to carry out removals that U.S. law would otherwise prohibit while turning a blind eye,” wrote the Senators.

You can read the full amicus brief HERE.

The brief was also signed by Senators Gary Peters (D-MI), Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Chris Coons (D-DE), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Alex Padilla (D-CA) and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

###

title: Grassley-Hassan Bill to Combat Counterfeit Imports Becomes Law
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – Bipartisan legislation authored by U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and U.S. Sen. Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.) to detect and intercept counterfeit imports has been signed into law after unanimously passing the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives. The new law authorizes U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to share the packing and shipping information of suspected counterfeit goods with key intellectual property (IP) rights holders, transportation carriers and e-commerce platforms.

U.S. Reps. Blake Moore (R-Utah) and Brad Schneider (D-Ill.) led the companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“As the holiday season gets underway, Americans want to be certain the gifts they’re purchasing for loved ones are safe and authentic. Counterfeit goods harm U.S. businesses, threaten our nation’s economy and can put consumers at serious risk. By increasing communication between government and private sector partners, this law will help prevent dangerous knockoffs from ever being distributed on American shores or finding their way under the Christmas tree,” Grassley said. “I’m proud President Trump has signed this important piece of bipartisan legislation into law.”

“Counterfeit products steal revenue from hardworking American small businesses, and because these products bypass important safety protections, they can also put Americans’ health and lives at risk,” Hassan said. “I am glad that our bipartisan bill to strengthen coordination between law enforcement and businesses is now law. This new law will help Customs and Border Protection better identify and stop counterfeit products before they reach our communities.”

"I am thrilled that the Counterfeit Notification Act has been signed into law! This bill safeguards American businesses and consumers from counterfeiters, IP thieves, and black-market traders by giving CBP additional authority to stop counterfeit and pirated imports,” Moore said. “I am grateful for the collaboration with my Ways and Means colleagues, Representatives Adrian Smith and Brad Schneider, and Senators Grassley and Hassan.”

“Counterfeit products are not victimless crimes. Inventors, designers, producers and consumers are all at risk. Disrupting counterfeit networks protects intellectual property and innovation and keeps communities across the country safe,” Schneider said. “I was proud to work with Congressman Blake Moore, Senator Chuck Grassley, and Senator Maggie Hassan to advance this bipartisan legislation through both chambers and am extremely glad to see it become law. We must continue to work together on common sense solutions that serve the American people, ensure economic growth, and maintain the United States’ leadership in global competitiveness and innovation.”

This law has backing from a number of stakeholder groups, including the Alliance for Automotive Innovation, the Alliance for Safe Online Pharmacies, the American Apparel & Footwear Association, the Automotive Anti-Counterfeiting Council, the Baby Safety Alliance, the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition, the International Trademark Association, the Partnership for Safe Medicines, the Pharmaceutical Security Institute and the Transnational Alliance to Combat Illicit Trade.

"We are deeply grateful to the bipartisan members of Congress and President Trump for signing this bill into law, ensuring that customs enforcement officials have the information-sharing tools they need to more effectively combat counterfeits, safeguard consumers, and support legitimate businesses. This decisive step forward in protecting Americans from counterfeit goods was made possible by the leadership and vision of Senators Chuck Grassley and Maggie Hassan, as well as Representatives Brad Schneider and Blake Moore. Thank you for your continued commitment to consumer protection ahead of the 2026 holiday season,” said Steve Lamar, President of the American Apparel & Footwear Association.

“Keeping dangerous counterfeits off of store shelves and out of consumers’ hands is only possible when everyone does their part. This legislation ensures that responsible stakeholders throughout the supply chain – whether rights-holders, shipping intermediaries, e-commerce platforms, or others – can provide timely and necessary support to help CBP keep American businesses and consumers safe from illicit imports,” said Bob Barchiesi, President of the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition.

“Counterfeit medicines pose a serious threat to patient safety, particularly as illegal online pharmacies and other digital platforms make it easier for dangerous products to reach unsuspecting consumers. This legislation strengthens the ability of U.S. Customs and Border Protection and private-sector partners to identify and intercept suspected counterfeit products before they enter the marketplace. We applaud Senator Grassley for his bipartisan leadership in advancing this important legislation and strengthening protections for American consumers,” stated the Alliance for Safe Online Pharmacies.

“Counterfeit medicines pose a serious threat to American patients, and it is critical to prevent these dangerous products from reaching our communities. The Customs Notification Act provides CBP with additional tools to work with the private sector to identify counterfeit imports, disrupt illicit supply chains, and stop hazardous products from reaching consumers. We applaud Representatives Blake Moore and Brad Schneider, along with Senators Chuck Grassley and Maggie Hassan, for their bipartisan leadership in advancing this important legislation,” said Shabbir Safdar, Executive Director of the Partnership for Safe Medicines.

Background:

Grassley is a co-chair of the Congressional Trademark Caucus. He has introduced this bipartisan legislation every Congress since 2021.

title: Appropsgiving Pie: Made in-House, Served by the Slice.
text:
Washington, D.C. – Few things are as American as pie. Here at the House Appropriations Committee, our Thanksgiving table includes a cornucopia of fiscal flavors – and we’re sharing our recipes for funding the nation’s priorities.

From hearings and oversight to markups and deliberation, House Appropriators put care into every ingredient. Our 12 subcommittees each bring something different to the mix: supporting servicemembers and veterans, strengthening public safety, investing in U.S. innovation, and much more.

Now it’s time to get to the crust of it. On the menu: a dozen slices – made in-House – each paired with a recipe card highlighting the essentials baked into its FY27 committee-reported bill. Together, they offer a taste of how appropriations serves the American people.

This Thanksgiving, we’re grateful for the work that went into bringing all 12 House bills to the table. With all 12 Senate bills now also public, every place is set for Congress to negotiate in earnest. A federal shutdown is something to be left off the holiday menu. Let’s keep the government open and get full-year funding bills done before we carve into the new year.

And because no Appropsgiving feast is complete without a look at the whole pie, we’ll also break down federal spending – including the difference between discretionary and mandatory dough, and where Appropriators fit into the pan.

So, without further ado, let’s dish out the details – there’s plenty to gobble up!

Agriculture: Cream of the Crop Pie

Flavor: Sweet Corn

INGREDIENTS

□ Research base of $1.795 billion for the Agricultural Research Service

□ Protective layer of frontline meat and poultry inspections through FSIS

□ Animal and plant health inspections to counter foreign pests and diseases

□ Rural development investments for broadband, housing, utilities, and local businesses

□ FDA inspections of foreign drug manufacturing facilities in China and India

□ Stronger tracking of foreign farmland purchases and USDA participation in CFIUS reviews

DIRECTIONS

1. Start with research that helps American farmers and ranchers compete.

2. Fold in food and drug inspections, rural lending, and Buy American requirements.

3. Add nutrition assistance for families in need and resources for child school food programs.

RECIPE NOTE: Trim burdensome regulations and leave climate hubs and climate corps out of the mix to ensure the dough goes toward agriculture’s core mission.

CJS: A Cherry Safe Community Pie

Flavor: Cherry

INGREDIENTS

□ Byrne JAG and COPS Hiring grants for state, local, and Tribal law enforcement

□ Increased DEA funding to combat fentanyl and other opioids

□ A $30 million measure for DOJ’s National Fraud Enforcement Division

□ A stellar helping of NASA’s Artemis program

□ Export controls and research security to counter Communist China

□ National Weather Service investments to improve forecasting and address radar gaps

DIRECTIONS

Combine law enforcement grants with tools to fight drug trafficking and fraud.

Fold in super intelligence, quantum research, and advanced manufacturing.

Keep sticky fingers out of the filling by guarding American research and technology against theft by Communist China.

Seal with protections for lawful gun ownership and a prohibition on censorship of lawful speech.

Finish with National Weather Service improvements to forecasting and radar coverage.

RECIPE NOTE: A cherry-picked mix of public safety, American innovation, and constitutional protections. Best served alongside safer neighborhoods and out-of-this-world discoveries.

Defense: Berry Strong Defense Pie

Flavor: Mixed berry

INGREDIENTS

□ A generous helping of higher military pay, including a 7% raise for E-5 and below and raises for all other ranks

□ A fresh batch of low-cost munitions, backed by $836 million and multiyear procurement authority

□ A powerful blend of hypersonic weapons and test infrastructure

□ A reinforced layer of submarine manufacturing and workforce training through $828 million for the industrial base

□ An extra measure of family support, with an additional $15 million for Military and Family Life Counseling

□ A required Modular Open Systems Approach to keep competition and readiness baked in

□ The Secretary's Special Seasoning: a dash each of Golden Dome, drones and autonomy, and acquisition reform, mixed in to taste

DIRECTIONS

Build the base with trained, equipped, and ready forces.

Fold in faster innovation, expanded production, and next-generation capabilities. Stir gently, and don't let the toppings exceed the 302(b).

Finish with stronger support for servicemembers and families, keeping resources focused on the mission.

RECIPE NOTE: Keep readiness on the front burner. Equip our forces to deter threats, defend freedom, and win when called upon.

Energy and Water: Pumpkin Up the Power Pie

Flavor: Pumpkin

INGREDIENTS

□ A strong layer of nuclear deterrence and naval propulsion through $27.072 billion for NNSA

□ A powerful helping of nuclear technology and domestic fuel development through $1.8 billion for nuclear energy

□ A fresh mix of discovery, science, artificial intelligence, and energy technology innovations through $8.525 billion for DOE Science

□ A generous serving of ports, waterways, and flood protection through $9.775 billion for the Army Corps

□ An extra measure of water conservation through $201 million for WIIN Act storage projects

□ A homegrown helping of critical mineral innovation to strengthen domestic supply chains

□ A firm seal against DOE funding flowing to foreign entities of concern like the Chinese Communist Party

DIRECTIONS

Combine nuclear stockpile modernization with naval reactor development.

Fold in advanced reactors, critical mineral extraction technologies, and grid cybersecurity.

Finish with ports, inland waterways, flood protection, and drought response.

RECIPE NOTE: Carve out the extras and only keep the gourd stuff by eliminating DOE’s Office of Energy Justice and Equity to keep this recipe focused on American power and innovation.

FSGG: Main Street Meringue Pie

Flavor: Lemon meringue

INGREDIENTS

□ Small Business Administration support for entrepreneurs and business development

□ Full funding for CFIUS scrutiny of foreign investments

□ Treasury tools to disrupt terrorist financing and protect the financial system

□ High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas funding to combat fentanyl

□ Cybersecurity and IT upgrades at Treasury, the Judiciary, and the Executive Office

□ A prohibition on developing a U.S. central bank digital currency

DIRECTIONS

Start with protections against IRS targeting of Americans for their beliefs.

Mix in support for entrepreneurs and a sound financial system.

Fold in limits on burdensome regulation.

Trim government overhead, strengthen oversight of pandemic spending, and add limits on unelected bureaucrats’ regulatory power.

RECIPE NOTE: Save the fluff for the meringue. Whip Washington into shape by cutting excess overhead, tightening financial safeguards, and clearing red tape so Main Street can rise.

Homeland: A S’more Secure Nation Pie

Flavor: S’mores

INGREDIENTS

□ Solid foundation of border security, with resources to sustain 22,000 Border Patrol agents

□ Concentrated effort against fentanyl through $25 million for Homeland Security Investigations initiatives

□ Protective helping of $30 million for child exploitation, forced labor, and human trafficking investigations

□ Generous serving of Coast Guard readiness, including $148 million for Waterways Commerce Cutters

□ Protective topping of critical infrastructure security and detection technology

□ Ready reserve of disaster response and first responder support, including $702 million for firefighter equipment, training, and staffing grants

DIRECTIONS

Build the base with resources to secure America’s air, land, and maritime borders.

Layer in tools to disrupt trafficking and protect essential infrastructure.

Finish with preparedness, response, and recovery resources for communities facing disasters.

RECIPE NOTE: Leave nothing to melt through the cracks. Layer border enforcement with infrastructure protection and keep disaster response resources ready to serve.

Interior: Pecan-servation Pie

Flavor: Pecan

INGREDIENTS

□ Rich base of public land stewardship and outdoor access, including $3.23 billion for the National Park Service

□ Protective layer of Park Protection, with a $134 million increase that includes U.S. Park Police in D.C.

□ Strong blend of wildfire response and federal land management, including unifying firefighting activities across the Department of the Interior into a new U.S. Wildland Fire Service.

□ Generous serving of domestic energy and mineral development

□ Full measure of Payments in Lieu of Taxes for public land counties

□ Strong helping of Tribal services, including $774.84 million for Tribal Public Safety and Justice programs

□ Refreshing mix of clean water investments, including $1.032 billion for community water and wastewater infrastructure projects

DIRECTIONS

Start with wildfire readiness, forest management, and access for hunting, fishing, and recreation.

Fold in onshore energy development, Alaska’s resource potential, and domestic critical mineral access.

Trim EPA funding by $1.8 billion, or 20%, and exclude American Climate Corps and eco-grief training funds.

RECIPE NOTE: Go nuts for America’s natural heritage. Blend responsible conservation with resource development, keep wildfire readiness baked in, and trim the regulatory crust so communities can thrive.

LHHS: An Apple a Day Pie

Flavor: Apple

INGREDIENTS

□ A generous helping of lifesaving research through $48.8 billion for NIH

□ A stronger layer of rural care through $575 million, including support for hospitals at risk of closure

□ A ready supply of biodefense and American-made medicines, with $65 million more for ASPR’s domestic production and supply chain efforts

□ A supportive blend of mental health care and recovery services

□ A fresh batch of skilled career pathways, including $290 million for apprenticeships

□ A strong measure of parental and local voices in education, with $60 million more for charter schools and $15.5 billion for special education

DIRECTIONS

Start with research and care that improve lives and strengthen communities.

Fold in health preparedness, domestic medicine production, and opportunities to build valuable skills.

Trim duplicative programs, strengthen fraud prevention, and keep families central to education decisions.

RECIPE NOTE: Get to the core of better care and greater opportunity. Peel away duplicative programs, keep families in the recipe, and give American innovation room to rise.

Leg Branch: For the Pie-ple, By the Pie-ple

Flavor: Peanut butter

INGREDIENTS

□ A constitutional foundation of Article I responsibilities

□ A generous helping of responsive constituent services

□ A strong layer of security across the Capitol complex for Members, staff, and visitors

□ A lasting supply of experienced staff and institutional knowledge

□ A practical blend of legislative research and support services

□ A firm topping of taxpayer safeguards and contractor accountability

□ Safety restrictions on purchasing technology and telecommunications equipment from Communist China and other adversaries

DIRECTIONS

1. Start with the people Congress serves and the constitutional duties it must fulfill.

2. Fold in resources for effective Member offices and a safe Capitol complex.

3. Trim inefficiencies, safeguard technology purchases, and return unspent office funds to debt and deficit reduction.

RECIPE NOTE: Give the pie-ple their due. Fill every slice with responsive service, responsible stewardship, and reliable research.

MilCon: A Sweet Salute to Service

Flavor: Sweet potato

INGREDIENTS

□ A full helping of veterans’ care and earned benefits, including $138.2 billion for medical care

□ A supportive layer of mental health, suicide prevention, homelessness prevention and modern VA facilities

□ A lasting commitment to toxic exposure-related needs through $54.6 billion for the FY27 Toxic Exposures Fund

□ A strong foundation of military construction and family housing through $19.2 billion

□ A comforting mix supporting the operational readiness and quality of life of our warfighters

□ An extra measure of accountability housing oversight

DIRECTIONS

Start with earned care and benefits, including support for toxic exposure-related needs.

Fold in mental health programs, suicide prevention, and more than $2 billion in capital improvements for VA medical facilities and four national cemeteries.

Build in the installations, housing, and family support that strengthen military readiness.

RECIPE NOTE: Build a crust as strong as the commitment to keeping veteran care fully funded and military families supported in every slice.

NSRP: Peach through Strength Pie

Flavor: Peach

INGREDIENTS

□ Firm foundation of America First diplomacy

□ Strong helping of support for Israel, Taiwan, and other key partners

□ Concentrated effort to counter Communist China

□ Protective layer of embassy security

□ Clear measure of foreign assistance oversight and burden sharing

□ Principled blend of religious freedom and American interests

DIRECTIONS

Start with diplomacy and partnerships that advance American security and prosperity.

Fold in tools to confront adversaries, counter fentanyl, and protect Americans serving abroad.

Trim wasteful contributions, prohibit funds for UNRWA and the Taliban, and require greater accountability for assistance.

RECIPE NOTE: Bakes a 6% leaner pie without skimping on strength. Reinforces U.S. security, allies, confronts adversaries, and keeps American interests at the pit center of its priorities.

THUD: Life in the Fast Lime

Flavor: Key lime

INGREDIENTS

□ Strong base of air traffic control modernization and $4 billion for FAA facilities and equipment, including telecom replacement

□ Fresh batch of 2,300 new air traffic controllers

□ Connected mix of highways, airports, rail, and ports, including $538 million for port infrastructure and $100 million for rail crossing elimination

□ Sturdy layer of maritime workforce and fleet investments

□ Supportive helping of housing assistance, including contract renewals serving about 120,000 elderly households and 33,000 households with disabilities

□ Extra measure of opportunity through $175 million for HUD Self-Sufficiency programs

□ Local serving of community development and infrastructure

DIRECTIONS

Start with safer skies and modern air traffic control.

Fold in highways, rail, ports, maritime academies, and strategic sealift programs.

Redirect $7.9 billion from lower-priority IIJA funding toward safety, freight movement, and more reliable travel while maintaining essential housing assistance.

RECIPE NOTE: Squeezes more purpose into every slice. Zests up transportation safety, keeps commerce moving, and gives communities a stronger foundation to call home.

Mandatory Spending: The Auto-Pie-lot

Flavor: Loaded chocolate cream

INGREDIENTS

□ Heaping portion of mandatory spending – roughly 60% of the federal budget

□ Prepared base of spending commitments established in law

□ Built-in eligibility rules and benefit formulas

□ Growing filling shaped by participation, demographics, and program costs

□ Projected annual growth of 4.5% over 2027–2036

DIRECTIONS

Measure before slicing. Mandatory spending accounts for about 60% of federal spending; discretionary spending accounts for about 25%.

Keep the recipes straight. Annual appropriations generally set discretionary funding, while mandatory spending follows existing law.

Check the rising filling. Changing its trajectory generally requires changing those laws – not simply reducing the smaller discretionary portion.

RECIPE NOTE: Keep an eye on the biggest filling – not just the slice making headlines. Mandatory spending takes roughly 60% of the pie and generally keeps cooking under existing law, while discretionary spending remains below its historical average as a share of the economy.

###

title: Boyle Statement on October 2026 PCE Inflation Data
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02), Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee, released the following statement after the Bureau of Economic Analysis reported an annual personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index of 3.8 percent for October 2026:

“Donald Trump has made life in America far too expensive. Today’s report shows once again that families are paying the price for his so-called ‘Big Beautiful Bill,’ his tariff taxes, and his disastrous war in Iran.

Next year, things could get even worse for millions of Americans as some of Trump’s most devastating health care and food assistance cuts take effect. As the next Chairman of the House Budget Committee, I’ll fight like hell to reverse these cruel cuts and make life more affordable.”

For more information on the Trump-Republican cost-of-living crisis in congressional districts across the United States, visit democrats-budget.house.gov/costofliving.

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Blasts Trump Administration's Latest Effort to Target Foreigners and Turn Banks into Immigration Enforcers
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, issued the following statement after the U.S. Treasury Department proposed to revise a longstanding rule by urging banks to collect immigration status and work-authorization information from certain business account owners.

“Trump and Secretary Bessent are once again trying to weaponize our banking system against vulnerable communities, and this time they are preying on immigrants. They weren’t satisfied with targeting immigrant families in their homes, workplaces, and communities, so now this Administration is seeking to abuse our banking system to further marginalize them. Banks are supposed to safeguard Americans' money, not serve as yet another weapon in Trump's cruel immigration enforcement operations.

“Despite claims from Trump that he wants to put an end to so-called ‘debanking,’ this frivolous targeting of immigrant communities is debanking at its worst. Banks already have extensive legal obligations to verify customers' identities and combat fraud and other financial crime. This proposal risks opening the door to discriminatory practices, wrongful account closures, unnecessary compliance costs, and the exclusion of hardworking immigrant business owners from essential financial services. Driving people out of the regulated banking system does nothing to strengthen its safety or integrity. Targeting foreigners who make a home in the United States does nothing to strengthen national security or public safety.

“This is yet another shameful example of the Administration using government power -- whether it is through banking regulations, ICE, the IRS, or more – to undo the progress and success of the civil rights movement. Trump is systematically taking away the hard-fought gains made for women, people of color, LGBTQ+ individuals, and, in this latest example, immigrants.

“Instead of demonizing immigrants, as Trump did in the ridiculous and racist executive order cited in the proposed rulemaking, Secretary Bessent should be focused on lowering costs, strengthening our financial system, and expanding access to banking. I demand thar Treasury to withdraw this proposal immediately.”

title: Ranking Member Maxine Waters Blasts Trump’s Latest Attempt to Cash In on His Failing Memecoin
text:
Today, Congresswoman Maxine Waters (D-CA), the top Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee, released this statement following president Trump’s latest gala hosted in a failed attempt to bolster his near-worthless memecoin.

“Trump’s flagrant crypto corruption persists at the expense of the people of this country, who just three weeks ago voted to root out corruption in DC. Trump’s gala dinner is a blatant effort to reward those funneling money to him and his family via the $TRUMP memecoin, granting exclusive access to the president in exchange for purchasing a worthless asset. Trump’s memecoin had a peak value of around $74 and now it is worth less than $1, meaning most investors lost big at the hands of Trump, while he raked in a windfall of $635 million in royalties on his memecoin last year alone.

“Donald Trump took an oath to faithfully execute the duties of the presidency, not use his office to line his pockets. While Americans struggle to afford housing, groceries, and other basic necessities, Trump continues to put his own financial interests first. That’s why I introduced the ‘Stop TRUMP in Crypto Act’ hours before Trump’s first corrupt memecoin dinner —to hold Trump accountable and ensure that all presidents focus on the job the American people elected them to carry out. Not only will we advance affordability solutions while we investigate Trump’s sham memecoin and other crypto ventures, but the first crypto bill our Committee must pass is to stop Trump’s crypto corruption.”

title: Meeks Calls on Admin to Immediately Halt DFC Role in Lukoil Deal
text:
Washington, DC — Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued a statement on the proposed purchase of Lukoil’s international assets by the United States International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and billionaire investors.

“Congress banned the DFC from investing in Russia less than a year ago, yet this Administration is circumventing that restriction by buying $10 billion in energy assets from Russia’s largest oil company, a corporation the U.S. sanctioned precisely to pressure Moscow to end its war in Ukraine. DFC exists to advance development in emerging markets, not serve as a finance vehicle for President Trump’s wealthy and well-connected friends.

“Time and again, this administration demonstrates it will stop at nothing to empower Russia and undercut Ukraine. The American people deserve to know why a U.S. government agency is taking an ownership stake in a Russian oil company’s portfolio while Russia continues its war, and Congress will continue to demand answers. I call on the Administration to put an immediate stop to this shameful deal.”

title: Meeks Issues Statement on the ICJ Genocide Ruling Against Myanmar
text:
Washington, DC – Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued a statement following the International Court of Justice ruling that the Burmese military committed genocide against Rohingya:

“Last week’s ICJ ruling in The Gambia v. Myanmar is the first time an international court has found a state responsible for genocide. It confirmed what the United States determined in 2022 – that the Burmese military committed genocide against Rohingya. That Secretary Rubio and the Trump administration are now engaging that very junta, without any clear direction on accountability, is not just morally reprehensible, it is also strategically inept and inconsistent with US law.

“Secretary Rubio has offered no strategy for how engagement would reduce the junta’s violence against civilians or end the scam operations that target Americans. At the same time, the administration has not implemented the sanctions the BURMA Act requires or the programs it authorizes to support Burma’s democratic forces. The administration’s policies are completely inconsistent with the BURMA Act, and I will be demanding answers from the Department on how it is complying with the law.”

title: Neal, Sánchez Slam Another Round of Dubious Trump Tariffs

committee.name: House Committee on Ways and Means

text:
WASHINGTON, DC— Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal (D-MA) and Trade Subcommittee Ranking Member Linda Sánchez (D-CA) released the following statement after the Trump Administration announced another round of price-hiking tariffs:

“Even after voters rejected his trade chaos, Trump is going to extraordinary lengths to attack his perceived enemies and reconstruct his struck-down IEEPA tariffs. He is dressing up new tariffs under a phony rationale, raising serious questions about the fairness of the Administration’s application of Section 301 authority and how his backroom deals may be impacting these rates. Trump is putting everything from family budgets to our national security at risk to keep his tariff scheme in place.

“The continuation of this chaos is all the more reason Congress must reassert itself on trade with fair, transparent policies that deliver for workers and businesses—small and large. When House Democrats get the gavel in January, we will lead the charge to put a stop to his recklessness.”

title: ICYMI: FEMA Administrator Hamilton Testifies on Agency Readiness, Disaster Response Capabilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, the Subcommittee on Emergency Management and Technology, led by Chairman Dale W. Strong (R-AL), convened a hearing entitled: “Beyond the Storm: Assessing FEMA’s Mission Readiness.” The hearing examined the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s (FEMA) operational readiness, organizational structure, and ability to effectively support state, local, tribal, and territorial governments before, during, and after disasters. Members emphasized the importance of congressional oversight in strengthening FEMA’s mission readiness, improving operational efficiency, and ensuring communities have the resources necessary to recover from devastating disasters. Witness testimony was provided by FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton.

In his opening statement, Administrator Hamilton outlined the Trump administration’s vision for returning FEMA to its core mission, reducing federal bureaucracy, and strengthening state and local disaster preparedness and resilience:

“Under the president’s leadership, FEMA is breaking the cycle of federal dependency, taking active steps to restore accountability, supporting states only when disasters truly exceed their capacity, radically simplifying recovery processes, safeguarding American taxpayer dollars through common sense reform, and returning power back to the American people through our resilience investments.”

Subcommittee Chairman Strong asked about how FEMA coordinated with states to prepare for recent hurricanes and what role the agency played in disaster response and recovery efforts:

“Just last month, a major hurricane struck the Southeast, prompting President Trump to approve emergency declarations for Alabama, Florida, and Georgia, as well as major disaster declarations for Florida. In Alabama alone, more than 300,000 residents experienced power outage. Administrator Hamilton, how did FEMA work with states to prepare ahead of storms, and what role has the agency played in supporting response and recovery efforts in the aftermath?”

Administrator Hamilton testified:

“Our preparedness activities lead on the front edge. It’s one of the spearheads of our resilience capability… There’s a robust leadership team there that engages with the state, every single state director, with state governors, you name it, to ensure that coordination efforts can be rolled out effectively. What we then did is we stage resources, we allocate different personnel, mission requirements––we dialogue with the state to ensure that we better understand where they think they may have limitations [and] how can we fill those gaps. And then we await the decision of the president, ultimately, on what level of federal support will be authorized.”

Chairman Strong continued, asking what lessons FEMA learned from the 2026 FIFA World Cup and how those lessons will help strengthen security preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics:

“Administrator Hamilton, what lessons has FEMA learned from administering World Cup security grants, and how will those lessons inform preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics?”

Administrator Hamilton testified:

“The counter-UAS space was a very unique phenomenon that allowed us to really target investments to state and locals to build their capability, not just buying stuff, but actually properly training their personnel and engaging in procedures to be more effective… We learned quite a bit about how the different levels of government would work together and coordinate. In addition to that, we’re looking at ways to strengthen with accountability as far as having data systems that communicate with one another; if we build a capability in one locality, can we leverage that with mutual aid to another––so there are many different compilations we are going through.”

Rep. Dave Joyce (R-OH) asked about the capacity of the Port Security Grant Program, administered by FEMA, to help states and localities protect our maritime infrastructure, to which Administrator Hamilton testified:

“The incident that we saw down in Louisiana, much of the infrastructure that was required for that response was actually paid for through federal dollars… Our goal and focus with these port security grants is to build capability, to be autonomous, so that the state can utilize it at a moment’s notice.”

Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) asked about whether federal disaster assistance evaluations should account for rural counties:

“Would you agree there is a fundamental difference between evaluating the financial impact of a disaster in a county with substantial property tax base and evaluating the same impact in a rural county where much of the land is federally owned and cannot be taxed?”

Administrator Hamilton testified:

“We try to do our best to analyze those particular nuances of every locality to better understand the devastation that they’re facing and what assistance might be eligible to help them recover.”

title: Mace and Burlison Announce Hearing on Detecting and Responding to AI-Enabled Cyber Incidents

text:

Members will also explore the current legal framework to protect against harm caused by AI and whether and how it could be modified to address new technological developments.

“As the public has recently seen, cybersecurity threats are increasing in their severity and frequency everyday now it seems, running the risk of everyday Americans, government offices, and corporations having sensitive information leaked in ways never before seen. Mace and Burlison.

title: Warren, Van Hollen, and Colleagues Call on SEC to Rescind Efforts to Create Special Treatment for Crypto Assets and Tokenized Securities

committee.name: Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

text:
Warren letter urges SEC Chair Atkins to rescind proposed “Regulation Crypto Assets” rule that would weaken investor protections and create new loopholes in securities laws.

Van Hollen letter urges SEC Chair Atkins to withdraw a September order granting exemptions from securities laws to Tokenized Securities Venues and certain liquidity providers.

Text of Letter on “Regulation Crypto Assets” Proposal (PDF) | Text of Letter on Tokenized Securities Order (PDF)

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) led two letters to Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Chair Paul Atkins urging the agency to withdraw a proposed rule and an order that would weaken investor protections and create new regulatory loopholes for crypto assets and tokenized securities.

In the first letter, led by Senator Warren and joined by Senators Van Hollen and Tina Smith (D-Minn.), the lawmakers call on the SEC to rescind its proposed “Regulation Crypto Assets” rule, warning that it would allow crypto companies to evade longstanding securities laws, weaken state oversight, and expose investors to fraud and scams.

“The proposal would create a new ‘tailored securities offering regime’ for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets,” wrote the senators. “However, the proposal only serves to help crypto assets escape from the SEC’s regulatory regime and gives them special treatment—with less oversight—compared to other traditional securities.”

The senators outlined four core problems with the proposal in the letter:

It invites opportunities for crypto fraud and investor harm with massive exemptions that permit crypto asset offerings with no SEC review, no financial statements in some cases, and scarce disclosure.

It prevents states from enforcing their own laws with respect to the registration of crypto assets that use the proposal’s loopholes.

It exceeds the SEC’s statutory authority and front-runs legislative efforts to develop a regulatory framework for crypto assets.

It undermines decades-old Supreme Court precedent that provides the basis for determining SEC jurisdiction.

The senators concluded by asking the SEC to rescind this proposal.

In the second letter, led by Senator Van Hollen and joined by Senators Warren, Smith, and Jack Reed (D-R.I.), the lawmakers urged the SEC to withdraw its September 2026 order granting sweeping exemptions from federal securities laws to Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) and certain liquidity providers.

The senators warned that the order would allow platforms trading tokenized stocks to operate outside longstanding market safeguards, including requirements designed to ensure fair pricing, market transparency, and protections against manipulation. They also raised concerns that the exemptions could facilitate illicit financial activity and create new risks for investors and publicly traded companies.

“The order would allow TSV platforms to operate a shadow stock market outside longstanding regulatory protections designed to ensure fair and transparent markets, impose new burdens on publicly traded companies seeking to protect their shareholders, and create unnecessary risks of illicit financial activity,” the senators wrote. “While technological innovation can strengthen our capital markets, it should not come at the expense of investor protection, market integrity, or national security.”

The lawmakers also criticized the SEC for issuing the order without a public notice-and-comment process, warning that the agency's actions exceeded its statutory authority.

Together, the letters raise concerns about the SEC's efforts to carve out special treatment for crypto assets and tokenized securities at the expense of investor protections and market integrity.

title: Wyden Statement on Trump’s Latest Tariffs
text:
Washington, D.C. — Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., today issued the following statement after the Trump Administration announced it intends to impose new tariffs on products from 40 countries around the world, under the guise of combating structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing sectors.

“Donald Trump lacks object permanence. Only weeks after Americans overwhelmingly voted against his high tariffs and higher prices agenda, he’s back with another round. This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs, no matter the cost to American families, workers, and small businesses. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution,” Wyden said. “As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, I will use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariff chaos and restore Congress’s constitutional authority over trade.”

Trump will impose these tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 (Section 301), in conjunction with previously imposed Section 301 tariffs purportedly to address forced labor. These tariffs are the latest in a string of price-hiking tariffs imposed to replace Trump’s original global tariff regime, which the Supreme Court struck down earlier this year.

As incoming Finance Committee Chairman, Wyden has pledged to end Trump’s tariffs, which are a tax paid by Americans, and to restore Congress’s constitutional authority over trade. Previously, he led the charge in the Senate to force a successful vote to overturn the global tariffs, led a bicameral, bipartisan amicus brief urging the Supreme Court to strike down the Administration’s unlawful global emergency tariffs, and authored the Congressional Trade Powers Reform Act.

title: Q3 GDP Strongest Growth Since Q3 2023, October Inflation Up, Disposable Income Increased
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Joint Economic Committee released its Monthly Expenditures Update for October. From September to October, headline personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index inflation was 0.32 percent. Core PCE price index inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose to 0.29 percent.

In the same period, spending decreased slightly while savings increased. Real PCE increased by 0.03 percent, or $5.82 billion. Real PCE on all services increased by 0.05 percent, or $6.13 billion. Real PCE on all goods decreased by 0.23 percent, or $13.38 billion. The nominal personal savings rate increased by 0.5 percentage points to 4.1 percent.

From October 2025 to October 2026, headline PCE price index inflation was 3.84 percent, higher than the Federal Reserve’s target of 2 percent. Core PCE price index inflation was 3.26 percent, the highest 12-month core PCE reading in three years.

Month-over-month, headline personal income increased by 0.73 percent, or $201.82 billion, while real disposable personal income per capita increased by 0.48 percent, which means that after tax income rose more quickly than prices.

For the full Monthly Expenditures Update, visit: https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/expenditures-update

Additionally, the Joint Economic Committee released its Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Update of Q3 2026, Second Estimate. Real GDP growth from 2026 Q2 to 2026 Q3 increased by 4.28 percent, up from the 2.22 percent in the second quarter, and the strongest growth since the third quarter of 2023. Current-dollar GDP increased by 6.2 percent or $493.173 billion, to a level of $33.056 trillion, the current size of the U.S. economy.

For the full GDP Update, visit: https://www.jec.senate.gov/public/index.cfm/republicans/gdp-update

title: Grassley, Cornyn, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Increase Government Transparency
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa), John Cornyn (R-Texas), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) and Peter Welch (D-Vt.) introduced the bipartisan FOIA Clarification Act to increase government transparency, expand public access to federal records and protect federal employees from retaliation for submitting FOIA or Privacy Act requests. Grassley and Durbin are the Chairman and Ranking Member, respectively, of the Senate Judiciary Committee. Cornyn and Welch both serve as committee members.

“Government is a service to the people, and Americans deserve to know what the government is doing on their behalf. I’m proud to join my colleagues in introducing this commonsense, bipartisan bill to improve the FOIA process and ensure government transparency,” Grassley said.

“Open government is a key tenet of the American tradition of democracy and our constitutional republic,” Cornyn said. “By expanding the American people’s access to public records and holding agencies accountable to the taxpayer, this legislation would better ensure we remain a government of the people, by the people, and for the people.”

“The American people have a right to know how federal agencies operate and make decisions. This bipartisan legislation strengthens FOIA by making more government records accessible to the public and ensuring that federal agencies cannot unnecessarily withhold information,” Durbin said. “Above all, it reinforces the principle that government information belongs to the American people, and only by understanding what our government is up to can we hold it accountable.”

“FOIA has played a major role in keeping the free press and the American people aware and informed for sixty years. But there’s more we can do to honor our commitment to civic transparency, a cornerstone of good governance,” Welch said. “Our bipartisan bill implements much-needed, commonsense reforms to FOIA to ensure the American people can hold our government accountable.”

Background:

The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) was signed into law in 1966 to the provide the American people an avenue to request the release of government records. Grassley chaired a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing last year to explore FOIA improvements.

The FOIA Clarification Act would enhance individuals’ ability to challenge government agencies that fail to comply with FOIA and modify the foreseeable-harm standard to require agencies to weigh the potential harm that could result from disclosure against the public interest. Additionally, it would require agencies to proactively publish more information online in machine-readable formats, including organizational charts, lobbying records, searchable FOIA request logs, agency leadership calendars, major contracts and grants, visitor logs and unclassified Inspector General reports. Overall, the bill aims to improve government accountability, promote public access to information and protect individuals exercising their information-access rights.

title: Senate Judiciary Committee Receives Partial Materials for Two Judicial Nominees
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – This evening, the U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee received partial materials for two potential new judicial nominees: Steve Fahey, to fill a vacancy in the Northern District of Texas that has been open since October 2025, and Jim O’Neill, to fill a vacancy in the Middle District of North Carolina that has been open since July 2026.

Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) has a long record of delivering successful nominees, having advanced more than half of the nearly 300 constitutionalist judges President Trump has nominated throughout his two terms. Grassley will continue his track record of ensuring President Trump’s judicial nominations succeed by speaking to his colleagues and determining if there is any agreement on whether a path to confirmation exists for these additional nominations before the end of the year.

Historic Nominations Progress:

Under Chairman Grassley’s leadership this Congress, the Senate has advanced and confirmed judges at the fastest pace since the Reagan administration and has confirmed 61 Article III judges thus far. Since November 3, 2026, the Senate has confirmed five judges, with another five judicial nominees currently pending on the floor awaiting confirmation votes. The committee will vote to advance thirteen additional judicial nominees in early December.

As of today, the average time between a judge’s nomination to their Senate confirmation during the second Trump administration is 85 days – a significantly faster timeline than any of the six prior presidential administrations.

title: Shaheen, Meeks Demand Answers on Administration’s Selective Release of USAID "Files"
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, and Representative Gregory W. Meeks (D-NY), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Acting USAID Administrator Bill Woolf after USAID released a set of cherry-picked documents to justify DOGE’s illegal dismantling of the agency and misrepresent USAID’s life-saving work around the world.

Full text of the letter is available HERE and provided below.

Dear Secretary Rubio and Acting Administrator Woolf:

We are writing to express our concern about the apparent misuse of the USAID.gov website. Last night, links to documents were posted that include Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and potentially other sensitive data in likely contravention of federal law and regulations. We urge you to immediately remove this information from the USAID.gov website and ensure any information that appears is in full compliance with applicable law and regulations.

The posting of files appears to be an effort to tarnish USAID’s decades of work promoting freedom and democracy abroad and cover up the appalling impact of the agency’s closure, which caused millions of preventable deaths and cost American taxpayers billions of dollars. By the agency’s own calculation, these costs may exceed $19 billion, not including interest payments and legal expenses.

“Moreover, the selective publishing of certain files and excerpts serves no purpose other than to sow disinformation. This is not a suitable or acceptable use of federal resources or a U.S. government website.

The release of files in this manner begs the question of what review was done of these files to ensure compliance with the Privacy Act (5 U.S.C. § 552a) and other applicable federal statutes regarding public disclosure. The site also fails to meet basic statutory and regulatory requirements, for example regarding the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and Inspector General records and providing links to these resources. An agency website cannot purport to exist and serve the public but omit the most basic requirements.

We urge you to engage in responsible stewardship of U.S. government resources, immediately remove any files containing PII and sensitive information from the USAID.gov website and bring it into compliance with federal laws and regulations.
